author: ycpiglet
body:
## Summary

- **Guard 1** (`scripts/regen_host_lock_if_needed.py`): Detects when `tests/fixtures/host/agent_runtime.lock.json` is stale relative to the current template tree. `--check` exits 1 with a clear `--write` hint; `--write` regenerates in place. Uses a tmp-dir copy for a non-destructive dry-run so the committed lock is never touched by `--check`. Prevents the cryptic `test_regenerate_noop_when_current` red when a developer edits a template without regenerating the host lock.
- **Guard 2** (`scripts/safe_ref_op.py`): Wraps `git branch -D` with a SHA verification step. `delete-branch <name> --expect-sha <sha>` re-reads the LIVE tip and **refuses** (exit 1) if the branch has advanced since the SHA was captured. `verify-tip <ref> --expect-sha` is a read-only pre-flight. `--force` bypasses the check. Background: COMPOUND-2026-06-22 — a `git branch -D` on a stale cached tip deleted a concurrent agent's unmerged commits.

Both scripts: ASCII output, not wired into `owner_governance_gate`, no template mirrors.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: failing tests written first (9 tests across both files), then implementations written to make them pass
- [x] `test_regen_host_lock_if_needed.py`: stale lock -> `--check` exits 1; after `--write` -> `--check` exits 0; regenerated bytes match canonical fixture
- [x] `test_safe_ref_op.py`: delete with correct SHA succeeds; delete with stale SHA is refused (branch intact); `--force` overrides; `verify-tip` exits 0/1 correctly
- [x] `test_lock_merge_driver.py` still all green (no regressions)
- [x] `python scripts/owner_governance_gate.py` exits 0

author: cldgayo
body:
## Phase 67 — Live Chat Inbox & Human Handoff

Real-time messaging portal where tenants intercept Messenger conversations and take over from the bot. Builds on the Phase 58 flows / Phase 66 broadcasts `flow_contacts` model.

> **Stacking note:** branched off `feat/phase-66-broadcasting` (PR #12, still open) because Phase 67 extends `flow_contacts`. Until #12 merges, this PR's diff also shows the Phase 66 commit. Review the Phase 67 commit (`5cda4a1`) for this feature's changes, or merge #12 first.

### What it does
- **Watch** live Messenger threads (contacts + transcript) in a master-detail inbox.
- **Take over**: a human reply dispatches via the Graph API and **pauses the bot for 24h** — both the durable `flow_contacts.bot_paused_until` stamp and the Redis HITL key — so neither the NEXUS Flow engine nor the LangGraph orchestrator replies while the operator is on the thread. Auto-resumes after 24h.

### Backend
- **Migration 0020** — `flow_contacts.bot_paused_until` (nullable TIMESTAMPTZ) + new `app.contact_messages` transcript table (composite per-thread index `ix_contact_messages_thread`).
- **models** — `ContactMessage` + `FlowContact.bot_paused_until`.
- **flow_engine** — `_pause_active` pure predicate · `is_contact_bot_paused` gate · `set_contact_bot_paused` stamper · `log_contact_message` transcript writer. Successful flow sends now log an `outbound` row (single tap via `_send_graph_message(run=…)`); the `pause` node also stamps the durable DB pause; `resume_flow_for_dm` short-circuits when paused.
- **webhook** — the HITL gatekeeper now also honours the DB pause (the `continue` halts BOTH the flow engine and the orchestrator); inbound messages logged to the transcript.
- **inbox router** (`require_manager`, tenant-scoped, header/path reconciled like broadcasts):
  - `GET  /api/tenants/{id}/facebook/inbox/contacts`
  - `GET  /api/tenants/{id}/facebook/inbox/contacts/{contact_id}/messages`
  - `POST /api/tenants/{id}/facebook/inbox/contacts/{contact_id}/send`

### Frontend
- `useInbox` hook — polled (5s) contact list + open thread, manual send.
- `InboxPage` — master-detail: contact list (paused/hot-lead badges, last-message preview), chat bubbles (user vs tenant), composer with handoff note.
- `/inbox` route + sidebar nav (manager-class) + i18n (`en/inbox.json`, `nav.inbox` across all 7 locales via `scripts/_phase67_i18n.py`).

### Test plan
- [x] `pytest messenger/tests/test_inbox.py` — 13 new (pause predicate; **paused-contact-blocks-engine**; inbox 404/400; router lockdown; send-dispatches-and-pauses-24h; graph-failure→502).
- [x] Full messenger suite green — **291 passed, 2 skipped**.
- [x] `ruff check` clean; new files `ruff format` clean.
- [x] `alembic heads` — single head `0020` chained off `0019`.
- [x] `npm run lint` — Phase 67 files clean (no new issues); `npm run build` — success.
- [ ] **Deploy (human, post-merge):** run `alembic upgrade head` on VPS to apply migration 0020 (`docker exec -w /app/rag nexus-api alembic upgrade head`). ⚠️ migration-number collision risk vs open PRs #10/#11 — reconcile down_revision chain at merge time.
- [ ] Manual smoke: send a manual reply from `/inbox`, confirm the user receives it, the bot stays silent for 24h, and the transcript renders both sides.

body:
## What

Gives users an in-app way to control whether the updater offers GitHub pre-releases (RC/beta), and makes the default **opt-out**.

- `UpdateManager.set_include_prereleases()` added (mirrors the existing `set_auto_check` setter).
- Default flipped `True` → `False` in `include_prereleases`.
- New checkable **Help → "Include Pre-release (Beta) Updates"** menu item, initialised from and bound to the setting.

## Why

`include_prereleases` was read-only and defaulted to `True` with no UI, so **every user was offered beta builds by default** and couldn't opt out without hand-editing the persisted QSetting. That contradicted:
- the checker's own default — `check_for_update(..., include_prereleases=False)` (`autoptz/update/checker.py`), and
- the release workflow's documented intent — pre-releases are "surfaced to users who **opted into** pre-releases" (`.github/workflows/release.yml`).

So this aligns the manager with the rest of the system rather than changing the intended behavior.

## Test

- `test_update_manager_prerelease_opt_in` — asserts the default is `False` and the setter round-trips/persists.
- Full suite green locally: `pytest tests/test_update.py tests/test_ui.py` → 104 passed (incl. the MainWindow smoke test that builds the new menu).

author: tim1016
body:
Follow-up to the 619-C series ([#631](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/631) / [#632](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/632) / [#633](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/633) / [#634](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/634) / [#635](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/635), all merged to master earlier today). Codex left three inline findings on the deleted feature branches — one **P1** and two **P2**, all real bugs in the as-shipped stack.

## P1 — Surface `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` through the operator error parser

PRD #619-C5 returns a structured 409 body in FastAPI's `HTTPException.detail` (`MutationOutcomeUnknownResponse`). The cockpit's `toOperationError` only read `error.detail` when it was a *string*; on a structured object it fell back to `HttpErrorResponse.message` and the canned (operation, 409) remediation. **Operators never saw `runbook_hint`** — the whole C5 change was invisible to the UI.

Fixed by:
- New `outcome-unknown` `ErrorCategory` distinct from `precondition`.
- New `OutcomeUnknownBody` interface mirrors the backend `MutationOutcomeUnknownResponse`.
- `toOperationError` recognises the structured body and overrides the canned remediation with the server-authored `runbook_hint`.
- 3 new Vitest cases pin the contract.

## P2 — Probe an auth-sensitive endpoint

The connectivity monitor probed `/health`, which `host_daemon` left unauthenticated for the data-plane probe. A missing / stale / rotated daemon token therefore never produced `AUTH_FAILED` — the monitor reported `CONNECTED` while every protected daemon call failed closed.

Fixed by gating `/health` with `dependencies=auth`. The data plane already forwards the token via the artifacts bind mount, so production stays green; tests + supervisor healthchecks now have to send the token.

- `test_health_requires_token` flipped from "must stay open" to "must require token".
- New `test_probe_daemon_health.py` (5 tests) pins the probe's full classification matrix via respx — 401/403 → `AUTH_FAILED`, 5xx → `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, ConnectError → `UNREACHABLE` (unambiguous), 2xx → `CONNECTED` with `daemon_boot_id` forwarded.
- `test_daemon_app_integration.py`'s 5 `/health` callsites updated to attach the token via the fixture-shared header.

## P2 — Wire `localTransportStale` into mutation dispatch

C4 defined `localTransportStale` and promised in its docstring to "short-circuit click handlers locally" — but nothing consumed the signal. Buttons stayed enabled and `dispatch*` methods fired regardless of transport state.

Fixed at both layers:
- **Template**: each action button (Resume/Pause/Stop/Flatten) adds `|| localTransportStale()` to its `[disabled]` predicate and shows `title=\"TRANSPORT_STALE\"`.
- **Component**: new `_refuseOnStaleTransport(label)` helper called by every `dispatch*` method. Returns early + populates `mutationError` with an operator-facing message. Defense in case the disabled button is bypassed programmatically.

2 new Vitest cases pin both layers.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend affected suite: **392 passed / 10 skipped** (host_daemon + control_plane + probe + live_instances + integration + services).
- [x] Backend full project: **5,169 passed / 60 skipped / 31 pre-existing failures**.
- [x] Frontend full suite: **120 files / 1,207 tests, all pass** (was 1,202; +5 new tests here).
- [x] `ruff check` clean on every edited backend file.
- [x] `eslint` clean on every edited frontend file.
- [ ] CI green

## Pre-existing failures surfaced

Same as the upstream PRs — `tests/lean_sidecar/*` (24+), plus the three collection-error tests. None introduced here.

author: luk8nhassil-maker
body:
## Causa raiz

Em sessões com `tentativasInvalidas: 2` acumuladas (ex.: cliente que mandou mensagens inválidas antes), uma saudação simples como `"boa noite"` não era reconhecida como categoria válida e caía em `respostaInvalida`. Isso incrementava o contador para 3, atingindo `LIMITE_TENTATIVAS` e disparando `respostaEscaladaPorLoop()` com `escalar: true`.

Com `escalar: true`, o guard na rota (`!result.escalar && pareceFallbackSeco(...)`) bloqueava `resolverFallbackInteligente` antes mesmo de rodar — ou seja, `ehMensagemSocial` e `fallbackDeterministicoMelhorado` nunca tinham chance de agir. O cliente recebia a mensagem de escalação por ter mandado "boa noite".

## Patch aplicado

Adicionada função `ehSaudacaoSimples(n: string)` local em `bot.ts` — sem nenhum import de `fallbackInteligente.ts` (zero risco de dependência circular).

Guard inserido nos 3 pontos de `respostaInvalida` com o mesmo risco:

| Step | Localização |
|------|-------------|
| `category` | antes de `respostaInvalida(mensagemCategorias(), session)` |
| `add_more` | antes de `respostaInvalida(…quer adicionar…, session)` |
| `name` | antes de `respostaInvalida(…não entendi muito bem…, session)` |

Quando a saudação é detectada, retorna:
```ts
return { messages: [msgInvalida()], session: resetaTentativas({ ...session, step: currentStep }) };
```

O `msgInvalida()` é seco e capturado por `pareceFallbackSeco` → `resolverFallbackInteligente` → `ehMensagemSocial` → `fallbackDeterministicoMelhorado` → saudação natural e humanizada. O contador de tentativas é zerado.

author: ryjm
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the control plane that agents use to mutate and then immediately read issue state during short heartbeat windows.
> - The issue/comment subsystem has to make those writes look consistent right away, because agent follow-up reads drive wake batching, blocked-task dedup, and review routing.
> - `PATCH /api/issues/:id` could update the issue first and add the optional comment afterward, which left a stale read-after-write window for both issue snapshots and comment lists.
> - The incremental `GET /api/issues/:id/comments?after=...` cursor path also relied on raw SQL comparisons that broke in DB-backed reads once typed values were bound through the driver.
> - This pull request moves PATCH-with-comment work into one transaction, keeps `updatedAt` aligned to the created comment timestamp, and makes cursor reads use typed Drizzle comparisons.
> - The benefit is that the first immediate read after a PATCH sees the committed comment/thread state instead of forcing a second verification fetch.

## What Changed

- Wrapped issue PATCH mutations plus optional comment creation in one transaction, including execution-decision writes when present.
- Refreshed the PATCH response issue snapshot from the created comment timestamp and delayed `issue.updated` activity logging until after the comment exists.
- Extended `issueService.addComment` to accept a caller transaction and use one shared timestamp for both the inserted comment row and the parent issue `updatedAt`.
- Reworked incremental `listComments(..., { afterCommentId })` cursor comparisons to use typed Drizzle `gt/lt/eq/or` conditions instead of raw SQL interpolation.
- Added regression coverage for transaction threading, response freshness, activity ordering, and DB-backed immediate comment visibility after PATCH.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run server/src/__tests__/issue-comment-visibility-e2e.test.ts server/src/__tests__/issue-update-comment-wakeup-routes.test.ts server/src/__tests__/issue-comment-reopen-routes.test.ts server/src/__tests__/issues-service.test.ts`
- `pnpm -r typecheck`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm test:run` still fails outside this PR in:
  - `server/src/__tests__/company-portability.test.ts`
  - `src/__tests__/network-bind.test.ts`
  - `src/__tests__/onboard.test.ts`

## Risks

- Low to medium risk in the issue mutation hot path: PATCH-with-comment now holds the issue update, decision write, and comment insert in one transaction.
- Incremental comment paging now depends on `createdAt` plus `id` typed comparisons; if future cursor semantics change, this code path will need to stay aligned with that ordering contract.

## Model Used

- OpenAI Codex, GPT-5-based coding agent in the Codex CLI environment, with tool use, terminal execution, and patch application. Exact internal deployment ID/context window were not exposed in-session.

author: jakechampion
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #3801 (auto-cancel superseded runs). That PR stopped runs *stacking*; this one cuts the absolute **number of jobs** the queue has to absorb in the first place — directly addressing "pushes to main should run the minimal amount of workflows" and "maybe remove the sharding".

## What

**1. Build & release stops running on every merge to main.**
On a push to main, only `Build & release` (full 3-platform build + `nightly` publish) and path-filtered `Pages` ever ran — the test matrix is `pull_request`-only. But `nightly` is a *rolling daily* build, yet the autonomous merge loop fired a full build+publish on **every** merge. Switched to:
- `schedule:` daily at 06:00 UTC (rolling `nightly` tracks main's HEAD at that time)
- `workflow_dispatch` (builds artifacts without publishing — gate moved from `event_name == 'push'` → `== 'schedule'`)

A routine merge to main now triggers **no heavy workflows** (only Pages, if docs/site paths changed).

**2. Halve the two most job-heavy workflows.** Now that per-ref `concurrency` (from #3801) caps stacking and the binding constraint is *queue capacity* not wall-clock:
| workflow | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| test-e2e-selfhost | 14 shards × 2 = **28 jobs** | 6 × 2 = **12 jobs** |
| test-e2e-differential | 4 shards × 2 = **8 jobs** | 2 × 2 = **4 jobs** |

**36 → 16 jobs/PR** from these two alone. The selfhost x86 long pole (~23 min real work) at 6 shards is ~6 min nominal/shard — well inside the existing 20-min job budget / 18-min `go test` timeout. Tuning comments updated to the new counts + rationale.

## Why reduce, not remove
A single unsharded selfhost job reintroduces a ~23-min long pole that would throttle the merge loop. Reducing keeps per-job wall-clock tolerable while cutting job count by >half.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new 0.75× scale option for card field zone overlays and refines the sizing and spacing of overlay badges and icons to improve visual hierarchy and readability.

## Key Changes

- **New scale option:** Added `0.75` to the allowed scale values for desktop and mobile overlay scales in card field zones, enabling smaller overlay badges when needed
  - Updated schema validation in `cardFieldZonesSchema.ts`
  - Updated type documentation in `CardImageOverlays.tsx` and `types/index.ts`
  - Added UI option in `CardFieldZoneBoard.tsx`

- **Overlay badge sizing improvements:**
  - Increased badge padding from default to `px-2.5 py-1.5` and text size to `text-sm` for better visual weight
  - Added explicit gap spacing (`gap-1.5`) and icon sizing (`[&>svg]:size-4`) to the badge component
  - Increased all overlay icons from `size-3` to `size-4` for consistency and improved visibility

- **Rating overlay refinement:**
  - Increased padding from `px-1.5 py-0.5` to `px-2 py-1`
  - Increased star rating size from `12` to `16` for better readability

- **Image overlay sizing:**
  - Increased image overlay size from `size-4` to `size-5`

- **Table zone layout simplification:**
  - Removed flex layout mode from the Table zone — it now always renders as a fixed two-column `label : value` grid
  - Simplified Table zone styling by removing layout rule application
  - Updated `CardZoneLayoutControls.tsx` to exclude the Table zone from layout configuration

- **Block zone layout refinement:**
  - Updated `flexFlowClass()` to accept a `fallbackDirection` parameter, allowing different default directions per zone (row for table zones, column for single-column zones)
  - Applied this to the Block zone's flex layout to respect custom direction settings while maintaining backward compatibility
  - Updated header gap styling in Block zone to use the zone's configured gap instead of a hard-coded value

## Implementation Details

The overlay sizing changes maintain visual consistency across all overlay types (badges, icons, ratings, images) while the new 0.75× scale provides finer control for space-constrained layouts. The Table zone simplification removes unnecessary complexity since that zone has a fixed structure. The `flexFlowClass()` refactor enables more flexible layout defaults per zone while preserving existing behavior through sensible fallbacks.

author: jotheeswaran-dev
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in `@claude_scope` option so the picker can track Claude Code running as **panes inside your own project sessions**, not only the dedicated `claude-*` sessions created by the launcher.

| `@claude_scope` | The picker lists… |
| --- | --- |
| `session` (default) | dedicated `claude-*` sessions created by `prefix`+`y` — **unchanged** |
| `pane` | every pane whose foreground command matches `@claude_command`, across all sessions |
| `auto` | `session` if any `claude-*` session exists, otherwise `pane` |

## Why

Today the picker only knows about sessions the launcher spawned (`list-sessions | grep '^claude-'`). Many people run Claude as a pane next to their editor/shell inside a project session — often several Claudes per session. For that workflow the picker shows `0/0`. This generalises the plugin to "find Claude wherever it runs" without changing the default behavior.

## Design / backward compatibility

- Default stays `session` → existing behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `state.sh` now stamps state on the **pane** (`set-option -p`) in addition to the session. The per-pane copy lets multiple Claude panes in one session report status independently; the per-session copy keeps `session` scope working exactly as before. Hook wiring (the `state.sh working|waiting|idle` calls) is unchanged.
- In `pane` scope, `enter` switches the client to the pane's window and focuses it (no popup overlay); `ctrl-x` kills just that pane.
- Pane detection matches `@claude_command`'s basename against `#{pane_current_command}`. If Claude runs under a wrapper that reports a different command (e.g. `node`), set `@claude_command` to match — happy to add a dedicated match option if you'd prefer.

## Testing

- `@claude_scope session` (default): unchanged behavior; with no `claude-*` sessions the list is empty, no errors.
- `@claude_scope pane`: lists all panes running `claude` across multiple sessions, each with independent working/waiting/idle status from the hooks; `enter` jumps to the pane; `ctrl-x` kills the pane.
- `@claude_scope auto`: resolves to `session`/`pane` as documented.
- `bash -n` clean on all changed scripts; verified on tmux 3.6b (macOS).

author: thswlsqls
body:
## Issue
Closes #5518

## Change

`GoogleGenAiContentMapper.toChatResponse()` built `TokenUsage` from only `promptTokenCount` and `candidatesTokenCount` via the 2-arg `TokenUsage(input, output)` constructor, which derives the total as `input + output`. The SDK's `usageMetadata.totalTokenCount()` was ignored.

For thinking-enabled Gemini models (2.5/3.x), `totalTokenCount` also covers thoughts, cached, and tool-use tokens, so `prompt + candidates` is smaller than the billed total and `tokenUsage().totalTokenCount()` was under-reported. The chat, streaming, and batch paths all route through `toChatResponse()`, so all three were affected.

This switches to the 3-arg `TokenUsage` constructor, passing `meta.totalTokenCount()` when present and falling back to `prompt + candidates` when absent. The sibling module `langchain4j-vertex-ai-gemini` (`TokenUsageMapper`) already uses this 3-arg pattern.

```java
int totalTokenCount = meta.totalTokenCount().isPresent()
        ? meta.totalTokenCount().get()
        : promptTokenCount + candidatesTokenCount;
return new TokenUsage(promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, totalTokenCount);
```

Tested with google-genai SDK 1.59.0.

Behaviour note: for thinking models the reported total now grows to the correct, larger value. No API or signature change.

| idle ≥ 75% budget | `waiting for model · 225s` | `waiting for model · 225s/300s idle timeout` |

Fanout / dispatch-pending labels are unchanged and take precedence.

## Design decisions

- **60s threshold**: long enough that most normal provider think-time completes before the counter appears, short enough that a genuinely stuck stream is flagged.
- **75%-of-budget gate**: full `Ns/Ms idle timeout` only surfaces when the stream is at real risk of timing out.
- **Header bar**: provider/model names stay there — no need to repeat in every footer stall reason.
- **Incident logger**: `maybe_log_provider_wait_incident` keeps full idle/budget detail regardless of footer copy.

## Tests (4 passed)

| Test | Scenario |
|---|---|
| `provider_wait_reason_fresh_show_only_label` | idle < 60s → "waiting for model" |
| `provider_wait_reason_thresholded_show_idle_seconds` | idle ≥ 60s → counter appears, no budget |
| `provider_wait_reason_near_timeout_show_full_idle_budget` | idle ≥ 75% → full detail |
| `provider_wait_reason_dispatch_pending` | pending dispatch label returned |

Close https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/3189.

## Summary

Fixes #776.

## Red (before) — drift examples

| Dep | Workspace | runtime pin | tool pin | other drift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| regex | 1.11 | 1.11.1 | **1.10** | — |
| rustc-hash | 2.1 | — | — | glr-core 2.1.1 |

| serde_json, syn, quote, proc-macro2, anyhow, tempfile, proptest, insta, rayon, smallvec | — | — | — | all pinned directly per-crate |

Every workspace-eligible dep in the 7 core crates now uses \`{ workspace = true }\`. The only remaining direct version pins are:

- \`tree-sitter\` in **tool** and **tablegen** (0.25.2) — deliberately left because the workspace pins \`=0.26.7\` but those crates require \`0.25.x\`. Migrating them needs a coordinated tree-sitter bump and is out of scope.

author: matheuscllm-lgtm
body:
## Bug: scanner precificou 223 listings, entrega saiu VAZIA

Run **27925869658** (CI daily scan pós-fix de secrets): o scanner precificou tudo —
`37749 listings EN encontrados` → `223 após filtros (NM, EN, não-graded, ≥$10)` →
`223/223 consultados` → `Com preço TCG: 223` — mas **0** bateram a margem do
threshold. O postprocess então entregou:

```
_(nenhum listing precificado — nada a entregar)_
```

Ou seja: **223 precificados, entrega ZERO**. O fallback near-miss (commit #26),
que deveria SEMPRE render uma tabela, ficou vazio.

## Causa-raiz (file:line)

- **`cardtrader_scanner.py:2572`** — `if margin < self.threshold: continue`. O
  scanner descartava **no scan-time** todo listing abaixo do threshold. Com 0
  acima de 30%, a aba `Oportunidades` do XLSX saía **só com cabeçalho**.
- **`cardtrader_postprocess.py:1066`** — `pd.read_excel(args.input)` lê a primeira
  aba (`Oportunidades`) → **df vazio** → `build_delivery_markdown` cai em
  `deals.empty` → "nada a entregar". O fallback near-miss estava **derrotado na
  origem**: as linhas precificadas-abaixo-do-threshold nunca chegavam ao
  postprocess pra servir de near-miss.
- Agravante: os filtros pós-validação do scanner (`validation_status`
  NOT_VALIDATED fora dos top-N validados, `--min-net-margin`) também esvaziariam
  a lista.

Não era o caso "0 oportunidades acima do threshold com mensagem enganosa" — era
**perda de dados real**: o XLSX não carregava as linhas near-miss.

## Conserto — contrato `keep_all_priced` (default ON)

- O scanner agora **persiste TODO listing precificado** no XLSX, mesmo abaixo do
  threshold (`Opportunity.below_threshold`). O threshold vira **classificação
  downstream**. Novo contador `priced_below_threshold` + linha no resumo
  (`Near-miss (< X%, no XLSX): N`) → distinção **honesta** entre "0 precificado"
  e "precificou, 0 acima do threshold".
- Os filtros duros pós-validação (status, `--min-net-margin`) só culam o
  **subconjunto de oportunidades**; near-misses ficam preservados e re-anexados
  ordenados por margem bruta.
- Flag legada `--opportunities-only` restaura o XLSX enxuto (filtro duro antigo).
- `postprocess.enrich_df`: fallback preenche `live_brl`/`net_margin` a partir dos
  campos de **scan** (`Scan R$ (raw)` / `Net Margin % (scan)`) só onde os REAL
  faltam (linha não validada) — a tabela near-miss sai com Margem%/CT US$
  preenchidos, não vazios. **Não toca linhas validadas** (COMPRA/REVISAR).
- Mensagem do beco verdadeiramente-vazio reescrita: df vazio agora = **0
  precificado** (sem cobertura TCG / 0 passou NM/EN/preço), distinto de
  "precificou mas 0 acima do threshold" (que vira a tabela near-miss).

### Entrega resultante (antes vs depois)

Antes: `_(nenhum listing precificado — nada a entregar)_`

Depois (mesmo cenário, 0 acima do threshold):

```
### CardTrader — entrega (top N por margem · margem BRUTA, threshold 30%)
_⚠️ Nenhum deal acima do limiar — mostrando os candidatos mais próximos por margem..._
| # | Margem % | CT US$ | TCG US$ | Dif | Carta | ... | Flag | Links |
| 1 | 7% | 59.41 | 64.00 | 4.59 | Pichu (22) | ... | abaixo do limiar | [oferta](...) · [TCG](...) |
```

## Invariantes preservadas

- Margem **BRUTA** (sem taxa embutida, `--hub-fee 0.0`).
- Coluna `Links` combinada `[oferta](url) · [TCG](url)`.
- Classificação COMPRA/REVISAR; threshold em fração.

## Teste de regressão

Novo `tests/test_delivery_handoff_contract.py` (4 casos) trava o contrato
scanner-output → postprocess-input ponta-a-ponta:
1. near-miss precificado sobrevive ao XLSX (não é descartado);
2. nomes de coluna do handoff existem no XLSX (anti-rename silencioso);
3. **XLSX→entrega NÃO-vazia** (anti-regressão direta do beco "nada a entregar");
4. opt-out legado `--opportunities-only` volta a enxugar.

Um futuro rename de campo/aba ou re-introdução do filtro destrutivo **falha um
teste** em vez de entregar vazio silenciosamente.

**Suíte: 132/132 verde** (128 + 4 novos).

author: rescrv
body:
Introduce register_scalar_builtins, which defines the symbolic
operator words (+, -, *, /, %, bitwise, shifts, boolean, comparison,
and equality) along with their type contracts and the arithmetic
refinement signatures. register_all_builtins now wires these in
alongside the existing stack builtins, so programs can use `+`/`*`
directly instead of the test-only ADD/MUL helpers.

Supporting changes:

- refinement: accept operator tokens (+, -, *, /, comparisons) as
  signature heads, not just identifiers, so builtin operators can carry
  refinement contracts like `+ : ( a: Num b: Num -- c: Num where
  c = a + b )`.
- solver: capture input bindings before applying an effect and merge
  them into the output-binder scope, so guarantee predicates may relate
  results back to inputs (e.g. `c = a + b`). Also make Fourier-Motzkin
  back-substitution total by witnessing genuinely-free variables with a
  neutral value instead of panicking.
- shadow: map the symbolic aliases ==, &&, ||, and ! onto their
  existing interpreted operators.
- types: revise the Tier-0 reconciliation note to reflect that scalar
  operators are registered builtins rather than absent from the core.
- README: update examples to use the registered operators (+, *, /)
  instead of the ADD/MUL/GT helpers.

body:
## Summary

Stages the `bmad-quick-dev` and `bmad-code-review` skills for the upcoming `bmad-auto` orchestrator while keeping standard interactive usage unchanged. An opt-in automation mode is gated entirely behind the `BMAD_AUTO_MODE=1` environment variable — when it is unset, both skills behave exactly as before.

## What changed

**Activation gate (both skills)**
- New `Step 0: Automation Check` reads `BMAD_AUTO_MODE`. When `1`, it sets `{auto_mode}` and loads the new `automation-mode.md` rules; otherwise the automation files are never read.

**`bmad-quick-dev`**
- Checkpoints that normally HALT for human input now resolve via the `automation-mode.md` decision table when `{auto_mode}` (split decisions, token-limit overrides, intent-gap/missing-spec escalations).
- Scope target widens to 1,500–4,000 tokens in auto mode.

- Implement step routes to the new `step-auto-finalize.md` (review + commit belong to the orchestrator) unless `BMAD_AUTO_SKIP_REVIEW` requests the unattended internal triple-review.

author: chisanan232
body:
## Description

Adds a full framework adapter for **Agno** (pip `agno`, formerly Phidata) so the
Python SDK genuinely governs Agno agents at the in-process SDK layer.

Agno runs **every** function-tool body through a single chokepoint:
`agno.tools.function.FunctionCall.execute` (sync) and `FunctionCall.aexecute`
(async). An `Agent` builds a `FunctionCall` from the model's tool-call request and
invokes that method, which runs the user's tool entrypoint and wraps the return in
a `FunctionExecutionResult`. The adapter patches that one method:

- **deny** short-circuits the body entirely (the tool never runs) and returns a
  `FunctionExecutionResult(status="failure", ...)` carrying the block message;
- **pending** waits for approval, then allows or returns an approval-rejected result;
- **allow** runs the body and records the result.

Decision normalization, fail-closed-under-enforce (AAASM-3107), and the approval
helpers are reused from the CrewAI adapter so posture is identical across adapters.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature

## Breaking Changes

- [x] No

## Related Issues

- Related JIRA ticket: AAASM-3537 (parent AAASM-3535)

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added (fake-framework: allow/deny/pending/record, unknown-verdict
  fail-closed, async path, idempotent apply+revert)
- [x] Integration tests added — **real Agno** `FunctionCall` driven through the
  patched `execute()` as a **negative control**: a deny must short-circuit the real
  tool body (the test fails if the patch is ever a no-op), an allow runs and records
  it, revert restores unguarded execution, and the registry auto-detects the adapter.
- [x] `agno>=2.0.0` added to the `test` dependency group so the integration test runs
  in CI rather than being skipped.

Verified locally: `pytest test/unit` (537 passed, 1 native-only skip), the new
unit + integration suite (17 passed), `ruff check` clean on new files, `mypy`
clean. Negative control confirmed: neutering the patch makes the deny test fail
(body executes `[1000]`); restoring it passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (README + `docs/compatibility/frameworks.md`)
- [x] All tests passing

Refs AAASM-3537

author: ajz34
body:
This PR focus on broadcast matmul like `[1, M, K] * [B, K, N] -> [B, M, N]` (the 7th rule of [matmul broadcasting](https://data-apis.org/array-api/latest/API_specification/generated/array_api.matmul.html)). (this PR description discuss in row-major)

Previously, only `[B, M, K] * [B, K, N] -> [B, M, N]` works (axes after third dimension exactly matches). Now the axes after third dimensions can be broadcasted.

The code also refactored the handling of matmul layouts. Now we added a function `layout_matmul_dyn_row_major_with_lc` in rstsr-common, and let all other devices to call this function when dealing matmul.

author: kailash-kumar04
body:
## Problem
Creating a Google Ads search campaign from AdZump failed with HTTP 400:

> Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name **"startDate"** at `mutate_operations[1].campaign_operation.create`: Cannot find field.
> Unknown name **"endDate"** … Cannot find field.

## Cause
`build_google_search_ad_payload.py` built the campaign create with camelCase `startDate`/`endDate`. The Campaign resource's date fields are **`start_date` / `end_date`** (`YYYY-MM-DD`) — the same fields our GAQL reads use in `adapters/google/optimization/*` (e.g. `campaign.end_date`). Only the JSON keys were wrong; the `DD/MM/YYYY → YYYY-MM-DD` conversion (lines 30–35) was already correct.

## Fix
Two keys in the campaign create dict:
```diff
- **({"startDate": start_date} if start_date else {}),
- **({"endDate": end_date} if end_date else {}),
+ **({"start_date": start_date} if start_date else {}),
+ **({"end_date": end_date} if end_date else {}),
```

## Test
Re-run the campaign create from AdZump (`/api/ds/ads/generate-campaign`). The v23 mutate should no longer 400 on the date fields.

body:
## Что это
Шаг 1–2 пересборки сайта на **Astro** по ТЗ. Это PR в ветке — **продакшн (main) и старый сайт не затронуты**. Новый сайт смотрим через **Netlify Deploy Preview** этого PR.

## Что сделано
- **Каркас Astro** (статика), реальные пути, нативная мультиязычность: RU на `/`, EN на `/en/`, KO на `/ko/` (+ заложена структура под будущие языки).
- **Бренд-система** (navy / серебро / кобальт, шрифт **Manrope**, «металлические» серебряные заголовки) — в одном файле стилей + скил `/.skills/brand-system`.
- **Главная целиком**: многослойный герой с лёгким параллаксом + секции **«Проверка»** (2 статуса), **«Категории»** (4 направления), **«Под заказ»** (с формой заявки), **«Присутствие»**, **«Как это работает»**. Плавный скролл (Lenis) и появление блоков при прокрутке; всё уважает «уменьшить движение» (reduced-motion).
- **Форма «под заказ»** — статическая, с `data-netlify` (на старом SPA детект форм ломался — здесь сделано правильно) + страницы **«спасибо»** на 3 языках. Брендированная **404**.
- **SEO**: уникальные title/description на каждую страницу и язык, canonical, **hreflang + x-default**, Open Graph/Twitter, **JSON-LD** (Organization/WebSite), `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`.
- **Три скила** в репозитории: `brand-system`, `astro-i18n`, `seo`.
- Конфиг сборки **Netlify** (`npm run build` → `dist/`), Node 22.

## Контент-правила (соблюдено)
- Слова **«гарантия / guarantee» нет нигде** (проверено по собранному сайту).
- Два статуса проверки (документированный факт, не оценка качества); модель **«под заказ»**; присутствие **Корея/Япония/Китай/Турция + другие под запрос**; футер — **«совместный бренд AIA Group Ltd и Teranova Group Ltd»**; легковые авто — out of scope.

## Как посмотреть
1. В этом PR внизу, в списке проверок, появится **«Deploy Preview … netlify»** — нажми «Details». Это и есть новый сайт.
2. Переключатель языков — справа вверху (**RU / EN / KO**).
3. На что смотреть: тёмно-синий герой с серебристым «металлическим» заголовком и лёгким параллаксом; плавная прокрутка; блоки «выезжают» при скролле; внизу секции «Под заказ» — форма заявки.

## Важно знать (риски и допущения)
- **Ветка.** В ТЗ просили `astro-rebuild`, но рабочая сессия привязана к ветке `claude/gallant-cannon-2lgpe5`, поэтому PR из неё. На Deploy Preview это не влияет. Нужно именно `astro-rebuild` — скажи, пересоздам.
- **Внутренние страницы** (каталог, о нас, FAQ, контакты и т.д.) — это **шаг 4**. Сейчас их ссылки в меню ведут на аккуратную заглушку «страница скоро появится». Так и задумано по плану.
- **EN/KO.** Перевод сделан аккуратно, но по правилу ТЗ язык публикуем **только после вычитки носителем**. Эталон — RU.
- **Логотип.** Пока аккуратные плейсхолдеры в `/public/brand/` + текстовый логотип в нужном шрифте. Финальные файлы клади в `/public/brand/` с теми же именами — подхватятся.
- **Домен** в canonical/SEO задан как `https://teranovagroup.com` (по email). Если домен другой — правится в одном месте (`astro.config.mjs`).
- **Lighthouse.** JS ≈ 19 КБ, шрифты `display=swap`, семантика и a11y — должно быть в зелёной зоне; точные цифры посмотри на превью (вкладка Lighthouse в Chrome).
- **package.json / netlify.toml добавлены намеренно**: сайт на Astro требует сборки. На старый сайт и `main` это не влияет до мёрджа. Railway-конфиги не добавлял (по правилу репозитория).

## Дальше по плану
**Шаг 3 — СТОП**: смотрим превью, собираем правки. Затем **шаг 4** — внутренние страницы + остальные формы.

## Итог
- **Что изменилось:** на ветке появился новый сайт на Astro — готовая главная (ru/en/ko) в гамме navy + серебро + кобальт, со слоистым героем, SEO и рабочей формой. Старый сайт и `main` не тронуты.
- **Как откатить:** просто не мёрджить (или закрыть) этот PR — прод остаётся на старом `index.html`. Если уже смёрджено — кнопка «Revert» на PR.

This PR builds an educational, production-style DeepStream 8.x repository for RTSP in/out instance segmentation with YOLO11-Seg, including PyServiceMaker-style component decomposition and a custom TensorRT parser path for `NvDsInferInstanceMaskInfo` mask metadata flow.

- **Pipeline architecture + service decomposition**
  - Added modular Python app structure under `app/` with reusable source, inference, tracker, OSD, and sink components.
  - Implemented typed config loading and service assembly flow matching:

  - Added `configs/tracker_config.yml` and `configs/pipeline.yaml` for source/tracker/sink/service settings.

- **Custom parser scaffold for instance masks**
  - Added `parsers/nvdsparse_yolo_instance_mask.{h,cpp}` and `parsers/CMakeLists.txt`.
  - Parser code covers candidate decode, class-score selection, mask-coeff decode, class-aware NMS, prototype-mask projection, and `NvDsInferInstanceMaskInfo` population.
  - Clarified mask-buffer ownership expectation for DeepStream downstream lifecycle.

- **RTSP output and scriptable workflows**
  - Added `scripts/build_parser.sh`, `scripts/build_engine.sh`, and `scripts/run.sh`.

- **Focused baseline tests**

author: jasisz
body:
## What

Extends conditional-law proving to two more families, both kernel-checked `universal: yes` in Lean.

**Sortedness of insertion** (`isaplanner/prop_77`, `prod/lemma_12`, `sorted(xs) -> sorted(insort(x, xs))`): the bare list induction hypothesis does not give the lower bound on the head of the inserted list, so the prover SYNTHESIZES the supporting lemmas — the order bridge + its totality, the head-of-insert lower bound, and the sortedness head/tail destructors + cons constructor — then inducts on the list given, threading the premise.

**Membership with an order premise** (`isaplanner/prop_86`, `lt(x,y) -> elem(x, ins(y,xs)) = elem(x,xs)`): the membership emit now also supplies the comparison bridges, so an order premise discharges the equality dispatcher it implies via the bridges + `omega`.

**Codegen fix:** a user fn named `and`/`or`/`insert` collided with Lean's Bool operators / `Insert` typeclass → ambiguous definition (a sortedness module did not even build). These names now escape like `max`/`min` (`lemma_12` went `passed:false` → `true`).

**Corpus:** `prop_77`/`prop_86` rewritten from the `fn implies` / `fn goal` wrapper encodings to a `when` premise.

**Dafny:** the list-induction hint guards its recursive call with the premise on the tail, so a membership lemma's precondition holds (`prod/prop_36`); a list-independent premise guards to itself, unchanged.

## Verification (fresh `-o` each)

- **11 laws now Lean `universal:true`, kernel-clean** `[propext, Quot.sound]`: prop_70, prop_36, prop_37, prop_38, prop_46, prop_47, prop_71, lemma_19, prop_86, prop_77, lemma_12.
- **8 Dafny `passed:true`**: prop_70, prop_36/37/38/46/47/71, lemma_19 (sortedness + the `lt`-premised prop_86 stay bounded in Dafny — Lean `universal` covers them in the union).
- Broad sweep of every `when`-law, both backends: no `passed` regression.
- `tests/proof_spec` 184/0; `cargo clippy --features wasm,wasip2 --lib` clean; 3 conditional regression tests (bridge / membership / sortedness).

## Safety

Fail-closed throughout: an unrecognized conditional keeps its bounded proof; the synthesized sortedness lemmas are themselves kernel-checked (a misrecognized fn fails its own lemma and `#print axioms` withholds credit), so no false `universal` is possible.

author: akullganesh19
body:
## 🧬 Self-Healing Architecture Added

**What:** Created a robust resilience module (`backend/core/resilience.py`) with configurable exponential backoff retries and circuit breakers for both synchronous and asynchronous operations.

**Failure scenario protected:** External service dependencies (like Twilio, Groq, local Ollama, and the OpenClaw agent) failing transiently due to network blips or temporary outages, which previously caused hard crashes, silent failures, or indefinite hanging. 

**Recovery flow:** 
When an external call fails (e.g., `requests.get` times out), the function will automatically retry with exponential backoff. If the service completely goes down and repeated attempts fail, the circuit breaker opens to fail fast, preserving system resources and preventing cascading failures across the application.

**Blast radius before:** A single API timeout could bring down background tasks or interrupt the core forensic pipelines without any chance of automatic recovery.

**Blast radius after:** The system transparently absorbs transient network faults. Extended outages result in clean, fast failures that degrade gracefully rather than hanging the server.

**Logging/alerting:** The `@with_retries` and `CircuitBreaker` classes log warnings on every retry and errors when the max attempts are exhausted or the circuit breaker trips.

**Remaining failure points:** Genesis should next address the idempotency of SMS dispatching and potential atomic race conditions in the threat scoring engine.

author: strsu
body:
## 문제

service repo admin에서 Step2(`EpisodeFaceIdentifyWorkflow`)를 단독 트리거하면 다음 오류로 액티비티가 실패하는 경우가 있었습니다.

```
{"message":"activity Heartbeat timeout","source":"Server","timeoutFailureInfo":{"timeoutType":"TIMEOUT_TYPE_HEARTBEAT"}}
```

## 원인

`identify_episode_faces()`가 가장 먼저 호출하는 `_seed_confirmed_faces()`는 **해당 웹툰 전체**의 수동 확정(`is_confirmed=true`) 얼굴을 조회해 Chroma에 시딩합니다. 이 함수는 얼굴마다 S3 crop 다운로드 + model-api 임베딩 호출을 **순차로** 수행하지만 `heartbeat_cb`를 받지 않아 루프 중 heartbeat를 전혀 보내지 않았습니다.

웹툰에 확정 얼굴이 누적될수록(회차가 진행될수록) 이 시딩 단계의 처리 시간이 길어지고, `face_identify_episode` 액티비티의 `heartbeat_timeout`(2분, `temporal/workflows.py`)을 넘기면 Temporal 서버가 heartbeat 미수신으로 액티비티를 강제 종료시킵니다.

다른 단계(`_fetch_and_embed_all`, 메인 매칭 루프)는 이미 동일한 패턴으로 heartbeat를 보내도록 구현되어 있었고, `_seed_confirmed_faces`만 빠져 있었습니다.

## 수정

- `_seed_confirmed_faces`에 `heartbeat_cb`/`heartbeat_value` 파라미터 추가
- 확정 얼굴 처리(또는 skip)마다 동일한 값으로 heartbeat 전송해 2분 타임아웃 타이머를 갱신
- `identify_episode_faces`의 호출부도 기존 `heartbeat_cb`/`resume_from`을 그대로 전달하도록 업데이트

## Test plan

- [ ] 확정 얼굴이 다수 누적된 웹툰에서 Step2 단독 재실행(admin) 시 heartbeat timeout 없이 완료되는지 확인
- [ ] 기존 `identify_episode_faces` 단위 테스트(있는 경우) 통과 확인

author: byvfx
body:
## What

Fixes #93 — the Gamma control did nothing while an OCIO view was active.

**Cause:** under OCIO the display chain (gamma → LUT → sRGB) is handed to OCIO, so the main shader runs with `gamma = 1` and the user's gamma was silently dropped; the OCIO blit pass never re-applied it.

**Fix:** re-apply the user gamma in **display space, after the OCIO transform**, on the image (the background stays neutral, composited after — matching the OCIO path's design):
- **GPU:** added `gamma` to `BlitUniforms` (reusing the spare `_pad_a` slot — no size/alignment change) and `pow(rgb, 1/gamma)` in the blit shader. The blit re-runs every frame with fresh uniforms, so gamma updates live **without** re-running the cached OCIO passes (no perf cost).
- **CPU fallback:** the same display-space gamma after `proc.apply_rgba` in `generate_texture_ocio`.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --lib` — 161 pass; `cargo build` + `cargo build --features ocio` clean; `fmt` + `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` clean.
- **Manual (the report):** with an OCIO display/view active, drag Gamma → image responds now; Shift+G / right-click resets to 1.0 (no-op); exposure unchanged; toggling OCIO off keeps the non-OCIO gamma path working.

Closes #93

# Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

Successfully implemented Vercel Web Analytics for this PHP-based e-commerce project (SaajGhar - a saree shopping website).

## What Was Implemented

### Framework Analysis
- Identified this as a pure PHP project (not a JavaScript framework like Next.js or React)
- No package.json or npm dependencies - this is a traditional PHP application with MySQL backend
- Project consists of 8 PHP pages generating HTML output

### Implementation Approach
Based on the official Vercel Analytics documentation (fetched from https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart), I used the **static site script tag approach** which is the correct method for PHP-generated HTML pages.

### Files Created
1. **includes/analytics.php** - Shared analytics include file containing:
   - Vercel Web Analytics initialization script
   - Deferred loading of analytics script from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`

### Files Modified
Added `<?php include 'includes/analytics.php'; ?>` to the `<head>` section of all 8 PHP pages:

1. **index.php** - Homepage with featured products
2. **products.php** - Product listing page
3. **product_details.php** - Individual product details page

The analytics implementation uses the official Vercel Web Analytics script pattern for static sites:

```html
<script>
  window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

This script:
- Initializes the `window.va` function for analytics tracking
- Loads the Vercel insights script asynchronously with `defer` for optimal performance
- Will be automatically served by Vercel when the project is deployed

- Now all pages have complete and valid HTML structure with analytics included

1. The `/_vercel/insights/script.js` route will be automatically available

## Summary

Follow-up to #2519 (which retired the draft answer-lane by defaulting `DRAFT_ANSWER_LANE_RETIRED=true`). This PR deletes the now-unreachable draft-transport code path that was already permanently off in production.

- Deletes `telegram-plugin/draft-transport.ts`, its tests (`draft-transport.test.ts`, `draft-retirement-wiring.test.ts`), and all dead branches gated on `sendMessageDraftFn`, `usesDraftTransport`, `SWITCHROOM_DRAFT_ANSWER_LANE` / `DRAFT_ANSWER_LANE_RETIRED`, and `PROGRESS_CARD_DRAFT_TRANSPORT`
- Simplifies `resolveAnswerLaneConfig` from a 3-state (visible / draft / dormant) to a 2-state (visible / dormant) decision table — the `draftFnAvailable` input is gone
- Folds in `src/config/schema.ts` in-place DM throttle default cleanup

**No runtime behavior change** — every turn has been landing on the in-place `sendMessage`+`editMessageText` path since #2519; this PR just removes the dead branches that can no longer execute.

## What was kept

- `stream-controller.ts`, `stream-reply-handler.ts` — in-place streaming engine

author: mohitraipr
body:
## Root cause
DRR's sales feed (**mini_sales_report**) froze on **Jun 11**. Diagnosed on prod:
- Sales live only in **Faridabad (173983, mohit@kotty.in)** + **Delhi (176318, pankaj@kotty.in)**; the primary/parent has zero sales.
- Commit `dae8692` (deployed **Jun 11**: `/access/token` auth + primary-location snapshot pull) added more report-queue calls per run. EasyEcom then **429-rate-limits** the report-queue endpoint, and there was **no retry/backoff** — so the Faridabad/Delhi mini-sales pulls silently failed every night (`mini_sales:delhi/faridabad error 429`). Orders kept working because `getAllOrders` is a live API, not a queued report.

Timing is conclusive: last good sync Jun 11 (old code that night), first broken Jun 12 (first run on the new code).

## Fix
- **429 backoff + retry** on `reports/queue` and `reports/download` (`withReport429Retry`, honours `Retry-After`, exp backoff 5→60s).
- **Global stagger** between every report-queue call (`EASYECOM_REPORT_GAP_MS`, default 4s) so the nightly burst stays under EasyEcom's limit.

So the nightly pull now self-heals instead of silently freezing. 115/115 tests.

## Also done out-of-band
- Ran a manual backfill (with this fixed code) to refill mini-sales Jun 12→today.
- Note for ops: if 429s persist even staggered, EasyEcom has an account-level report cap worth raising with them.

author: marko1olo
body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced O(N*M) lookups inside nested loops in `communalAuthoredOwnerForRoomName` and `reinforceCommunalRingAuthoredHqTerritory` with map lookups (O(N+M)).
- Created a static initialization map `COMMUNAL_AUTHORED_OWNER_MAP` to fetch territory owners by name dynamically.
- Constructed a `roomByName` map mapping room name to `Room` at the beginning of `reinforceCommunalRingAuthoredHqTerritory`'s second half.

🎯 **Why:** 
Previously, `communalAuthoredOwnerForRoomName` and `reinforceCommunalRingAuthoredHqTerritory` performed linear searches across `world.rooms` (using `Array.prototype.find`) while inside a loop over the constant `COMMUNAL_HQ_COMPOUNDS`. This caused unnecessary performance overhead for generating room configurations on certain procedural design floors. Using standard ES6 Maps makes the lookups practically O(1).

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Based on isolated benchmark testing simulating 3000 rooms and 200 specific target targets scattered:
- Old time: ~2498ms
- New time: ~265ms
- Improvement: ~9.39x speedup in the specific loop iterations.

## What this is

A ~20.5s, 16:9 **launch/intro film for momfluence.app**, authored to the [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) composition contract. It opens by *grabbing* the signature HyperFrames **"HTML → video"** kinetic title and re-pointing it at the product — `HTML → video → moms → money` — then walks the locked product-thesis message: **the news → the eligibility puncture → the CTA.**

Everything lives under `videos/momfluence-intro/`. Nothing in the app/build changes.

## 👀 Review it now (no install)

Open **`videos/momfluence-intro/storyboard.html`** in a browser. It's a reviewable scene table that embeds every scene's **densest beat** as a live, looping composition at 0.32× scale, plus the named components and the transition map.

## What's in the package

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `frame.md` | Design system **inverted for the frame** — navy/coral tokens, fixed-px scale, locked voice (no web chrome) |
| `storyboard.md` | Scene table + per-scene narration, arc = **Hook → Build → Punch → Resolve** |
| `storyboard.html` | **Reviewable HTML scene table** — embeds all keyframes + components live |
| `components/kinetic-title.html` | The **"HTML → video" word-morph** (the grabbed launch animation) |
| `components/prompt-box.html` | Recommendation → tracking link → payout chips (the mechanism) |
| `components/transitions.html` | Named seams: `flash-through-white`, `coral-wipe`, `mask-up`, `prompt-send` |
| `compositions/scene_s1…s6.html` | One composition per scene, opening on its **most visually dense beat** |

## The 6 scenes

1. **s1 · Hook** — kinetic `HTML → video → moms` morph
2. **s2 · The news** — "moms are getting paid *celebrity-tier money*…"
3. **s3 · Eligibility puncture** — 1M struck vs `500 ✓ a regular mom` + group-chat bubble
4. **s4 · The mechanism** — prompt-box: reco → link → `20–50%` payout chips
5. **s5 · The product** — dashboard, earnings count-up `$0 → $40`, `$5/mo`
6. **s6 · CTA** — lockup + "Real moms. Real money. Real easy." + **momfluence.app**

## Conventions followed (HyperFrames contract)

- Root `data-composition-id`/`data-scene-id`, fixed `data-width/height/duration`, `overflow:hidden`
- One **paused** GSAP timeline per file on `window.__timelines`, built synchronously
- Deterministic: no `Math.random` / `Date.now` / network / `repeat:-1` in the registered timeline
- Transform/opacity/clip-path only; layout pre-computed; each keyframe carries `data-poster-time` = its densest beat

## Rendering to MP4

The CLI/render half of HyperFrames isn't vendored here (install was out of scope). To produce the actual video:

```bash
npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes
npx hyperframes preview videos/momfluence-intro
npx hyperframes render  videos/momfluence-intro --out momfluence-intro.mp4
```

Source of truth: voice from `docs/product-thesis.md`; tokens from `docs/design/lp-baseline-v2/tokens.html`.

author: idan
body:
Spike of the procedural scene editor from `docs/scenes`: a SvelteKit (Svelte 5) + Tailwind + bits-ui app with a CodeMirror shader editor beside a live 64×64 simulator, including transport controls, type-driven uniform inputs, inline compile errors, and an opcode/pixel cost estimator. It implements a GLSL-flavored shader language (lexer/parser/AST), a bytecode compiler that lowers vectors to scalar ops, and a shared Rust renderer (`renderer/`) — an f32 stack VM compiled to wasm32 — that drives the preview, with the TS tree-walking interpreter kept as a parity oracle (bit-identical, Δ0/255, via portable integer-hash value noise). Also adds an authoring guide (`docs/scenes/authoring.md`) and updates `CLAUDE.md`/`docs/scenes/README.md` to reflect the new `web/` and `renderer/` workspaces. The renderer crate compiles to WASM via `bun run build:wasm` (wasm-pack); build artifacts and secrets are gitignored, so a fresh checkout runs `bun install` + `build:wasm`. The large `web/worker-configuration.d.ts` is wrangler's generated Cloudflare runtime types from the scaffold.

author: tianshanghong
body:
## Problem
`./miuops add-domain <host> dev.example.com` (or a subdomain in host_vars on `up`) failed with **`Zone not found for 'dev.example.com'`**. Cloudflare zones exist at the **registered-domain** level (`example.com`), so querying `zones?name=dev.example.com` returns nothing.

This blocked the documented prod/dev split (apex on one server, `dev.` subdomain on another).

## Fix
`cf_zone_id` now walks up the labels (`dev.example.com` → `example.com`) and returns the first/most-specific matching zone. The subdomain CNAMEs (`dev.example.com` + `*.dev.example.com`) are then created **in the parent zone**, which is how Cloudflare expects subdomain records. Apex behavior is unchanged. Auth/network errors still fail fast.

## Tests
Adds offline tests: subdomain→parent walk, apex regression, and die-when-no-parent-zone. `bash tests/cli_test.sh` → ALL PASS.

author: hsgiga
body:
## Summary

Adds a `deploy.placement` config block that maps 1:1 onto Cloudflare Wrangler's [`placement`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/placement/) object, so Smart Placement and region/hostname hints land in the generated `wrangler.jsonc`. Implemented like the existing `deploy.vpc` feature: a pure helper, wired into the generator, with schema + docs + tests.

Example:

```yaml
deploy:
  name: status
  placement:
    mode: smart
    region: aws:eu-central-1
    hostname: api.example.com
```

## Changes

- **`scripts/lib/placement.ts`** (new): `validatePlacementConfig` + `buildPlacement`. `mode` is restricted to `smart` (the only value Wrangler accepts); `region`/`hostname` pass through; at least one field is required.
- **`scripts/generate-wrangler.ts`**: emits `placement` into `wrangler.jsonc` when `deploy.placement` is set, following the delete-then-conditionally-set pattern used for `vpc`/`send_email`/`routes`.
- **`scripts/lib/deploy-config.ts`**: `placement?` added to `DeployConfig`.
- **`config.schema.json`**: `placement_config` def under `deploy` (`mode` enum `["smart"]`, `region`, `hostname`; `additionalProperties: false`, `minProperties: 1`).
- **Docs**: `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` (new `deploy.placement` section), `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (pipeline note), `config.example.yaml` (commented example).
- **`test/placement.spec.ts`** (new): parsing/validation + generated-config coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Config accepts `[placement]` with `hostname`, `mode`, and `region` (as `deploy.placement` in this project's YAML config).
- [x] Generated Wrangler configuration preserves supplied placement values.
- [x] `mode = "smart"` is supported.
- [x] `region = "aws:eu-central-1"` is supported.
- [x] Tests cover parsing and generated configuration.

## Verification

Generated `wrangler.jsonc` from a `deploy.placement` block:

```json
"placement": {
	"mode": "smart",
	"region": "aws:eu-central-1",
	"hostname": "api.example.com"
}
```

Omitted entirely when `deploy.placement` is unset.

author: takashi-matsuyama
body:
## What

Closing the open chat is now easier: **clicking/tapping anywhere outside the panel** closes it, and so does **Escape** — in addition to the × button.

## How

- A document-level `click` handler closes the panel unless the event target is **inside the widget root**. Since both the launcher and the panel live inside `root`, the click that *opens* the panel never self-closes it, and interacting with the chat itself doesn't close it either — only a genuine outside click/tap does.
- `Escape` closes the panel when open (standard dialog affordance).
- `close()` gains an optional `returnFocus` (default `true`): the × button and Escape return focus to the launcher, but an **outside click does not steal focus** from wherever the visitor clicked on the page.

## Verification

- typecheck / build (widget 9.35 kB) / lint / format green; full repo **1226 tests passing**. `dist/` gitignored.

author: bimapangestu28
body:
## Summary

Adds a first-class **flow-emit channel**: a flow can emit a business event via an `emit.event` node, and that event surfaces on the public `RunResult.emitted_events` for the host (greentic-start) to re-route. This is the emit-side of the Operala event program (#4).

Data path: `emit.event` node → dedicated `emitted_events` channel on `ExecutionState` (kept **out** of the reply `egress`) → `FlowExecution.emitted_events` → `RunResult.emitted_events: Vec<serde_json::Value>`.

- Payload is passed through **verbatim** — the engine does NOT mint envelopes (greentic-start is the sole minter of `event_id`/`occurred_at`/`source`/`scope`). Raw `serde_json::Value` keeps zero greentic-types coupling.

## Commits
- `feat(runner): add emit.event builtin node kind with dedicated emitted_events channel`
- `feat(engine): thread emitted_events through FlowExecution finalize` (introduces `FinalizedFlow`; egress→reply logic behavior-preserved)
- `feat(runner-desktop): surface emitted_events on RunResult`
- `style(runner-desktop): rustfmt A3 test code`
- `fix: clear emitted_events from snapshot on Waiting paths to prevent double delivery`

## Correctness notes
- **Reply isolation:** `emit.event` never leaks into the user reply; `emit.log`/`emit.response`/other still go to `egress`. `clear_egress` does not touch `emitted_events`.
- **Once-only delivery across wait/resume:** a pre-wait emitted event is surfaced on the Waiting result and then cleared from the persisted snapshot, so it does NOT reappear on resume. Covered by a flow-level wait→resume regression test.

## Testing
- `cargo clippy -p greentic-runner-host/-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --lib` (default features): green.

author: allyblockcast[bot]
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Phase 1.5 of `reconcile-milestones` iterates all `milestone-link:*` plugin state entries and stamps PC issue `milestoneId`. For it to visit a Linear milestone's issues, a MilestoneLink must exist for that milestone.
> - Initial hypothesis: the reverse issue state key was missing for host-linked issues → `getLinkByLinear` returned null → skipped. The PR's phase 1.5 fallback addresses this.
> - Human tester refuted: `replaceExisting:true` relink (which rewrites both the forward AND reverse issue state keys) did NOT heal the issue. "The skip is NOT simply reverse state missing."
> - Investigation: the tester queried Linear directly via `paperclip-linear-mcp-token` and confirmed `BLO-4133.projectMilestone = { id: 4407a49e, name: "Tokeneconomics + supply dashboard" }`. So the issue IS attached to a milestone in Linear.
> - Root cause identified: PC milestone `956b7913` ("Tokeneconomics + supply dashboard") was created by title-backfill and was never bound via a MilestoneLink. Phase 1's `getMilestoneLinkByLinear("4407a49e")` returns null → it creates a NEW PC milestone (duplicate) and writes a MilestoneLink for that new milestone. The original `956b7913` stays unbound. Phase 1.5 never visits BLO-4133 via `956b7913`, and when it visits via the new duplicate, the PC issue's `milestoneId` gets stamped with the WRONG (duplicate) milestone ID.
> - Fix: before phase 1 creates a new PC milestone, check if one with the same name already exists in the same project. If so, bind to it instead.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**
After BLO-11247 formed host-links between legacy Linear-native milestone-attached Paperclip issues, `reconcile-milestones` phase 1.5 ran but stamped 0 PC issues (`326 skipped`). Even after relinking `119230d6 ↔ BLO-4133` with `replaceExisting:true`, re-nulling `milestoneId`, and re-running reconcile — still `0 stamped`.

**Root cause (confirmed)**
PC milestone `956b7913` ("Tokeneconomics + supply dashboard") was created by title-backfill, not by phase 1 import. Phase 1's `getMilestoneLinkByLinear("4407a49e")` returns null and creates a NEW PC milestone (duplicate). The original `956b7913` never gets a MilestoneLink, so phase 1.5 never visits BLO-4133 in the context of the canonical milestone. On subsequent runs, phase 1 sees the MilestoneLink for the duplicate and skips — the duplicate proliferates.

**Expected behavior**
Phase 1 should bind to the existing PC milestone when one with the same name already exists in the project, not create a duplicate. After that, phase 1.5 stamps `milestoneId` against the canonical milestone.

**Paperclip version or commit**
`sha-ec8292c` (deployed 2026-06-22)

**Deployment mode**
Self-hosted server

## What Changed

### Phase 1 dedup fix (root cause)
- **`worker.ts`** (phase 1): Pre-load all PC milestones into a `projectId:normalizedName` map before phase 1 runs. When `getMilestoneLinkByLinear` returns null for a Linear milestone, check the map first. If a PC milestone with the same name exists in the same project, call `createMilestoneLink` pointing to it (`reconciled++`) instead of creating a new PC milestone (`imported++`). The cache is updated after any new creation to handle duplicate Linear milestone names within a single run.
- **`worker.ts`** (phase 2): Reuse the same preloaded list instead of calling `ctx.milestones.list` a second time.

### Phase 1.5 host-link fallback (defense in depth)
- **`sync.ts`**: export `repairReverseLink(ctx, link)` — writes only the reverse plugin state key. Throws if either field is falsy. Idempotent.
- **`worker.ts`** (phase 1.5): hoist `getByLinearIssueId` availability check to a one-time pre-loop warn; when `getLinkByLinear` returns null and fallback is available, look up DB host-link, verify `forwardLink.linearIssueId === li.id && forwardLink.paperclipIssueId === hostLinked.id`, call `repairReverseLink`, stamp.
- **`worker.ts`**: add `membershipSkipped` to return value (was missing).

### Tests
- **`tests/plugin.spec.ts`**: add test "phase 1 links to an existing PC milestone by name instead of creating a duplicate (BLO-11742)" — confirms `ctx.milestones.create` is NOT called and `createMilestoneLink` is called with `paperclipMilestoneId: existing-id`.
- **`tests/plugin.spec.ts`**: add test "stamps milestoneId via host-link fallback when reverse plugin state key is missing (BLO-11742)".
- **`tests/plugin.spec.ts`**: add `repairReverseLink` mock.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm --filter paperclip-plugin-linear test` → 219/219 pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter paperclip-plugin-linear exec tsc --noEmit` → clean
- [ ] After deploy: trigger `reconcile-milestones`, confirm `stamped ≥ 1` and `milestoneId` of `119230d6` restored to `956b7913`

## Risks

- **Low** — phase 1 dedup is additive: only changes the path when `getMilestoneLinkByLinear` returns null AND a same-name PC milestone already exists
- **Low** — the preloaded milestone map is loaded once per reconcile run; no per-milestone API calls added
- **Low** — host-link fallback is idempotent; only repairs missing reverse keys, no overwrites

Claude Sonnet 4.6 (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) via Paperclip BackendEngineerGo agent; tool use enabled

## Ce schimba

Review-ul a semnalat ca serviciile de notificari au shape-uri runtime "prea generale" (`GuildSettings & Record<string, unknown>`, payload-uri `unknown`). Partea **contenita si sigura** din asta:

`GuildSettings` poarta deja `[key: string]: unknown`, deci `& Record<string, unknown>` **nu adauga nimic** — era zgomot pe calea critica. Simplificat la `GuildSettings` (7 ocurente in `updateNotificationService.ts` + `discountNotificationService.ts`) si scoase **3 caste redundante**:
- `(guild as { seenHashVersionUpdates?: unknown }).seenHashVersionUpdates` si varianta `Discounts` — index-sig-ul da deja `unknown` la acces direct;
- `guilds as Array<GuildSettings & Record<string, unknown>>` la `runConcurrent` — `guilds` e deja `GuildSettings[]` din contractul `GuildModel`.

The `/reel/[postId]` deep-link page rendered **10 hardcoded French strings** to every user regardless of interface language — a Prisme-UI break on a *publicly shared entry surface*. author: hua-bang
body:
## Summary
Fixes text clipping in full-width TUIs (like Claude/Codex) by removing horizontal padding from xterm rows, and improves terminal startup UX with a boot overlay that masks the blank panel while the shell initializes.

## Key Changes

- **Terminal column overflow fix**: Removed `padding: 0 4px` from `.xterm-rows` in WorkspaceTerminalDock, AgentNodeBody, and TerminalNodeBody. The FitAddon derives column count from the container element and cannot account for padding on inner rows, causing the last column to overflow and get clipped. Container padding now serves as the gutter instead.

- **Boot overlay**: Added a "Starting terminal…" overlay with spinner animation that displays from the moment the dock opens until the first byte of PTY output arrives. This prevents the blank white panel during shell initialization from appearing as a stalled state.

- **Terminal initialization improvements**:
  - Call `fitAddon.fit()` immediately after opening the terminal (before spawning) so the shell starts at the correct cols/rows rather than the 80×24 default
  - Set `booting` state to `false` on first data byte, exit, or spawn error to dismiss the overlay

- **Favicon handling refactor**: Extracted favicon display logic into a `NodeLeadingGlyph` component in CanvasNodeHeader that properly manages favicon load failures with state, replacing inline conditional rendering. Removed favicon display from IframeAddressButton and associated CSS.

- **Markdown code block labeling**: Added `AUTO_DETECT_LABEL_MIN_RELEVANCE` threshold (5) so highlight.js auto-detection only labels code blocks when confident. Low-relevance guesses (e.g., JSON mislabeled as CSS) now fall back to neutral `text` label while retaining syntax coloring.

- **Contenteditable serialization**: Fixed pasted multi-line text collapsing into a single line by treating block-level elements (div, p, li, blockquote, etc.) as line boundaries in `serializeEditable()`.

- **i18n**: Added `'workspaceTerminal.starting': 'Starting terminal…'` message and Chinese translation.

## Implementation Details

- Boot overlay uses `position: absolute; inset: 0` to cover the terminal container and `pointer-events: none` to remain non-interactive
- Spinner animation (`workspace-terminal-spin`) rotates 360° over 0.7s; overlay fades in over 0.18s
- `NodeLeadingGlyph` uses `useEffect` to reset favicon failure state when the URL changes, allowing recovery after navigation
- Block-level tag detection in `serializeEditable()` checks `BLOCK_LINE_TAGS` set and only inserts newlines when not already at output start or newline

- **PUT /api/v1/auth/session/active-organization**（`switchActiveOrganization`, operator-authenticated）— body `{ organizationId }`。所属メンバーシップを検証し、対象 org の externalId + その org での role + **不変の superadmin** で apex JWT を**再発行**（claims は login と同形）。応答は `AuthSession`。

### 認可・セキュリティ

- ⑤ i18n 4 言語（ADR 0009 方針により据え置き）。

author: jcfischer
body:
Fixes #327.

### Problem

The #326 fail-closed backstop (`src/adapters/grok/hooks/shell-policy-core.mjs`, `matchedPrivateMarkerSource`) denied the reported `Frobnicate-Item @.soma/memory/x`, but the **class** was not fully closed. An interposed `./` or `~/` between the non-path prefix and the marker still fell through to ALLOW:

- `Frobnicate-Item @./.soma/memory/x` → **ALLOW** (should DENY)
- `Frobnicate-Item @~/.soma/memory/x` → **ALLOW** (should DENY)

The `/` from `./`|`~/` is a path-continue char, so it sits immediately before `.soma` and the plain `(?:^|boundary)\.soma/` scan misses. These `@`-glued tokens also resolve via `resolveToolPath` to a literal `@.`/`@~` segment under no root (branch-1 miss) and carry no absolute marker (absolute-scan miss), so they reached `policy check` as a toothless ALLOW.

### Fix

Add an optional, **boundary-gated** relative anchor `(?:\./|~/)?` between the boundary and the marker. It stays boundary-gated, so the over-block guards hold:
- benign `my.somatic` → ALLOW (no `.soma/`, no boundary-anchored bare `.soma`)
- nested `proj/.soma/x` → ALLOW (project-local soma, not the home root — `/` before `.soma` with no boundary-gated `./`|`~/` anchor)

### Tests

- Unit (`createShellPolicyExtractor`): both `@./.soma/` and `@~/.soma/` emit the private **root** as `sourcePath` (rides the relative leg — empty `policyMarkers`), plus a nested-`proj/.soma` over-block guard.
- Installed-hook e2e: both glued forms deny end-to-end (`decision: deny`, exit 2).

### Verification

- `bun run typecheck` — clean.
- `bun test test/grok-hook.test.ts` — 49 pass / 0 fail (47 + 2 new).
- `bun test` grok-adapter/doctor/install/uninstall + substrate-adapters — 77 pass / 0 fail.
- Regex matrix checked directly: the two `@./`/`@~/` variants now DENY; `my.somatic` and `proj/.soma` (and deeper `a/b/.soma`) stay ALLOW.

macOS run only (the suite is platform-independent by construction — hooks spawn via node with pinned HOME, no live grok); CI runs the Linux gate.

body:
[FIX] avoid opening non-printer vendor-specific USB devices
=
Avoid opening arbitrary vendor-specific USB devices during printer
discovery. Some non-printer devices (e.g. fingerprint readers) expose
bulk endpoints and were incorrectly treated as printer candidates,
causing intermittent USB access errors on Windows.

Limit discovery to actual printer devices to improve reliability and
prevent false access-denied errors.

[FIX] Support cash drawer opening on both kick-out pins
=
Some cash drawers are connected to pin 2 instead of pin 1.
Previously, the open drawer command was sent only to pin 1, causing
certain cash drawers not to open.

This change sends the kick-out pulse to both pin 1 and pin 2 to improve
compatibility across different printer and cash drawer configurations.

body:
## Release v0.51.577 — failed steer no longer cancels active run (#4577)

Ships **#4577** (dso2ng) — a behavioral fix so a failed Steer doesn't silently kill your in-flight run.

### What
When `/steer` (or the `busy_input_mode='steer'` path) couldn't be delivered — the agent isn't running/cached, or an older hermes-agent doesn't support steer — WebUI used to silently fall back to interrupt+queue, **cancelling the active stream**. It now restores your draft to the composer and leaves the active run untouched, so you explicitly choose Queue or Interrupt. `_trySteer` returns a `delivered` boolean; `send()` only clears staged files when the steer was actually delivered (a failed steer keeps them staged).

### Review trail
- **Codex (regression gate): SAFE TO SHIP** — verified a failed steer does not touch `CANCEL_FLAGS`/cancel the run, the draft + staged files are preserved on failure, a delivered steer still clears files, no stuck-busy state, the backend hunk is comment-only (failure paths already returned `{accepted:False}`), and the i18n changes are value-only on pre-existing keys (locale parity intact).
- **Full suite: 10059 passed, 0 failed.** Steer/busy-input tests: 48 passed; locale parity: 173 passed.

Co-authored-by: dso2ng <dso2ng@users.noreply.github.com>

Closes #4577

author: yumike
body:
Resolves the three grouped maintainability/correctness items in #545, all verified against current viewer code.

## Changes

**1. `documentId` guard on `resolve`/`reopen`** (`state/comments.svelte.ts`)
`create`/`delete`/`restore` already gate their `items` write on `this.documentId === response.documentId`; `resolve`/`reopen` did not. A resolve/reopen completing after the user navigates away could write the updated row into the next page's comment view. Added the same guard, making all four mutators consistent.

**2. Abort the in-flight `list()` on `clear()`** (`state/comments.svelte.ts`)
`load()` already holds an `AbortController` and guards its success write with `if (signal.aborted) return`, but `clear()` didn't abort. Navigating to a page that shows no comments (e.g. Home) calls `clear()` without re-triggering a load, so an in-flight fetch resolved with `signal.aborted === false` and repopulated the just-cleared list with the previous page's comments. `clear()` now aborts and nulls the controller so the existing guard drops the result.

**3. Dedupe five duplicated mutation handlers** (new `lib/comments/actions.ts`)
`resolve`/`reopen`/`delete`/`restore`/`reply` were byte-for-byte identical across `PageComments.svelte` and `CommentSidebar.svelte`. Extracted into a plain `createCommentActions(comments, notify)` factory matching the other `$lib/comments/*` helpers. The four status/delete actions notify-and-swallow; `reply` notifies and rethrows so the composer keeps the draft. Each component keeps only a thin `handleReply` wrapper for its component-specific focus restoration (which diverged after the keyboard-focus fix landed). Net −124 lines in the components.

## Testing

- New unit tests: `createCommentActions` factory (7 cases), the `clear()`-abort behavior (production-faithful reject-on-abort path + the resolve-after-clear guard), and the `documentId` guard across all four mutators (resolve/reopen/delete/restore).
- `npm -w @rwdocs/viewer run check`: 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- `npm -w @rwdocs/viewer test`: 542 passing.

author: marianodelrio
body:
## T-020 — Training loop (InfoNCE)

### What was implemented
- `libs/ml/trainer.py` — new file with `train(session, profile) → TrainingResult`, InfoNCE contrastive loss with in-batch negatives (τ=0.1), Adam optimizer (lr=1e-3, 20 epochs), gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0). Saves `user_tower.pt`, `item_tower.pt`, and `vocab.json` to `models_store/`.
- `libs/ml/trainer.py` — also defines `TrainingResult` and `TowerPair` dataclasses; `TowerPair` is designed for use by T-021 (inference engine).
- `tests/unit/test_trainer.py` — 6 new tests: `TrainingResult`/`TowerPair` field validation, loss-decreases-over-5-epochs on synthetic data, model files saved verification, `_populate_features` helper (skips missing tracks, populates known tracks).

### Key decisions
- **Signature `train(session, profile)` instead of `train(session)`**: the task spec says `train(session)` but `build_training_set` requires a `UserProfile`, and importing `libs.profile` from `libs.ml` would violate the DAG. The API layer calls `build_profile(session)` first, then passes the result to `train()`. Approved by human before implementation.
- **Single-user InfoNCE**: all user feature vectors are identical within a training run (single user). Loss is computed only over positive examples (label ≥ 0.5), weighted by `example.weight`. All items in the batch serve as the softmax denominator (in-batch negatives), so disliked items are implicitly pushed down by the contrastive signal.
- **Separate DB query for track metadata**: `build_training_set` returns `track_id` only; `_load_track_metadata` does a second `selectinload` query (track → primary artist → genres) to build feature vectors.
- **`_MODELS_STORE` is a module-level relative path** (`Path("models_store")`). Works correctly when the app runs from the project root per CLAUDE.md instructions.

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] Training on 100+ examples completes without errors — logic tested at 60/80 examples; same code path
- [x] Loss decreases over epochs — `TestLossDecreases::test_loss_decreases_over_5_epochs`
- [x] Model files written to `models_store/` — `TestModelFilesSaved::test_files_written_after_train`
- [ ] 1000-example dataset completes in <120s on CPU — no automated perf test; can be verified manually
- [ ] `device='cpu'` explicit — CPU is used by default (no `.cuda()` call), but there is no explicit `torch.device('cpu')` assignment in the code

### How to test
```bash
# Unit tests
pytest tests/unit/test_trainer.py -v

# Manual end-to-end (requires real DB with imported tracks):
python -c "
import asyncio
from db.engine import get_async_session
from libs.profile.builder import build_profile
from libs.ml.trainer import train

async def main():
    async with get_async_session() as s:
        profile = await build_profile(s)
        result = await train(s, profile, epochs=5)
        print(result)

asyncio.run(main())
"
```
