В таблицу «Задание в производство» (1078) добавлен реквизит-ссылка **«Лидер»** (id 82519, ref → справочник «Лидер» 1132). Этот PR заполняет его при планировании, копируя лидера из позиции заказа.

### Что сделано
- **`loadLeaders()`** — загружает справочник «Лидер» (1132) и строит карту `{ метка(lower) → id }`; вызывается в общей инициализации. Таблица необязательна (нет — карта пуста, поведение прежнее).
- **`resolveLeaderId(label)`** — резолвит метку лидера в id записи справочника. Это нужно, потому что отчёты `positions_list`/`cut_planning` отдают лидера **меткой** («Глобал Принтинг»), а ref-реквизит при записи требует **id записи** целевой таблицы, а не отображаемое имя (`docs/kb/crud.md`).
- Лидер прокинут в раскладку (`lay.leader = group.leader`) и пишется во всех путях создания заданий:
  - **автогенерация** (`runGenerateCuts`) — лидер профиля группировки;
  - **создание под позицию** (`createCutForPosition`) — лидер покрываемой позиции;
  - **записи-продолжения** дробления по дням (`applySplitPlan`) — лидер родительской резки.
- В карты `CUT_REQ` / `CUT_WRITE_LABELS` / `cutReqIds` добавлен `leader`.

body:
## What

Adds an **RPT-Live-style spectator HAND FEED** to the public viewer (`/live/:id`) — one rich card per completed hand — plus a neon-green felt pass. Inspired by RPT Live / FullRing (the closest legally-safe benchmark: reporting offline tournaments, no money movement).

All behind a NEW flag **`FEATURES.liveHandFeed` (default OFF)** → with the flag off the viewer is **byte-identical to today** (the feed hook never mounts, layout unchanged, zero extra reads). **READ-ONLY**: every field derives from already-persisted data — no write-path / RPC / Edge / migration / operator-console change.

## Increments (all in this branch)

- **PR1 — data layer:** pure `handFeedDerive.ts` (pot+BB, board, per-player chip delta abs&BB, winner, revealed/face-down hole cards, tags ALL-IN / BIG POT / HIGH HAND[`evaluate7`] / Eliminated) + read-only `useCompletedHandsFeed` hook (paginated completed-hands query mirroring `HandSelector`, batched `.in()` joins, visibility-aware 13s poll, `loadMore`) + 14 unit tests. Reuses `computePotBreakdown` / `evaluate7` / `toEvalCard`.
- **PR2 — cards:** `HandFeedCard` / `LiveHandFeed` (PokerVN Stitch Dark neon-green, reusing `PokerCard`/`CardBack`/`fmtCompact`), mounted in `LiveHub` as the primary block.
- **PR3 — filter/search:** tag chips + this-table/all-tables toggle + hand#/player search.
- **PR4 — share + deep-link:** `?hand=N` opens that hand in the **existing** replay via an additive controlled-prop chain (`TournamentLiveTracker` → `LiveHub` → `TournamentLiveView.initialReplayHandNumber` → `HandSelector.initialHandNumber`). No new replay logic.
- **PR5 — consolidation:** flag-ON → the live-action ticker sits on top + the hand feed is primary, `LiveStoryFeed` eliminations fold into the cards (RPT-Live layout). Flag-OFF keeps today's layout (reversible).
- **PR6 — neon felt:** additive `LiveFelt` `viewerNeon` prop (dark blue-black + neon-green `--primary` rim/glow instead of burgundy `--poker-felt`), passed only by the spectator viewer under the flag → **operator racetrack / TV / replay stay burgundy, byte-identical**.

## Safety

- Flag OFF ⇒ no behavior change; every shared-component edit is an **optional prop defaulting to current behavior** (`LiveFelt.viewerNeon=false`, `HandSelector.initialHandNumber=null`, `TournamentLiveView.initialReplayHandNumber=null`).
- 🟢 **Hole-card guarantee** (documented in code): `hole_cards` persist only when the operator reveals them at showdown/runout (already face-up at the table); no hidden/RFID source; completed hands only → the viewer never knows more than the table → no leak, no delay. ⚠️ Adding an RFID source later would break this — a delay/policy would then be required.

## Verify

- `tsc -b`: 71-error baseline, **0 new** in touched files (the `TournamentLiveView:283` `ActionLog` error is pre-existing).
- `npm run build`: ✅.
- `vitest viewerHub + handinput + trackerPoker`: 248 pass / 2 fail — both `showdownInput.render` are **pre-existing** text-drift (unrelated; that panel is untouched).

## UAT (owner, flag ON on a preview branch)

Open `/live/:id` for a tournament with completed hands → cards render (pot, BB, board, deltas, 👑, revealed vs face-down); tags/filter/search work; "Xem ván" + `?hand=N` open replay on the right hand; share copies the hand link; felt reads neon-green; mobile tidy. **Flag OFF ⇒ viewer identical to today.**

## Deferred

Structure / Payouts / Photos tabs; editorial commentary + COOLER tag (need a write-path / rules engine).

author: koenvanexem
body:
## Summary
`OrderQuantityBreak.AppsOnPostDerive` asserted that at least one of `FromAmount`/`ThroughAmount` is set, but passed `this.M.OrderValue.ThroughAmount` as the second roletype:

```csharp
… AssertAtLeastOne(this, this.M.OrderQuantityBreak.FromAmount, this.M.OrderValue.ThroughAmount);
```

`OrderQuantityBreak : Object` does **not** extend `OrderValue` and declares its own `ThroughAmount`. The foreign `OrderValue.ThroughAmount` roletype reads as absent on an `OrderQuantityBreak`, so a break with only its own `ThroughAmount` set was wrongly rejected with the "at least one" error. Now asserts on `this.M.OrderQuantityBreak.ThroughAmount`.

## Test
Adds `OrderQuantityBreakTests.GivenOrderQuantityBreakWithOnlyThroughAmount_WhenDeriving_ThenNoAtLeastOneError`: builds a break with only `ThroughAmount` and asserts the "at least one" error is **absent**.

- **RED** on un-fixed code (right reason): `Assert.DoesNotContain() Failure: Filter matched` — the error was present despite `ThroughAmount` being set.
- **GREEN** after the fix. The existing `OnBuildThrowValidationError` (empty break) still passes — its message renders against the concrete type and is unaffected.

author: seonghobae
body:
💡 What: In R/vuongtest.R, cached the original tmpvc matrix inside calcAB() and reused it in calcLambda() instead of using chol2inv(chol(AB1$A)), which mathematically computes the exact same matrix but incurs substantial overhead.
🎯 Why: A <- chol2inv(chol(tmpvc)) computes the inverse of tmpvc. Calling chol2inv(chol(A)) simply re-inverts A back to tmpvc. Double matrix inversion of large positive-definite symmetric matrices represents a redundant O(N^3) operation.
📊 Impact: Speeds up the function notably for models with many parameters by entirely removing a double inversion step. Reduced time in a loop of 100 iterations of simple cfa models from ~8.7s to ~6.2s.
🔬 Measurement: Verified output is mathematically identical and package tests still pass.

author: asrcpq
body:
# Overview

This PR initialized language feature stabilization policy, creates the first basic spec, and updated the implementation.

## Changes

- initialize `docs/spec/`. Add guideline of spec writing and draft of the first spec.
- implement cyclic reference memory leak detection. Though leak is still not recoverable, at least we know it happens.
- implement cyclic reference detection in returned value (in FlowExpr correctly via trait). Previously they exploded memory and went into dead loop.
- add type value `type` and let type() return the instantiated singleton type class, not string. `int()` etc. now are properly constructors, not registered functions.
- rename map->dict and string type name string->str to reduce unnecessary Python inconsistency.
- dict() now takes no argument (empty dict) or dict as argument (shallow copy).

## Note

- Note that flow language could still have major breaking changes to the doc before the release.
- Maybe we need safer (recoverable) cyclic reference solution. Go full GC, or scoped linked-list arena. Need considering because cyclic reference could be very rare in actual reearth-flow use cases so maybe current report-only mechanism is sufficient.
- We should NOT expose FlowExpr Value enum variants directly. A cleaner solution is to wrap it as a private field in a pu struct with getter/setter methods. List/Dict should expose handlers to provide borrow/borrow_mut methods, not exposing the `TrackedGc` instances directly.
- The test `test_cyclic_list_increases_live_alloc` for testing memory leak detection needs to leak memory, the leak is tiny so should be fine.

body:
Finishes the verdict-tuning flag cluster started by #1044. Migrates the four remaining env-only verdict knobs in `services/agent/experiment/verdict.go` to live `agent.json` flags, read via typed getters in `services/agent/flags/flags.go`.

## The four flags (all float)
| env var (removed) | flag | type | preserved default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_VERDICT_EFFECT_THRESHOLD` | `verdict_effect_threshold` | float | `0.5` (`DefaultEffectThreshold`) |
| `AGENT_VERDICT_MIN_RAW_EFFECT` | `verdict_min_raw_effect` | float | `0.02` (`DefaultMinRawEffect`) |
| `AGENT_VERDICT_SD_FLOOR` | `verdict_sd_floor` | float | `1e-4` (`DefaultSDFloor`) |
| `AGENT_VERDICT_ANCHOR_MARGIN` | `verdict_anchor_margin` | float | `0.02` (`DefaultAnchorMargin`) |

## Mirror of the `verdict_min_n` / `verdict_min_pairs` siblings
Same wiring end-to-end as the #1044 siblings:
- Declared in `services/flagd/agent.json` + `ci/agent.json` with the same block shape (3 numeric variants, `defaultVariant: default`).
- Keys/struct fields added to `ExperimentDefaults` + `ExperimentConfig`, read via the **typed float getter** `floatFlag`/`FloatValue` (NEVER `ObjectValue` — the #903/#1127 silent-TYPE_MISMATCH trap).
- Live-mirrored onto the verdict each experiment tick via the registry: `Reconfigure` (min_n/min_pairs) + new `ReconfigureVerdictFloats` → `Verdict.SetThresholds` / new `Verdict.SetFloatThresholds`.

## Fail-open defaults
These are TUNING knobs, so they **fail OPEN** to the verdict's `Default*` constants when flagd is undefined/unreachable — matching the min_n/min_pairs siblings. The env consts + `floatFromEnv` reader are removed; the constants are now the fail-open fallback the flags resolve to. The four floats are snapshotted under `v.mu` in `Evaluate` and passed to `evaluatePaired` / `applyRecentRealAnchor`, so a hot-reload is honored between evaluations while a single evaluation sees one coherent threshold set. author: xuzhougeng
body:
## What

On macOS the in-app keybinds were migrated from Ctrl to Cmd in `82e7a60`, but the NSMenu in `menu_macos.zig` kept a **separate hardcoded copy** of the shortcuts on Ctrl. This fixes that drift, plus refines the macOS copy binding.

- Edit ▸ **Paste Image** showed `⌃⇧V` while the real binding is `⌘⇧V` (likewise Copy/Paste and the rest of the menu).
- Worse: an NSMenu key equivalent is intercepted by AppKit **before** the terminal sees the keystroke, so the stale `⌃V` / `⌃⇧V` equivalents **hijacked Ctrl+V / Ctrl+Shift+V** (literal-next and friends) as Paste / Paste Image — breaking them in vim/readline.

## Changes

**1. Align the NSMenu shortcuts with the keybinds** (`menu_macos.zig`)
- Every menu item moves `ModCtrl → ModCmd`, mirroring `keybind.Set.defaults()`. Tab switching (`Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab`) intentionally stays on Ctrl to match the keybinds and avoid the system app switcher.

**2. Copy = Cmd+C only on macOS** (`keybind.zig`, `menu_macos.zig`)
- Windows/Linux keep `Ctrl+Shift+C` because `Ctrl+C` is the terminal's SIGINT. macOS has no such conflict, so copy now binds to the single conventional `Cmd+C` (the migrated `Cmd+Shift+C` is dropped). The Edit ▸ Copy menu shows `⌘C`.

**3. Tests** (`test_macos_menu.zig`, `keybind.zig`)
- Fixed two menu tests that asserted the stale `⌃` values.
- Added a **drift-guard test** pinning every action item's modifiers to `keybind.Set.defaults()`, so the menu and the keybind table can never silently diverge again.
- Added a keybind test pinning the per-platform copy default (`Cmd+C` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+C` elsewhere).

## Notes

- The original report was "Edit ▸ Paste Image does nothing." On current `main` this does **not** reproduce — thread-aware instrumentation showed the menu click fires `paste_image` on the main thread, reads the clipboard image, and pastes the file path successfully (`pasteSavedClipboardImage ok=true`); the menu item is `enabled=true`. The observable defect was the wrong/hijacking shortcuts, which this PR fixes.
- The startup-shortcuts cheat-sheet overlay was checked and needs **no change**: it derives `.action`/`.pair`/`.quad` entries live from `g_keybinds` via `formatTrigger` (Cmd on macOS), so it already reflects the Cmd bindings, including the new `Cmd+C`.

## Verification

- Live macOS app, decoded via Accessibility: Edit now shows `⌘C` / `⌘V` / `⌘⇧V`; whole menu on Cmd; Tab still `⌃Tab` / `⌃⇧Tab`; menu-click paste still works.
- `zig build test-macos-menu` ✓ · `zig build test-macos-services` ✓ · `zig build test` (fast) ✓ · `zig build test-full` (native regression) ✓

author: meroton-benjamin
body:
This commit builds on top of our split and splice blob support to make
it a mandatory first class feature in Buildbarn. With this commit the
Content Addressable Storage (CAS) is created from two Storage
configurations that work in tandem. A Chunk Storage (CS) which is
content addressed and contains chunks of blobs, and a Chunk List Storage
(CLS) which is addressed by a blob digest and contains a manifest
describing the chunks that make up the blob.

All api calls are automatically translated to use Chunk Lists created
with RepMaxCDC. Effectively this means that large blobs no longer exists
in the storage layer, individual chunks of the large blobs are in turn
deduplicated in such a manner that the chunks are stored only once.

The automatic translation makes certain that clients that are not cdc
aware can still continue to use the storage backend without performing
any changes. Clients which support RepMaxCDC also gets a significant
reduction in the amount of blobs to transfer as they only need to
transfer modified chunks rather than the entire blob.

author: taotao-real
body:
Summary
- Detect local-memory physical alias when two different `pto.alloc_tile` roots carry known constant address ranges that overlap.
- Keep address-unknown / dynamic cases on the existing root-based fallback path, so this does not turn all root-different unknown buffers into may-alias and does not broadly increase redundant sync.
- Add issue #844 regressions for the missing `PIPE_MTE3 -> PIPE_V` WAR sync and for the disjoint-address no-extra-sync case.

Motivation
- Fixes #844.
- PyPTO MemoryReuse can share storage for logical tiles whose sequential IR lifetimes do not overlap, then emit distinct `pto.alloc_tile` roots with the same or overlapping physical `addr`.
- PTOAS InsertSync previously treated different `rootBuffer`s as non-alias unless they shared a view/root chain, so it could miss WAR/WAW dependencies introduced by physical local-memory reuse.

Design
- `PTOIRTranslator::UpdateAllocTileOpMemInfo` now records `baseAddresses` only when `alloc_tile addr` is a constant. Missing or non-static addresses remain unknown instead of being recorded as address 0.
- `MemoryDependentAnalyzer::MemAlias` now gives local physical ranges priority when both sides have known address and size: overlap means alias, disjoint means no-alias, regardless of different logical roots.
- GM aliasing and unknown-address fallback behavior are intentionally unchanged.

Concern / Future Alignment
- If PTOAS treated every root-different + address-unknown case as may-alias, InsertSync would likely add a large number of redundant syncs.
- For future dynamic-address reuse, PyPTO should pass storage identity metadata such as `storageId` / `reuseGroup` to identify logical tiles sharing one physical storage object.
- PTOAS should then evolve from a root-only model to a unified model of `logical root + physical range + storage identity`, using symbolic range analysis only inside the same storage group.
- This keeps correctness for dynamic reuse without making unrelated unknown-address buffers all alias each other.

Testing
- `git diff --check`
- `ninja -C build-codex lib/PTO/Transforms/CMakeFiles/obj.PTOTransforms.dir/InsertSync/PTOIRTranslator.cpp.o lib/PTO/Transforms/CMakeFiles/obj.PTOTransforms.dir/InsertSync/MemoryDependentAnalyzer.cpp.o`
- `ptoas --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync --pto-insert-sync-debug=2 test/lit/pto/issue844_local_physical_reuse_sync.pto -o - | FileCheck test/lit/pto/issue844_local_physical_reuse_sync.pto`
- `ptoas --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync --pto-insert-sync-debug=2 test/lit/pto/issue844_local_physical_disjoint_no_sync.pto -o - | FileCheck test/lit/pto/issue844_local_physical_disjoint_no_sync.pto`

Local build note
- Full `ninja -C build-codex ptoas` is blocked in this local checkout by pre-existing LLVM API mismatches unrelated to this patch (`Type::isFloat8*` calls and other current main/LLVM21 compatibility issues). The touched InsertSync objects compile successfully.

author: brelian
body:
## Summary

The initial Dependabot run from #198 produced a flood of 17+ PRs (#199–#216), most of them non-security version bumps that nobody asked for. All have been bulk-closed. This PR tightens `dependabot.yml` so future runs stay quiet.

## Changes

- **Group all updates per ecosystem into a single PR/week** — instead of one PR per dependency
- **Ignore all major version bumps** — they routinely break things and need manual review (e.g. the closed #213 wanted `actions/checkout v4 → v7`, #215 wanted `@types/node v20 → v26`)
- **Drop `open-pull-requests-limit`** from 10/5/5 to 3/2/2

## What this does NOT block

Security PRs from Dependabot bypass both the per-week limit and the `ignore` rules. So CVE fixes still arrive promptly — only routine version bumps are throttled.

## Expected weekly volume

| Ecosystem | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm | 13 PRs on first run | 1 grouped PR/week max |
| github-actions | 4 PRs on first run | 1 grouped PR/week max |
| pip | 0 (no pip deps changed yet) | 1 grouped PR/week max |

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/dependabot.yml'))"` parses clean

body:
### Motivation

- Add a new neuron type that mixes standard leaky LIF dynamics with a configurable fraction of autonomous (non-leaky) neurons to explore heterogeneous intrinsic drives and autonomous spiking behavior.
- Expose the new neuron via the command-line interface and provide reproducible default training commands for all supported datasets.
- Document the HALIF usage and tunable parameters so experiments can be reproduced and tuned consistently.

### Description

- Implemented `HALIFNeuron` in `modules/neuron.py` which supports a fixed `auto_ratio` of autonomous neuron positions, grouped heterogeneous intrinsic drives, deterministic mask seeding, hard-reset for autonomous neurons, and ASN/success-modulation integration; also added `List` to typing imports.
- Integrated HALIF into `train.py` by adding `HALIF` to the `-neuron_model` help text, registering HALIF-specific CLI args (`-halif_auto_ratio`, `-halif_num_auto_groups`, `-halif_drive_periods`, `-halif_auto_drive_values`, `-halif_v_reset`, `-halif_auto_T`, `-halif_auto_seed`), mapping the `HALIF` selection to `neuron.HALIFNeuron`, propagating the HALIF settings into `neuron_kwargs`, and including HALIF metadata in the run name components.
- Updated documentation in `README.md` to list `HALIF` in the available neuron models and added an example command, and expanded `neuron_training_commands_by_dataset.txt` with HALIF-specific descriptions and ready-to-run training commands across datasets.

### Testing

- Performed a lightweight automated smoke test by importing and instantiating the neuron and running a single forward step with a dummy tensor using `python -c "import torch; from modules import neuron; n=neuron.HALIFNeuron(); x=torch.zeros(1,4,4,16); n.reset_state(); print(n(x).shape)"`, which completed without error.
- No new unit tests were added to the test suite in this change.

body:
## Fixes the PHP 8.3 CI cell (red on main since 2026-06-21)

`main` has been failing `PHPUnit (PHP 8.3)` since the `track composer.lock` commit (`d8b6b676`): the tracked lock was resolved under PHP 8.5, so `composer install` on the 8.3 matrix cell hit `symfony/* v8.1` (php >=8.4.1) + `spatie/laravel-activitylog 5.0` (php ^8.4) → **"lock file does not contain a compatible set of packages"**.

### Root cause
Nothing in the tree actually needs PHP 8.4+: `laravel/framework 13.16.1` accepts `symfony/console ^7.4.0 || ^8.0.0`, and `laravel/ai 0.8.1` + every padosoft package require only `php: ^8.3`. The lock simply over-resolved on a newer local PHP.

### Fix (durable)
Pin `config.platform.php = "8.3.0"` (the declared floor) so **every** `composer update` — any dev, any local PHP — resolves for 8.3. Regenerated: symfony → **7.4.x**, activitylog → 4.12.x. An 8.3/8.4/8.5-installable lock. `laravel/ai` stays **v0.8.1**; guardrails 1.2.0 / regolo 1.2.1 / finops 1.4.0 unchanged.

### Verification
Full local suite green on the 8.3-resolved lock: **2989 tests, 11166 assertions, 0 failures**. CI must now show `PHPUnit (PHP 8.3)` green.

author: yumi-alt
body:
## FIXES

**Do not delete the branche please !**

## Description

Implementation of the elevation (incantation) coordination system for the Zappy AI, enabling bots to reach level 4. This PR introduces the leader/follower logic via broadcast, navigation toward gathering tiles, and incantation triggering once all conditions are met.

### How

- Added `elevation.py` containing the `Elevation` class, which drives the incantation state machine (candidate → leader, follower → navigation → incantation)
- A bot that has collected all required stones declares itself a **candidate** via `become_candidate()`, waits a few ticks, then becomes **leader**
- The leader broadcasts an `INCANT` message encoded with its level, the number of missing players, and its position
- Followers receive the `INCANT` broadcast, navigate to the leader's position via `navigate()`, drop their stones, and send a `JOIN`
- The leader listens for `JOIN` messages and, once the quorum is reached, checks the tile via `Look` then triggers `Incantation`
- On success (`Current level` in the response), levels and inventories are updated; on failure, stones are picked back up
- A `DONE` broadcast is sent at the end to release the followers
- Added `compute_max_wait()` to compute a dynamic timeout based on map size and the number of players required
- Integrated into `comportement.py`: the `ELEVATING` status triggers `elevation.update()` every tick
- Refactored `parser/args.py`: replaced `argparse.Namespace` with a `ZappyArgs` dataclass supporting multiple team names (`-n name1 name2 ...`)
- Refactored `main.py`: spawns one process per team via `Process` and `ZappyAI.launch_bot`
- Added network modules: `socket.py` (ClientSocket with buffer and select), `zappyClient.py` (in-flight command management, async event parsing), `broadcast.py` (encode/decode for INCANT/JOIN/POS/RESOURCE/DONE messages)

### Testing
1. **Execution**:
   ```bash
   ./binaries/zappy_server -p 4242 -x 10 -y 10 -n TEST -c 5 -f 100
   uv run src/main.py -p 4242 -n TEST
   ```
2. **Validation**:
   - Verify that bots reach level 2 → 3 → 4 without getting stuck indefinitely
   - Verify that stones are properly removed from the tile after a successful incantation
   - Verify that on incantation failure, bots pick their stones back up and resume collecting

### Notes
- **Next**: Support levels 5 to 8 (same logic — `PLAYERS_REQUIRED` and `ELEVATION_REQUIREMENTS` constants already cover up to level 8)
- **Technical Details**: Leadership conflict resolution is based on position comparison `candidate_pos < player.position` — simple but effective to prevent two leaders at the same level in the same area
- **Refactoring**: None

## Summary

- Replace manual `lastIndexOf('.')` + regex-split (`/[\\/]/`) in `mimeUtils.ts::getExtension` with `node:path.extname()` and a simple `replaceAll('\\', '/')` normalize step
- Eliminate the regex `/[\\/]/` test for path-separator detection in favour of `normalized.includes('/')`
- Add a JSDoc comment to `getExtension` describing the three accepted input forms

## Why

A codebase-wide scan surfaced this as the one place where extension extraction was done manually instead of via the already-available `path.extname()`. The rest of the codebase (e.g. `pathCore.ts::getExtensionLowercase`) consistently delegates to `path.extname()`; this brings `mimeUtils` in line.

The refactor preserves all three input forms the function intentionally handles:
| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Full path `/tmp/clip.opus` | `.opus` |
| Dotfile `.mulaw` | `.mulaw` |
| Bare extension `opus` | `.opus` |
| Extensionless path `/tmp/opus` | `''` |

author: extratoast
body:
## What

Folds the browser-driven credential login into the existing agents-ui site (`agents.jorisjonkers.dev`) instead of a separate SSO host, and trims the service down to the privileged worker.

## Why

The first cut shipped a whole separate public surface — its own `agents-login.jorisjonkers.dev` host, a dedicated `AGENTS_LOGIN` permission, a MyApps card, and a standalone controller UI server. That is overbuilt: the login is just another authenticated page on the agents site, which is already behind the `AGENTS` forward-auth gate. The browser UI and its CSRF/forward-auth handling belong in agents-ui / agents-api; only the part that must run the CLIs over a PTY and write Vault needs to be its own process.

## Change

Removed:
- the public `agents-login` host in `fleet.yaml` and its rendered IngressRoute / edge-catalog / Gatus entries;
- the `AGENTS_LOGIN` `ServicePermission` (auth-api) and its tests;
- the app-ui MyApps card and placeholder icon;
- the standalone **controller** — its `Deployment`/`Service`, its `NetworkPolicy`, and the `src/controller/` code (UI server, CSRF, worker client) plus the controller-only tests.

Kept and retargeted:
- the Vault schema + `agents-oauth-writer` RBAC and the VSO projections (unchanged);
- the **worker** as an internal ClusterIP service in `agents-system`. Its `NetworkPolicy` now admits ingress from the `agents-api` pods (which proxy the browser flow) instead of the deleted controller; the image is trimmed to a single worker entrypoint (`config.ts`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-entrypoint.sh`, README, and `config.test.ts` follow).

## Verification

- `services/agents-login`: `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` clean — 66 tests, 91.2% line / 82.9% branch coverage.
- All five render scripts run and leave no `agents-login` host in the rendered edge/Gatus output; `kubectl kustomize` builds the production overlay; `fleet.yaml` has no `agents-login` references.
- auth-api and app-ui changes are clean reverts of the permission/card commits.

The agents-ui **Credentials** page and the agents-api proxy to the worker land in a companion PR in the agents repo.

## Summary

Split `hashicorp/go-msgpack` into two packages, one per major version
(following the existing `go-gopkg-yaml.v2`/`.v3`/`.v4` convention, as agreed
with @misaka00251):

- **Rename** the existing `go-github-hashicorp-go-msgpack` (which builds the
  v2.x release, module `github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack/v2`) to
  `go-github-hashicorp-go-msgpack-v2`. Its `go_import_path` was the root path
  while the source is the `/v2` module, so the built RPM provided **no usable
  `go(...)` path at all** (only the bare RPM name); this fixes it to
  `github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack/v2` so it provides
  `go(github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack/v2)`. Also adds the missing
  `#!RemoteAsset` sha256 and switches `%{?autochangelog}` → `%autochangelog`.
- **Add** a new `go-github-hashicorp-go-msgpack` packaging the **v0.5.x**
  release at the root import path `github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack`, required
  by `hashicorp/memberlist`, `serf` and `consul` (they import
  `.../go-msgpack/codec` at the root path). vet is disabled and the old test
  suite's flag incompatibility is tolerated, with rationale comments.

No existing package in main referenced `go(github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack...)`,

## Purpose
This pull request refactors how the Promote Agent drawer initializes and manages environment configuration state, improving the user experience by ensuring that in-progress edits are preserved and that the editor is pre-filled with the correct environment's configuration. The main changes are focused on state management and data fetching logic.

**Improvements to configuration pre-filling and state management:**

* The drawer now fetches and pre-fills the editor with the existing configuration of the selected target environment, rather than always starting with a blank or source environment configuration. This ensures users edit from the current state of the target environment.
* The logic tracks which target environment has been pre-filled to avoid overwriting user edits during background refetches, only re-filling when the user switches to a different target environment.
* The previous logic that fetched the source environment configuration and initialized form state on drawer open has been removed, simplifying state handling and reducing unnecessary data fetching. author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary

Harden the CSS emitted when `hide_cursor` is enabled so the mouse cursor reliably disappears across browsers and elements.

## Why this matters

In #784 a user reports the mouse cursor stays visible in the upper-left of the kiosk display even with `hide_cursor` enabled. The on-main implementation in `internal/templates/partials/head.templ:31` emitted only `* { cursor: none !important; }`. That single rule can be defeated when an element re-asserts a cursor through a pseudo-element or on hover, and some engines do not treat `html`/`body` as covered by the universal selector in every case.

This change extends the existing `if viewData.HideCursor` style block to also target `html`, `body`, `*::before`, `*::after`, and `*:hover`, all with `cursor: none !important;`. It stays CSS-only and inside the existing guard, matching the direction of the `robust-cursor` development image already prototyped for this issue. No Go logic, config, or template-data changes.

## Testing

- `templ generate` regenerates the partial cleanly and the generated CSS contains the new selectors.
- `go vet ./internal/templates/partials/`
- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./internal/templates/partials/`

Fixes #784

author: sorawit-w
body:
## Why

`pixel-art` is the obvious name-match for "pixel art," so it gets invoked for **composed/branded SVG-asset jobs** (banners, icon sets, exact-text layouts) it cannot do — and instead of saying so, it **silently generated a raster** and presented it as the deliverable. It also wrote outputs to a repo path (`docs/pixel-art/`), gated generation on a fixed list of **named** MCP servers (host-native generators invisible), and shipped pseudo-pixel-art (tens of thousands of colors, no real grid). This reworks all four.

Scoped from a brief + a `team-composer` workshop; five review findings folded in. Single PR (the brief's two-PR split was collapsed to dissolve a sequencing honesty-gap).

## What changed

- **Honest decline (no silent substitution).** New **Phase 0 deliverable-type gate**: a brief needing exact rendered text, an exact layout/viewBox, brand tokens, an editable vector source, or a multi-asset set is a composition job the skill does not do — it states the mismatch and **stops**, rather than down-converting to a raster or naming a substitute tool. **Title cards** and **single-sprite-SVG** are explicit carve-outs.
- **Repo-agnostic.** Writes nothing to disk; **returns** every artifact to the caller. Purged all `docs/pixel-art/` saves across SKILL.md, README, and the prompt-brief template (`grep` = 0 hits).
- **Attempt-then-fallback capability detection.** Routes on *"can I generate at all?"* (host-native or MCP) and **attempts** generation, instead of *"is named server X connected?"*. Vendor list + per-vendor density-ceiling table demoted to optional phrasing nudges.
- **Deterministic quantize.** New `scripts/quantize.py` (Pillow, **median-cut** — not k-means, which would break determinism) downscales to a real grid + clamps the palette → true grid-aligned pixel art, PNG or single-sprite SVG. `scripts/test_quantize.py` asserts three invariants.
- **Identity / BETA removal.** Sharpened `description` so composed/branded asset requests don't trigger; removed BETA/v0.1 from SKILL.md, both READMEs, and the skill-graph node. Eval fixture updated with honeypot neighbor-steal cases.

## Versioning

`5.4.0 → 5.5.0` — **MINOR** despite the breaking behavior change (triggering + output contract), because the skill was draft/BETA with no real dependents. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

> **Note:** introduces the repo's **first external Python dependency** (Pillow, declared skill-locally in `scripts/requirements.txt`). Prior Python scripts are stdlib-only.

## Verification

- ✅ `python3 skills/pixel-art/scripts/test_quantize.py` — 3 invariants pass (grid-aligned + ≤palette colors; PNG ≡ SVG grid; byte-identical across runs)
- ✅ `python3 scripts/check-skill-compat.py` — exit 0; version parity at 5.5.0; description 1001 chars (warn-only soft cap)
- ✅ `grep -rn docs/pixel-art skills/pixel-art/` — zero hits
- ✅ In-session `skill-evaluator` — **29/29 gradable assertions** (split-role, graders never saw the skill text). Phase 0 decline gate, both carve-outs, attempt-then-fallback, and repo-agnostic-under-save-pressure all held.

### Known coverage gap
The Path B **genuine-absence** branch is under-tested: the skill-evaluator executor sub-agent had a live image-gen MCP in its runtime, so it correctly gated on *actual* capability and generated rather than simulating absence. A worktree-isolated executor (MCPs stripped) would close this. Not a skill bug — the skill behaved as designed.

### Recommended before merge
A **separate-session** `skill-evaluator` run for outer-bias insulation (this PR's author wrote the code, the fixtures, and read the verdicts).

author: im007
body:
## What
Claude Code's Bash tool rebuilds the shell from a snapshot that captures zoxide's functions but **not** its `chpwd_functions`/`precmd_functions` hook registration. zoxide's doctor warns precisely when that hook is unregistered, so it false-positives on every `cd` inside Claude. This is a different failure mode from the $PATH-after-init case the existing positioning logic handles, and position-fixing cannot cure it.

## Change
- Add a `$CLAUDECODE`-gated `export _ZO_DOCTOR=0` **before** the zoxide init block. Claude-only, so the (useful) interactive doctor is preserved; inert on machines without Claude Code.
- Placed ahead of the positioning block so a freshly-appended guard gets repositioned behind the must-be-last init in the **same run** (upgrade machines self-correct in one pass).
- New `tests/test_zo_doctor_guard.sh` mirroring `test_zoxide_init.sh`.

## Verification
- New guard test: 7/7. Existing `test_zoxide_init.sh`: 23/23 (unchanged). `bash -n` clean.
- Combined-flow check: fresh / upgrade / idempotent-rerun all end with `zoxide init` last + exactly one guard line.

body:
I følge XSD-en er `<Prioritet>` definert som `<xs:element minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1" name="Prioritet" type="ArrayOfPrioritetsAngivelse">`. Altså skal det være maksimalt ett Prioritet-element, som inneholder et eller flere PrioritetsAngivelse-elementer, ikke et separat Prioritet-element for hver prioritetsangivelse.

Det hadde vært kjekt å ha CI som gjorde basic validering av eksemplene opp mot XSD-en…

I tillegg slang jeg på `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="./afpant-forutsetningsbrev.xsd"` i eksemplene, så IDE-er som støtter det faktisk validerer dem mot skjemaet. Dette førte til at jeg oppdaget at `<BeloepGjelder>` er spesifisert i begge eksemplene, til tross for at det ikke er i skjemaet (jfr. #108).

/cc @javaguruen

body:
## Why

The public robustness narrative made empirical claims with no recomputable evidence committed in the public repo: concurrency/soak ("8 threads", "zero crashes, zero errors", "no net memory growth"), cross-locale "identical bytecode", and a "committed adversarial corpus". Determinism is the only robustness claim with public recomputable proof. This is a **docs-only** honesty alignment — same principle as the prior honest-claims pass — not a product change.

## Changes (README.md, site/index.html)

- **Concurrency** — removed "zero crashes, zero errors", "no net memory growth", and the hardcoded thread count. Now states the per-thread compiler model and that concurrent + soak execution is exercised every release in CI under ASan/UBSan. The `AX_ERR_CONCURRENT_COMPILER_USE` runtime guarantee is **retained**.
- **Locale** — replaced "identical bytecode across OS locales (C, Turkish, German, French, …)" with the DET-002 locale-independence contract + CI-exercised cross-locale equivalence. (Site heading: "Identical Bytecode Across Locales" → "Locale Independence".)
- **Fuzzing corpus** — reworded "committed adversarial corpus" → "adversarial corpus (maintained in the engine repository)", and dropped the specific "integer overflow in priority parsing" anecdote in favor of generic "caught and fixed bugs before release".

## Verification

**Corpus location:** NOT public — no `corpus`/`fuzz`/`seed` directories or files exist anywhere in this repo. → reworded to "maintained in the engine repository".

**Anecdote:** Cannot confirm — this is the SDK/docs repo (no engine source in history); the only commit mentioning "priority" is an unrelated docs commit. No "integer overflow in priority parsing" determinism-bug fix found. → specific detail dropped.

**Grep sweep (zero remaining hits):**
- `no net memory growth` → none
- `zero crashes` / `zero errors` → none
- `committed adversarial corpus` → none
- hardcoded `N threads` (md/html) → none
- `integer overflow` / `priority integer overflow` (md/html) → none
- `AX_ERR_CONCURRENT_COMPILER_USE` → retained in README.md & site/index.html

README/site are not in the contract-gate set, so no "Contract change: YES" marker. CI gates (contract-gate, evidence-sanity, public-surface, verify-canonical) are unaffected by docs.

author: amitgangrade
body:
## What

Fresh full-suite run (59 pairs, 59/59 byte-identical) on current `main`, which now includes: P0 (#20), GC-during-JIT (#21) + its O(n²) fix (#23), strings round 2 + dict-hash + struct-writer (#18), and P1 closure/tuple JIT (#22). Refreshes `REPORT_V2.md` with a new "Current standing" section at the top (prior milestone sections kept for provenance), regenerates `REPORT_V2_tables.md`, and saves `results_v2_main_postfix.json`.

## Headline

| | run-3 (prev published) | current `main` |
|---|---|---|
| **Geomean speedup (all 59)** | 0.96× | **1.28× — net faster than CPython** |
| Wins / ties / losses | 26 / 0 / 33 | **28 / 4 / 27** |
| Core | 4.72× | 4.87× |
| Systems | 1.39× | **1.80×** |
| Data structures | 0.58× | **0.69×** |
| Strings | 0.31× | **0.59×** |

First run where the whole-suite geometric mean is **above 1.0×**. `ds_class_alloc` recovered from the #21 regression (135× → 0.71×, faster than CPython); large string-track gains (`str_http_parse` 12.5×→3.0×, `str_fstring_format` 8.2×→2.8×, `sys_struct_pack` 4.2×→2.1×, …).

## Remaining slow spots (future work)

`ds_dict_ops` 4.0× (key `str()` construction), `sys_file_io` 3.8× (no buffered IO), `ds_set_ops` 3.3× (dict-emulated), the string-formatting cluster (~2.5–3.3×), and the P2/P3/P4 targets (`ds_closures_hof`/`ds_sort_by_key`, `ds_exceptions`, `ds_nullable`). `ds_generics` is already ~parity now.

Docs/data only — no code changes.

author: srjn45
body:
## Summary

Implements the [worktree-GC & lifecycle hardening design](https://github.com/srjn45/warden/pull/14) — garbage collection of orphaned git worktrees and the provenance/guard hardening around it. Built as a 4-stage pipeline; this is the cumulative result, rebased clean onto current `main`.

Closes the four gaps from the spec:

1. **Orphaned-worktree leak** — new `warden prune` reconciles `git worktree list --porcelain` (filtered to `.worktrees/*`) against active + archived records, removing orphans under the same dirty/unpushed guard. `--dry-run` (plan is byte-identical to the real run), `--force`, `--include-archived`. Plus read-only `warden worktree ls`.
2. **Stale admin metadata** — `git worktree prune` now runs after `RemoveWorktree` and at the end of a real prune sweep.
3. **pr-review branch leak** — detached pr-review captures the `gh`-created branch (`rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`) so cleanup deletes it; falls back to `Branch=""` (prune sweeps) on error.
4. **created-vs-adopted not persisted** — `Session.WorktreeCreated` / `BranchCreated` persisted; `RemoveWorktree` only `branch -D`s a branch warden created (adopted branches safe even under `--force`; explicit `--delete-adopted-branch` escape hatch). One-shot migration backfills legacy records (`Branch==ID` heuristic, sentinel-guarded).

Companion: `worktree_keep_done` / `worktree_auto_prune` config (mirrors `pipeline_keep_done`). `keep_done=false` removes a clean worktree on archive; `auto_prune=true` runs an hourly + startup sweep that **never** touches archived-owned worktrees and never forces past the guard.

## Stats

26 files, +1770/−61. New: `internal/lifecycle/prune.go`, `internal/daemon/worktree_prune.go`, `internal/cli/worktree.go`, plus tests (`prune_test.go`, `provenance_test.go`, `worktree_prune_test.go`).

## Verification (CI Go 1.26.2)

- `gofmt -l` clean · `go vet ./...` pass · `go build ./...` pass
- `go test -race ./...` — all 18 packages pass

## Notes for review

- The archived-owned protection invariant in the auto-prune sweep (`IncludeArchived=false`, `Force=false`) is the key safety property — guards the gitignored-files blind spot called out in the spec.
- Migration backfill (`backfillProvenance` + `.provenance-migrated` sentinel in `internal/store/file.go`) is implemented despite intermediate stage handoffs reporting it unbuilt — worth a confirming look.
- Worth scrutiny: the prune guard/ownership classification and default-branch protection in `internal/lifecycle/prune.go`.

## Summary

Scaffolds Steam Workshop distribution via MegaCrit's official [`sts2-mod-uploader`](https://github.com/megacrit/sts2-mod-uploader), per #13. **No mod source changes** — this wraps the existing build + manual-install flow in an uploader *workspace* + script.

- `dist/workshop/workshop.json` — title/description (notes `source_hooks` ships off by default), `visibility: private`, empty `tags` (avoids the reserved `tool` tag), no deps

- `scripts/package-workshop.sh` — builds Release, stages `content/` (DLL + `STS2_DamageCharts.json`), then runs or prints the `ModUploader` command
- `.gitignore` `dist/workshop/content/` (build output) + `tools/` (CLI binary); workspace config + future `mod_id.txt` stay tracked
- `mod_manifest.json` author → `zaxnyd`
- README **Steam Workshop** section (players: subscribe; maintainers: publish flow) + `CLAUDE.md` pointer
- Commits the existing `docs/examples/` screenshots (referenced by docs, reused for the preview)

## Verification

- `scripts/package-workshop.sh` runs clean: builds (0 warnings/errors), stages `content/` with `STS2_DamageCharts.dll` + `STS2_DamageCharts.json`, prints the upload command when the CLI isn't present
- `image.png` is exactly 512×512; `workshop.json` + `mod_manifest.json` are valid JSON
- `dist/workshop/content/` is git-ignored; only `workshop.json` + `image.png` are tracked under `dist/`

## Left to maintainer (needs Steam client logged in — not CI)

1. Download `ModUploader` (osx-arm64) → `./tools/ModUploader`
2. Run the script for the first **private** publish → commit the auto-written `dist/workshop/mod_id.txt`

author: claude-murgat
body:
## Contexte

Le 2026-06-22 le cluster Patroni est tombé en entier (plus de leader, alarme
incapable de sonner) : du WAL a saturé les disques de **node1** (207 Go → 100 %)
et **node3** (cloud, 100 %), PostgreSQL ne redémarrait plus. Surtout, la panne est
restée **silencieuse 2,5 jours** — *rien* ne surveillait le remplissage disque. On
a plafonné la rétention WAL (`max_slot_wal_keep_size=8GB`), mais il manquait toujours
une **alerte précoce** si un disque se remplit pour n'importe quelle raison.

## Ce que fait cette PR

Sonde disque légère, sans dépendance, déployée sur les **3 nœuds** :

- **`scripts/disk-check.sh`** — `df` sur `/` et `/var/lib/docker`, seuils **WARN 85 %**
  / **CRIT 92 %**, **1 email par épisode** + re-notif au plus toutes les 6 h + email de
  retour à la normale. Dédoublonnage par device (si `/var/lib/docker` est sur le même fs
  que `/`, une seule alerte). État dans `/var/lib/alarm/disk-check/`.
- **`scripts/send-alert-email.py`** — helper SMTP réutilisable qui emprunte **exactement
  la même voie d'envoi et les mêmes secrets** que le watchdog modem
  (`/opt/alarm/.env.prod.*`, STARTTLS + login). stdlib only. Le glob des `.env.prod.*` le
  rend portable sur **node3** (cloud, sans stack modem).
- **`systemd/alarm-disk-check.{service,timer}`** — oneshot + timer **15 min**.
- **`install.sh`** — copie les 2 scripts, pose/active les units. Le timer est `enable --now`
  (sonde read-only sans risque ; ne pas la démarrer reproduirait la classe de bug de
  l'incident). Tourne aussi sur node3 (les warnings modem y sont bénins).
- **`README.md`** — entrée tableau + section « Supervision disque ».

Surchargeable par env : `DISK_WARN_PCENT`, `DISK_CRIT_PCENT`, `DISK_CHECK_PATHS`, `DISK_RENOTIFY_HOURS`.

## ⚠️ Revue manuelle requise

`infra/**` — **pas d'auto-merge** (pas de label `ai:review`). À relire/merger à la main.
Aucune config live n'a été touchée ; rien n'a été exécuté contre la prod.

- [x] `disk-check.sh --dry-run` (parse `df`, niveaux OK, dédoublonnage `/` + `/var/lib/docker` vérifié)

- [x] Recovery (retour normale) + `--test-email` + usage du helper

body:
## What

Closes the **supply-chain release integrity** gap (std-supplychain / workflow-cicd) — the one outright "definition of done" mandate that was missing.

- **CI `supply-chain` job** (runs on every PR/push): generates a **CycloneDX SBOM** (`anchore/sbom-action`) and runs a **Trivy** filesystem **vuln + misconfig** scan, **merge-blocking on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL** (`ignore-unfixed: true` to avoid blocking on unpatchable base-image noise).
- **`release.yml`** (tag-triggered, `tenantforge-v*`): builds the artifact once, packs the tarball, attests **non-falsifiable SLSA build provenance** (`actions/attest-build-provenance`, **keyless via OIDC** — no stored signing keys), and publishes a GitHub Release with the tarball + SBOM attached. Verify with `gh attestation verify <tarball> --repo <repo>`.
- All third-party actions **pinned by commit SHA** (repo convention); least-privilege per-job permissions.

## Scope note (container deferred)

A hardened + scanned + signed **container image** is intentionally deferred: it needs a registry + deploy-target decision, and a correct pnpm-workspace multi-stage Dockerfile can't be validated locally here. The SBOM + provenance + vuln-scan core of the mandate ships now, GitHub-native (no external registry/secrets). Documented in README + CHANGELOG.

## Validation

Both workflow YAMLs parse cleanly; actions resolved to current commit SHAs. The new `supply-chain` CI job is exercised **on this PR**, so the SBOM generation + Trivy scan are validated for real before merge. No source changes — existing gates (lint/tsc/version/tests/coverage/CodeQL/secret-scan) unaffected. The `release` workflow fires on the next `tenantforge-v*` tag.

author: waterrrforever
body:
## What

Two independent source-layer changes that came out of the skills/capture work:

1. **`fix(core)`** — standalone sub-composition previews that rendered blank/black now render correctly. Three distinct failure modes in `buildSubCompositionHtml`, all of which only surface in a *standalone* preview (a full composition masks them via its mounting host).
2. **`feat(cli)`** — `generateAssetDescriptions` now surfaces captured **video clips** in the asset description list, tagged `[video]`.

## Why

### Standalone sub-composition previews

A full composition mounts each sub-composition under a `data-composition-src` host that supplies its size, background, and composition-id binding. A **standalone** preview has no such host, so any of the following silently produces a blank/black frame:

1. **Digit-leading `#id` CSS selectors.** A CSS identifier cannot start with a digit, so an authored rule like `#01-wall-pushes-back { width: 1920px; height: 1080px; background: … }` is an *invalid* selector and the browser drops the **whole rule** — taking the root's size and background with it. In a full composition the host paints/sizes the frame so the collapse is masked; standalone falls back to `height: 0` + transparent → blank.
2. **Regex `<template>` extraction fooled by comments.** The old `/<template[^>]*>([\s\S]*)<\/template>/` could latch onto a literal `"<template>"` appearing inside an HTML comment (e.g. a head note like "the HF runtime clones ONLY `<template>` contents") and mis-slice the capture, re-wrapping the real content in an inert `<template>` that the browser never renders → no `[data-composition-id]` element, no registered timeline → blank.
3. **`data-composition-id` only on the `<template>` tag.** A common authoring pattern. With no host wrapper to carry the id, the rendered body has no `[data-composition-id]` element, the runtime never binds the registered GSAP timeline, seeking does nothing, and the frame renders at its pre-animation state (GSAP `fromTo` pins `opacity:0`) → blank.

### Captured video asset descriptions

For a product/demo capture, the moving clips are usually the strongest hero material, but `generateAssetDescriptions` only described images/SVGs/fonts — videos were invisible to downstream planners.

## How

### `packages/core/.../subComposition.ts`
- `fixDigitLeadingIdSelectors(root)` — collects element ids that start with a digit, then rewrites matching `#id` selectors in `<style>` blocks to their escaped, valid form (`#\30 1-wall-pushes-back`, which still matches `id="01-wall-pushes-back"`) so the rule applies and the full declaration block returns. Scoped to ids actually present on elements, matched as `#id` not followed by another ident char, so hex colors (`#1F2BE0`) and other values are never touched. Run across the whole document (ids live in `<body>`, their rules may live in a `<head>` `<style>`) and in each content branch of `buildSubCompositionHtml`.
- `extractTemplateInnerHtml(rawComp)` — locates the wrapping `<template>` via `querySelector("template")` (a real element node) instead of a regex, so comment text can't fool it.
- `promoteTemplateCompositionId(rawComp, body)` — when the id was declared only on the `<template>` tag and the content has no `[data-composition-id]`, carries it onto the content's first rendered root element. No-op when an element already exposes the id, so compositions that already render correctly are untouched.

These compose cleanly with the post-processing added in #1605 (`stripEmbeddedRuntimeScripts` / `tagRootCompositionFile`): the new helpers handle content **extraction**, #1605's run afterward on the extracted body.

### `packages/cli/.../contentExtractor.ts`
- `generateAssetDescriptions` reads `extracted/video-manifest.json` (written earlier by `captureVideoManifest`, carrying each clip's DOM heading/caption + dims) and emits each *downloaded* clip **first**, tagged `[video]`, with a trimmed caption/heading and `~W×H`. The `videos/` dir is skipped in the image walk (entries come from the manifest, which has the captions the bare files lack).

## Test plan

`packages/core/.../subComposition.test.ts` — 4 new cases, all green (`7 passed`):
- escapes `#id` selectors whose id starts with a digit so the rule is not dropped;
- extracts the real `<template>` even when a head comment mentions the literal text `<template>`;

author: aita
body:
## Bug
`analysis.KindOf` maps `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` to `StmtSelect` and ignores the lock clause, so `StmtKind.IsWrite()` is `false` for it. querytrace's write checks all key off that classification:

- `WarnWriteForbidden` (ForbidWrites context)
- `WarnWriteInReadOnly` (ReadOnly context)
- writes-outside-transaction detection
- `Report.WriteCount`

So a **locking read** — which acquires row locks and is rejected by a read-only transaction or a replica — slipped past every write guard. A `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` under a `ReadOnly()`/`ForbidWrites()` trace context raised **no warning**.

(The routing layer's `Statement.Access` is already lock-aware and routes a locking read to the primary; only the `analysis` classification path was not.)

## Fix
Add `Analysis.LockingRead` (set when a parsed SELECT carries a `Lock` clause) and `Analysis.IsWrite()` (`Kind.IsWrite() || LockingRead`), and switch querytrace's three write checks from `q.Kind.IsWrite()` to the promoted `q.IsWrite()`. Regression test `TestAnalyzeLockingReadIsWrite` covers the classification (a plain SELECT stays a read).

author: zuptalo
body:
## Why

A push to `develop` ran the full build/test/**e2e** suite and rebuilt + republished the `:develop` Docker image **unconditionally** — even for doc/spec/ROADMAP-only commits, whose built app is byte-identical to the previous one. That's a wasted ~12-minute build + multi-arch image push per docs change. (PR CI was already path-filtered; only the develop **push** path wasn't.)

## What changed

One line in `ci.yml`: `verify`'s `if` now gates on the existing `changes` path-filter for **both** PRs and develop pushes:

```diff
-    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true' }}
+    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true' }}
```

- A docs/spec/`.specify/`/ROADMAP/`scripts/`-only push to develop now **skips** `verify`; since `develop-image` chains off `needs: verify`, it skips too — no rebuild, no republish.
- Anything under `src/`, `server/`, `e2e/`, `public/`, deps, `tsconfig*`, `vite/vitest/playwright` configs, `Dockerfile`, or `.github/workflows/**` still **always** runs the full suite and publishes on a develop push.
- `workflow_dispatch` remains an unconditional **force-republish** escape hatch.
- `ci-gate` (required check, `if: always()`) treats a skipped `verify` as pass, so branch protection is unaffected.

## Verification

This PR touches `.github/workflows/**`, so the `changes` filter marks it `code=true` and the **full suite runs on this PR** (proving the gate still fires for workflow changes). After it lands, the follow-up ROADMAP status-bump push will be the first to exercise the docs-only skip.

author: nasyrov
body:
Selecting a table cell in the editor did nothing — no highlight, no inspector. The walker tags each block via an external wrapper `<div data-plumix-id>`, but a `<div>` can't wrap a `<td>`/`<tr>`, so the table sub-blocks were marked `inline` (bare fragment, **no seam**) and became unselectable. The same wrapper indirection meant a per-block style class only *inherited* down to the element, so e.g. text color on a Heading lost to the theme's `h2 { color }`.

This adds a cooperative seam, Gutenberg-style. The walker computes the seam attributes (`data-plumix-id` in edit mode, `data-plumix-block`, style `className`) once and passes them to `render` as `blockProps`. A block that sets `selfSeam: true` spreads `{...blockProps}` onto its own root element and receives no wrapper div; the `<style>` rides as a fragment sibling. Every other block keeps the wrapper div exactly as before. The table rows/cells and the heading opt in.

Result: table cells/rows are selectable (verified live — `data-plumix-id` count inside a table went 0 → 16, and selecting a cell populates the inspector), and a heading's style class now beats the theme's element color.

Known follow-ups (out of scope): the slot wrapper `<div data-plumix-slot-parent>` is still emitted inside `<table>` (the `<table> cannot contain a nested <div>` console warning — it's the slot seam, not the block seam); a styled table-*row* emits its `<style>` inside `<tbody>` (browser-tolerated). Both noted in the `selfSeam` doc.

Part of the editor visual-refinement pass (task #56).

author: diegoparrilla
body:
## Summary
Tooling to bring up the real Atari ST bridge (sidecartridge multidevice) against the browser. The Hatari gateway ↔ browser path already works live; the real-ST-bridge path is the untested one, and a real MIDI port's hard 31250-baud pacing + lock-step timeouts (C-01) are the likely failure points. A software ST-node model for CI was judged redundant against the working Hatari oracle.

### STORY-01 — live interop telemetry (D-key overlay)
- **`sim/checksum.ts`** — FNV-1a `worldChecksum(world)` over every player/drone's per-tick integer state. All nodes step the identical joystick table, so all nodes must show the **identical checksum each tick** (C-02); a drift between two browser screens pins a desync to its tick.
- Expose the per-tick **joystick ring** (`NetGame.lastJoy`) and **last control byte sent** (`ByteChannel.lastControlByte`, `>= 0x80` only).
- New `interop (live)` overlay section: checksum, tick (+ `RING TIMEOUT`), last ctrl tx, joystick ring in hex.

### STORY-02 — ST-bridge timing/pacing review
- The `SEND_DATA` block is **4123 bytes**; `sendPaced` bursts `sendWindow` bytes before the first echo returns, so it must fit the receiver buffer. A real ST ACIA has **no receive FIFO** (Hatari buffers generously, hiding this), so the window is now tunable — `setSendWindow`/`getSendWindow` (default 50, clamped 1..512) + a **`?sendWindow=N`** URL override to drop it at the venue without a rebuild.
- Time each ring exchange (`NetGame.lastTickMs`) and show `ring rtt : <ms> / 1500ms` in the overlay, flagging **`NEAR LIMIT`** past 66% so a tightening real ring is visible before it false-times-out (C-01). Active `send window` is shown too.

The right values are empirical and come from real hardware; this PR provides the knobs and the gauge. EPIC-18 stays `in-progress` pending that manual validation.

## Test
- `npm run lint` clean, `vitest` 145 tests pass (new: world-checksum, `lastControlByte`, `lastJoy`, send-window clamp), build OK.
- Manual: press **D** in a networked game — checksum + joystick ring update each tick; `?sendWindow=N` changes the shown window; `ring rtt` tracks tick latency.

## Summary

Brings up the project's documentation site with a Kartoza-branded MkDocs
build, a combined Doxygen C++ API reference, and automated GitHub Pages
publishing. The code itself is unchanged in this PR.

When merged, the **📚 Docs** workflow runs against `main` and the site
goes live at
[`kartoza.github.io/kartoza-screencaster/`](https://kartoza.github.io/kartoza-screencaster/).

## One-time setup before merging

Enable GitHub Pages once on the repo:

**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**

The Docs workflow takes over from there.

## What's in the box

### Site structure
- Landing page rewritten around end-user value ("Record. Don't edit.")
  with a hero, why-it-exists, and an outcome-led card grid.
- Section landing pages and skeleton stubs for Getting Started, User
  Guide, Administrator Guide, Developer Guide, and About.
- `docs/assets/walkthrough/` set up with a README explaining how the
  maintainer's screen-recording walkthrough frames should land there
  (ffmpeg one-liner included).

### Brand
- `docs/stylesheets/kartoza-tokens.css` — single source of truth for
  Kartoza palette and type stack (Nunito + JetBrains Mono).
- `docs/stylesheets/extra.css` — Material-for-MkDocs adapter that
  consumes the tokens. Flat hero, brand-coloured admonitions,
  outcome-led cards, brand-flat screenshot frames.

### Combined Doxygen + MkDocs publish
- Doxygen output relocated from `docs/doxygen/` to `build/doxygen/` so
  MkDocs doesn't pick it up as orphan files.
- `Docs.yml` CI workflow installs Doxygen + Graphviz, builds the API
  reference, builds the MkDocs site, merges `build/doxygen/html` into
  `site/api/`, and deploys the combined site to GitHub Pages.
- A build-time placeholder at `docs/api/index.md` keeps
  `mkdocs build --strict` clean while making the local-vs-deployed
  story explicit.

| Command                       | What it does                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nix run .#docs-serve`        | MkDocs serve, live reload. `/api/` shows the placeholder.          |
| `nix run .#docs-build`        | Strict MkDocs-only build into `./site`.                            |

| `nix run .#docs-full-build`   | MkDocs + Doxygen, merged at `./site` with `/api/`.                 |
| `nix run .#docs-full-serve`   | Combined build + static-serve so the `/api/` link works locally.   |

The dev-shell `shellHook` lists all five at the top of the

## Problem

The `Container Images CD` build on master is failing at the `pnpm --frozen-lockfile` step:

```
ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY  Broken lockfile: no entry for 'posthog-js@1.391.6' in pnpm-lock.yaml
```

A botched merge left the `products/ai_gateway` importer in `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolving `posthog-js` to `1.391.6`, while the catalog (`^1.391.7`) and all 27 other importers use `1.391.7`. There is no `packages:`/`snapshots:` entry for `1.391.6`, so the frozen install rejects the lockfile and the image build aborts.

## Changes

Bump the single stale `products/ai_gateway` importer entry from `1.391.6` to `1.391.7`. One-line change; the `1.391.7` package and snapshot entries already exist in the lockfile.

I'm an agent (PostHog Slack app). I ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter=@posthog/plugin-transpiler...` (the exact target that failed in CI) locally against the edited lockfile — it now resolves and installs cleanly. No manual app testing.

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Investigated a failing master CD build at Ben White's request from a Slack thread. Traced the Depot build failure to a `frozen-lockfile` mismatch, isolated the single stale importer (`products/ai_gateway`, line 2567), and confirmed the fix by reproducing the failing `--frozen-lockfile` install locally before and after the edit. author: alexfrmn
body:
## What

Implements **native request-reply (design B)** for `murmur_request`: an optional read-only NATS tap that returns the reply as soon as a matching envelope is observed, instead of waiting out the store-poll interval.

Closes the Planned roadmap item "NATS native request-reply (JARVIS)".

## How

- **`broker-nats`: `subscribeRaw(subject, onEnvelope)`** — plain `nc.subscribe`, **no ACK / no dedupe / no JetStream consumer**. A plain subscriber receives `js.publish`'d messages in real time and (no queue group) never steals delivery from the durable daemon consumer. Malformed frames ignored — it's a wake signal, not a delivery path.
- **`mcp-server`: `waitForReply()`** — pure, injectable wait-loop. Store polling always runs (durable fallback); an optional `onSignal` source short-circuits the wait. **Arm-before-check** guards against lost wakeups.
- **`mcp-server` `murmur_request`** — lazy ephemeral broker (`jetstream:false`, `try/catch → null` graceful degrade to pure polling). The tap reads only envelope **metadata** (`conversationId`, `senderAgentId`) to match the reply — **no payload decrypt**; the daemon stays the source of truth for decrypt + persistence. New optional `grace_ms` knob (default 250ms) lets the daemon persist before re-checking.

## Design B constraints (locked with CODEX-VOLT)

| Constraint | How it's met |
|---|---|
| No send outside outbox | tap is subscribe-only; sending unchanged (outbox.enqueue) |
| Store-poll stays fallback | polling always runs; signal only accelerates; null broker ⇒ pure poll |
| Decrypt = existing path | tap reads envelope metadata only; daemon decrypts + persists |
| Tests prove durability (live-wait off / timeout) | see tests below |

## Tests

`tests/mcp-request-reply.test.mjs` (pure, real timers, deterministic):
- **A** resolves via store-poll fallback when no signal is wired (durability, live-wait off)
- **B** returns null on timeout
- **C / C2** signal accelerates past a long poll interval; without it, times out
- **D** lost-wakeup safety (signal fired *during* the store check)
- `buildReplyMatcher` unit

Full suite green: `npm test` → unit **63 pass**, core 6, a2a 6, broker-ws 4, federation 24, ws4/ws5/notify smoke ok. Build `tsc -b` clean.

## For review (CODEX-VOLT)

1. **New dep**: `@murmurv2/broker-nats` added to `mcp-server` (for `NatsBroker` tap). Acceptable, or prefer raw `nats`? broker-nats felt cleaner.
2. **Heads-up**: `packages/broker-nats/dist` is **tracked** (force-added earlier; every other package's dist is gitignored). I kept it in sync with src in this PR. Worth a separate cleanup (`git rm --cached` to match the others)?
3. Ephemeral broker is a lazy singleton, never explicitly closed (drains on process exit). OK for the long-lived stdio mcp-server, or add a shutdown path?

author: bahugunajii
body:
Refs #546 (Phase 1)

## Why

`code` values are duplicated for some `chapter` and `topic` rows in production. The end goal (per #546) is a DB-level unique index on `code`, but that **can't be added yet** — a `create unique_index` migration would crash on deploy the moment it hits an existing duplicate, and merging those duplicates is manual work (checking each row's associations first).

So this is **Phase 1**: stop *new* duplicates immediately, without touching existing data and without any migration that could break the deploy.

## What

Adds an application-level uniqueness check on `code` to both the `Chapter` and `Topic` changesets via `unsafe_validate_unique`. Because both the `resource`/chapter/topic APIs **and** the CSV import worker go through these changesets, this covers all the normal write paths.

The check is guarded to only run when a `code` is actually supplied (`get_change` returns a non-empty value), since the column is still nullable for now — rows without a code are left alone, and `unsafe_validate_unique` already excludes the current row on updates.

### Known limitations (by design)

This is a **stopgap, not the final guarantee**:
- Not race-safe — there's a small TOCTOU window between the check and the insert (acceptable here: chapters/topics are admin/import-created, low concurrency).
- Doesn't cover raw SQL / direct DB writes.

The **DB-level unique index** (plus making `code` `NOT NULL`) remains the eventual guarantee. That's **Phase 2**, which depends on first manually merging the existing duplicates and backfilling any null codes — to be tracked separately. Once the index exists, this validation becomes fully race-safe (and we'll pair it with `unique_constraint/2`).

## Tests

New `test/dbservice/chapters_test.exs` and `test/dbservice/topics_test.exs` cover, for each table:
- duplicate `code` on create → rejected with `"has already been taken"`
- multiple rows **without** a code → allowed
- updating a row without changing its code → allowed (no self-collision)
- updating a row to a code used by another row → rejected

`mix test` → 8/8. `mix format` + `mix credo` clean.

author: shin1ohno
body:
## Summary

Layer 1 of the reshaped 2-layer self-heal design (`~/self-heal-observability-loop-design.md`). Closes the fleet's **notification-delivery gap**: Kibana already runs ~38 alerting rules (uptime/synthetics + ~30 `.es-query` "Process down" rules), but their only action is the `.server-log` connector (journal, unread) — Kibana notification connectors are a paid feature. Firing state lands in alerts-as-data indices nobody watches; live proof: a `Process down: roon / RoonAppliance` alert sat `status=active` **unnoticed for 21 days**.

A read-only bash poller on CT 111 reads those indices, dedups via the existing `self-heal-state` index (Phase 0, #453), and pushes **NEW/RESOLVED transitions to a human via AWS SNS**. It is NOT a detector (Kibana detects) and NOT a classifier (that is Layer 2 / Phase 2 AI).

- **`cookbooks/self-heal-observer`** — bash driver + cron.d (every 5 min, +2 offset from the orchestrator, own `flock` — mirrors `auto-mitamae-orchestrator`) + `observer.env`. Polls `.alerts-observability.uptime.alerts-default` + `.alerts-stack.alerts-default` for `kibana.alert.status=="active"` with **no `@timestamp` window** (`@timestamp` is not refreshed while an alert stays active — verified live — so a recency filter would drop real continuously-active problems). Dedup via `self-heal-state` (upsert by `sha1(dedup_key)`, status open/resolved). First run notifies current-open once as a baseline, then transitions only. Emits node_exporter textfile metrics.
- **`cookbooks/lxc-monitoring/files/alerts/self-heal.yml`** + the `lxc-monitoring` remote_file wiring — `SelfHealObserverStale` / `SelfHealObserverErroring` (a dead observer silently reports all-clear, so Prometheus watches it).
- **`pve/lxc-monitoring.rb`** — include after `lxc_entry`.

## Merge-safety

The SNS topic ARN is read **at runtime** from SSM `/monitoring/self-heal/sns-topic-arn`. Until the home-monitor TF PR creates that parameter, the observer polls + writes textfile but **skips publish** (logs a WARN), never erroring the converge — so this PR is main-mergeable independent of the TF PR. `pve-bootstrap-ssm` already reads `/monitoring/*`.

## Deferred / companion

- **home-monitor TF (companion PR):** `aws_sns_topic` (AWS-managed encryption) + email subscription + a narrow `sns:Publish`-on-this-topic-ARN grant to `pve-bootstrap-ssm` + the `/monitoring/self-heal/sns-topic-arn` SSM param. Apply that + confirm the email subscription to turn on delivery.
- Next Layer-1 increment (separate): foundation watchdog for ES-red / Kibana-down / pipeline-stale (the things Kibana can't self-report).

## Test plan

- `ruby -c cookbooks/self-heal-observer/default.rb`; `bash -n`; **shellcheck 0.11.0 rc=0**
- `bin/lint-cookbooks` clean (174 recipes); `bin/audit-cookbook-reachability` clean (140/140)
- **Live smoke test on CT 111** against the real ES cluster (throwaway state index, SNS off, dropped after): baseline run wrote 3 open docs (the real strict mapping accepted them, incl the 21-day roon), dedup run produced `new=0`, textfile `result=ok active_alerts=3`. Real `self-heal-state` left untouched (baseline preserved).
- Post-apply on CT 111: confirm `/etc/cron.d/self-heal-observer`, textfile `last_run` advances every 5 min, `SelfHealObserverStale` green; after the TF PR applies, a real NEW alert reaches the SNS email within one cycle and a continuously-active alert does not re-notify.

author: ecodiacode
body:
## Problem
Field report (Tate): clicking download made you wait for the whole offline bundle before you could get directions offline. `/build` blocked the manifest on 16 live Overpass/API overlay queries (traffic/hazards/weather/fuel/heritage/...) plus the route score - the slow part - and `/download` streamed every overlay before the trip was usable. Navigation needs none of that.

## Fix (phased)
Nav-critical = navpack + corridor graph + corridor-tiles (+ places). The iOS unpacker already requires only navpack + corridor for offline-ready and is idempotent, so overlays can land later and merge.

- `BundleBuildRequest.nav_only` (default false): `/build` skips the 16 overlays + score, returning the manifest as soon as places + corridor + tiles-key are ready.
- `/bundle/{plan_id}/download?tier=nav`: `build_zip(nav_only=true)` ships only manifest + navpack + corridor + corridor-tiles + places, skipping the 16 richness overlays. `tier=full` (default) unchanged.

Client (iOS, glovebox-ios e121be3) downloads tier=nav first -> navigable immediately -> background tier=full merges overlays.

Additive + default-preserving. 81 backend tests pass. Deployed to roam-backend revision 00103-wgm.

`useI18n.t(key)` renvoie la **clé brute** (string truthy) tant que le namespace n'est pas chargé ou si la clé manque. Donc `t('key') || 'Connexion magique'` est **doublement cassé** :

author: pher217
body:
## Goal
Make `ask_human` actually round-trip: a typed Telegram reply becomes the answer the waiting coding session receives. This is the missing piece behind \"typing 'hello' did nothing\" — the input channel for driving an orc session turn-by-turn.

## Root cause
`ask_human` (called without options) creates a **FREE_TEXT** prompt, `_deliver`s it to the operator's chat (`ORC_PROMPT_CHAT_ID` → forum General), then the MCP client polls `result(nonce)` for `status=answered`. **Nothing ever resolved a FREE_TEXT prompt from an inbound message:**
- `handle_callback_query` → only button callbacks (approve/deny).
- `handle_forum_reply` → creates a *new* PTY inject-approval, never resolves the pending question.
- `handle_update` → routed typed text to the chat LLM.

So a typed answer had nowhere to go → every `ask_human` hit `[no answer: timeout]`. (Buttons/approvals always worked; this is purely the free-text path.)

## Changes
- `apps/connectors/service.py` — new `resolve_pending_ask(text, by)`: resolves the most-recent pending, non-expired FREE_TEXT prompt with the typed reply via the row-locked `prompts.service.resolve`. Returns `None` when nothing is waiting. FREE_TEXT is only ever created by `ask()`, so this is scoped to connector questions.
- `apps/telegram/service.py` — `handle_update` calls `resolve_pending_ask` (operator-gated on `from_user_id`) before chat-LLM dispatch; on success sends a confirmation and returns.

## Approach / scope
- Single insertion point matching the delivery path: the FREE_TEXT prompt is delivered with no `message_thread_id` (forum General / DM), so the reply lands in `handle_update`, not `handle_forum_reply`. No change to the PTY-inject or approval flows.
- Request → answer driving: while a question is pending, the operator's next message answers it; afterwards messages route to the LLM again. Loop `ask_human` for continuous driving.
- Security: strictly less powerful than PTY inject (returns text to the agent; no keystroke injection). Operator-gated; anti-replay via `select_for_update`.

## Test Summary
- `apps/connectors/tests/test_ask_reply.py` — 4 tests: resolves FREE_TEXT + `result()` returns answer; `None` when none pending; ignores CHOICE prompts; targets most-recent question.
- `apps/telegram/tests/test_ask_reply_inbound.py` — 2 tests: typed reply resolves the pending ask and does NOT hit the LLM; normal dispatch preserved when nothing pending.
- Full `apps/connectors apps/telegram apps/prompts` suite: **159 passed**, ruff clean.

## Note for testing live
The reply must arrive where the prompt is delivered — `ORC_PROMPT_CHAT_ID` (falls back to `TELEGRAM_FORUM_CHAT_ID`), i.e. the forum **General** topic (not a mirror topic). That chat must be in `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS`, same gate as all other inbound messages.

## Files Changed
- `apps/connectors/service.py` — `resolve_pending_ask`
- `apps/telegram/service.py` — wire into `handle_update`
- `apps/connectors/tests/test_ask_reply.py` — new
- `apps/telegram/tests/test_ask_reply_inbound.py` — new

# Pull Request Description closes #10 ## Adding Dynamic CSS Classes to Requirements Based on Attributes ### Summary This PR adds functionality to dynamically apply CSS classes to requirement items based on their YAML attributes. This enables visual styling of requirements based on their properties (e.g., normative status, verification method) without modifying the core Python code. ### What Changed **Modified Files:** - `doorstop/core/template/views/doorstop.tpl` - Added JavaScript to apply CSS classes dynamically **How It Works:** 1. When publishing HTML, item attributes (e.g., `normative`, `verification-method`) are collected from the document object 2. JavaScript in the template iterates over all items and finds their HTML elements by ID 3. CSS classes are applied to elements based on attribute values 4. Attribute values are automatically sanitized to create valid CSS class names (e.g., `"Test & Inspection"` → `"test-inspection"`) ### Usage Example **1. Define attributes in your requirement (e.g., `REQ001.yml`):** ```yaml normative: true verification-method: "Test and Inspection" ``` **2. Publish HTML:** ```bash doorstop publish all ./dist --template doorstop ``` **3. Result:** ```html

REQ-001 Requirements

``` **4. Style in CSS (`doorstop.css`):** ```css .normative { border-left: 4px solid blue; } .verification-method-test-and-inspection { background-color: #f0f8ff; } ``` ### Currently Supported Attributes - **`normative`** (boolean) → CSS class: `normative` or `non-normative` - **`verification-method`** (string) → CSS class: `verification-method-{sanitized-value}` ### Extensibility New attributes can be easily added by: 1. Adding attribute collection in the template 2. Adding the corresponding CSS class handler 3. Defining styles in `doorstop.css` No Python code changes required - all customization is done in the template. ### Benefits - **Flexible styling**: Visual representation of requirement attributes - **No code changes**: Implemented entirely in the template layer - **User-customizable**: Users can add their own attributes without modifying Doorstop core - **Backward compatible**: Existing functionality remains unchanged ### Testing Tested with: - Multiple documents with various attribute combinations - Special characters and whitespace in attribute values (properly sanitized) - Missing attributes (gracefully handled) - Items without IDs (skipped without errors)

body:
## Summary

Fixes #461.

The italic regex in `_convert_segment` was matching standalone arithmetic asterisks (e.g. `5 * 3`) as italic markers because the lazy `(.+?)` captured the text between two spaced-apart `*` characters. This corrupted any Slack reply containing two or more standalone `*` (multiplication, glob patterns, shell snippets outside code fences).

**Root cause (`router/slack_format.py:43`):**
```python
# before
text = re.sub(r"(?<!\*)\*(?!\*)(.+?)(?<!\*)\*(?!\*)", r"_\1_", text)
```

**Fix:** Require the opening `*` to be immediately followed by a non-whitespace, non-asterisk character, and the closing `*` to be immediately preceded by one:
```python
# after
text = re.sub(r"(?<!\*)\*(?=[^\s*])(.+?)(?<=[^\s*])\*(?!\*)", r"_\1_", text)
```

## Test plan

- [x] New test `test_arithmetic_asterisks_not_converted` reproduces the exact case from the issue (`5 * 3 = 15 and 2 * 4 = 8` → unchanged)
- [x] New tests for single and multiple standalone asterisks
- [x] Existing italic tests still pass (e.g. `*italic*` → `_italic_`)
- [x] New test confirms italic and arithmetic asterisks coexist correctly
- [x] All 23 unit tests pass
- [x] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass
