body:
## Summary

Two improvements from [@zwangjacket](https://github.com/zwangjacket):

### Fix: fal.ai `thinking_level` validation error

Running nano-banana-2 failed with:
```
[{'type': 'literal_error', 'loc': ['body', 'thinking_level'], 'msg': "Input should be 'minimal' or 'high'", 'input': ''}]
```

**Root cause:** `thinking_level` was defined as a free-form `string` with `default=""`. The empty string was forwarded to the fal.ai API which only accepts `'minimal'` or `'high'`.

**Fix:**
- `model_registry_falai.py`: Change `thinking_level` to a `select` with `choices=('', 'minimal', 'high')` and `default=""`, so the UI renders a proper dropdown.
- `validation.py`: Extend `_omit_blank_parameter` to silently drop empty-string user values for any optional `select` parameter (one whose choices include `""`), preventing the blank value from being sent to the provider.

### Feat: copy-prompt button in image info tooltip

The info tooltip showed the prompt text but it was not selectable or copyable (`pointer-events: none`).

**Changes:**
- `metadata.js`: Adds a clipboard icon button below the prompt line. Clicking it calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(prompt)` and shows a brief green "Copied!" confirmation for 1.5s. Button is hidden when no prompt is available.
- `app.css`: Enables `pointer-events: auto` on the visible tooltip; adds `.tooltip-copy-prompt` and `.tooltip-copy-prompt-done` styles.
- `eslint.config.js`: Registers `navigator` as a readonly browser global.
- Rebuilt `app.js` bundle.

## Tests

- All 378 Python tests pass (`uv run pytest`).
- All 56 JS tests pass including 2 new tests for the copy button (`npm run js:check`).
- `uv run ruff check src tests` — clean.

author: aborii
body:
## Summary

Adds NestJS-native **guards, interceptors, and exception filters** for Telegram Bot API updates, so cross-cutting concerns (authorization, rate limiting, logging/timing, error handling) compose around `@TelegramUpdate` handlers exactly the way they do for HTTP routes — using the standard `CanActivate`, `NestInterceptor`, and `ExceptionFilter` contracts.

Closes #10.

## Note on scope (re-investigated per the issue)

The issue said it *"Depends on the decorator system (bot decorators issue)."* I re-investigated the live code first: that decorator system (`@TelegramUpdate`/`@Command`/… + `TelegramBotUpdatesRegistrar`) **already exists** under `src/lib/bot/updates/`, and the registrar's per-handler dispatch is the single binding point (the decorator docs even flagged guards as the planned extension here). So the dependency is satisfied and this builds directly on it — no decorator work was needed.

## What changed

**Core enhancer layer** (`src/lib/bot/updates/execution/`)
- `TelegramExecutionContext` — adapts a Telegraf `Context` to a NestJS `ExecutionContext` (`getContext()`, `getType()==='telegram'`, `getHandler()/getClass()`; the `switchTo*` HTTP/RPC/WS accessors throw with a clear message). Static `create(host)` recovers it from the `ExecutionContext`/`ArgumentsHost` Nest hands enhancers.
- `@UseTelegramGuards` / `@UseTelegramInterceptors` / `@UseTelegramFilters` — attach enhancers at the class level (all handlers) or per method; accept ready instances **or** DI class refs.
- `TelegramEnhancerResolver` — resolves refs to instances (`ModuleRef.get`, fast-fails with `TelegramConfigError` if a class ref isn't a registered provider), reads standard `@Catch(...)` metadata, and orders guards/interceptors **class-first** and filters **method-first**.
- `runWithEnhancers` — the pipeline: **guards → interceptors (rxjs `CallHandler` chain) → handler → exception filters**. Guard denial stops silently (debug log); an unhandled error keeps the existing "isolate & log" guarantee.

**Built-ins**
- `ChatAllowlistGuard`, `UserAllowlistGuard` — allow/deny by chat or sender ID.
- `RateLimitGuard` — per-key token bucket (chat ID by default), injectable clock for tests.
- `TelegramExceptionFilter` — default catch-all: logs + optional user-facing reply (string or factory).

**Wiring**
- `TelegramBotUpdatesRegistrar` resolves each handler's enhancers once at bootstrap and dispatches through the pipeline; **handlers with no enhancers keep the original fast path** (no `ExecutionContext`/pipeline overhead).
- `TelegramEnhancerResolver` registered in `TelegramBotModule`; public surface exported from the `nestjs-telegram` root and `nestjs-telegram/bot` subpath.

**Docs & example**
- New `docs/BOT-GUARDS-FILTERS-INTERCEPTORS.md`; updated `docs/BOT-UPDATE-DECORATORS.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`, `README.md`; runnable `examples/bot-enhancers.example.ts` (typechecked).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A guard can block an update — verified end-to-end (handler never runs; DI-resolved guard class).
- [x] A filter catches a thrown handler error — verified (`catch(error, host)` receives the error + a `TelegramExecutionContext`).
- [x] An interceptor wraps execution — verified (pre → handler → post ordering).
- [x] Fully typed, tested, no network. No `any`, no `enum`. Bot⟷client decoupling preserved (no cross-imports).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (incl. `examples/`).
- `npm test` — **335 passed / 41 suites** (was 122 on the bot side; +new specs). New files at ~98%+ statements/lines; the only uncovered lines are the registrar's unreachable exhaustiveness `default` and a couple of defensive guards.
- `npm run build` — succeeds (`.d.ts` emitted).

author: juanpablolfavot-coder
body:
## Qué resuelve

Dos problemas en el registro de cargas de combustible (los que mostraste):

1. Al registrar una carga, el campo **CHOFER** no se autocompletaba con el chofer del camión.
2. En el listado, la columna **CHOFER** mostraba al **encargado que registró** (ej. "Soldevila Marcelo" en todas), no al chofer real del camión.

## Causa raíz

El backend **ignoraba** el campo `driver` del formulario e insertaba `driver_id = req.user.id` (el usuario logueado = el encargado). El listado mostraba `users.name` de ese `driver_id` → siempre el encargado.

## El fix

- **Nueva columna `fuel_logs.driver_name`** (texto): el chofer real de la carga. El `POST` ahora lee `driver` del form y lo guarda ahí. `driver_id` sigue siendo *quien registra* (lo necesita el filtro del rol `chofer` y la trazabilidad de quién cargó).
- **GET** ahora devuelve `COALESCE(fl.driver_name, v.driver_name, u.name)`:
  - Registros **nuevos** → el chofer guardado.
  - Registros **viejos** (sin `driver_name`) → caen al **chofer asignado del vehículo** (no al encargado). Así el listado existente también queda bien.
- **Modal**: al elegir la unidad, autocompleta el chofer con el asignado al vehículo. Queda **editable** por si ese día maneja un suplente.
- Columna agregada a `schema.sql` (bases nuevas) y vía `ALTER ... IF NOT EXISTS` idempotente (base existente).

## Riesgo
Bajo. La columna es aditiva; `driver_id` no cambia (no rompe el filtro del rol chofer). Requiere `npm run migrate` (o se autocrea en el primer POST por el ALTER idempotente).

## Prueba
- [ ] Registrar carga eligiendo una unidad → el campo Chofer se autocompleta con el chofer del camión, y se puede editar.
- [ ] En *Registro de cargas*, la columna CHOFER muestra el chofer del camión (no el encargado).
- [ ] Cargas viejas muestran el chofer asignado del vehículo.
- [ ] Un usuario con rol `chofer` sigue viendo solo sus propias cargas.

author: okalldal
body:
Refs #228
Part of #255

## Done-when (one line)
A test-only, deliberately Python-shaped `PythonTransformerOracleBuilder` replays the C1 action specs over the shaped parse tree, emits both a final value and an ordered callback trace, and matches Python's value JSON **and** trace for every C1 fixture under LALR + basic and LALR + contextual — no public API.

## What it does
- The backend (a `mod transformer` inside `tests/test_transformer_oracle.rs`, test-only) holds the action spec keyed by **callback-name / terminal-name** — the same name world the C2 `tree_builder::OutputBuilder` seam speaks (`build_node(tree_name, …)` / `build_token`). It resolves each visited node to that world (`Tree::data` = the alias/template/origin Python's `create_callback` dispatches on; `Token::type_` = the terminal name) and reproduces Python Lark's `Transformer.transform` bottom-up post-order walk over the already-shaped tree.
- `TransformValue::to_json` mirrors the generator's `_serialize_value`, and the rule/token action interpreters mirror `_apply_rule_action` / `_apply_token_action`, so Rust values are byte-comparable to the committed Python value JSON.

## Engine-token vs visible-callback (RFC §5)
`transform_token` honors the load-bearing distinction: the engine materializes a `Token`-compatible value for **every** kept terminal, but a *visible* terminal callback is logged only when the spec defines a method for that terminal (else `__default_token__` if set); a kept terminal with **no** method is materialized **silently** (no trace entry). A dedicated pin (`test_engine_token_vs_visible_callback_distinction`) uses `token_normalizer_upper`, where `NAME` has a method (logged) and `PUNCT` does not (silent). Discard filtering, `maybe_placeholders` `None` pass-through, aliases, `expand1`, transparent inlining, and `keep_all_tokens` are all covered by the fixture set.

## Oracle evidence
- `cargo test --test test_transformer_oracle` → **8 passed**, including:
  - `test_transformer_backend_value_and_trace_parity` — every one of the 15 C1 cases × {lalr_basic, lalr_contextual} = 30 configs, value JSON **and** trace JSON both match the committed oracle.
  - `test_engine_token_vs_visible_callback_distinction` — RFC §5 pin.
  - the five pre-existing C1 schema/coverage tests still green.
- Before this PR, no Rust backend consumed the C1 fixtures' value/trace — only the schema was validated. This PR turns "did we really implement Python's transformer semantics?" into a hard gate.

## /code-review summary + dispositions
Two finder passes (correctness + cleanup/conventions) over the diff:
- **Float `str()` divergence (Finding 1, fixed):** Rust `format!("{f}")` drops the trailing `.0` Python's `str(float)` keeps. Added `py_float_str` so a future fixture that joins/concats `float_value` children stays faithful.
- **`sum`/`product` assumed `i64` children (Finding 2, fixed):** replaced `expect_int` with a `Num` numeric-tower fold (`reduce_numeric`) that promotes to `float` on any float child, matching Python's polymorphic `sum`/`*`.
- **`int_value`/`float_value` parse narrower than Python `int()`/`float()` (Finding 3) and `return_value` big-int literal (Finding 4):** left as documented limitations — matching Python's full coercion/arbitrary-precision tower in a test-only oracle is out of proportion to the committed specs (plain `[0-9]+`). Noted in code.
- **Discard at the start rule (Finding 5):** already an in-code loud-fail path; no fixture exercises it.
- **Cleanup pass:** no CLAUDE.md rule violated; the full-tree clone in `parse_tree_as_child` and a few "mirror-the-generator" arms are deliberate and immaterial at fixture scale. Consuming the public `ParseTree` (the `pub(crate)` `OutputBuilder` seam is unreachable from an integration test) is the only available test-only path.

## Local gate
`lark-rs/scripts/check-fast.sh` (fmt + `cargo test --all`) passed (also run by the pre-push hook). No production code changed — a single test file.

## Follow-ups
None required. The deferred numeric-coercion edge cases (Findings 3–4) would only matter if a future C1 fixture introduces underscore/whitespace numeric literals or out-of-`i64` arithmetic; the action interpreters mirror the generator closely enough to extend then.

author: markokraemer
body:
## Why
`kortix self-host start` was booting an **empty database** (zero `kortix` tables) on a fresh install since **#3588** moved schema setup to an explicit migrate step that the self-host compose never ran. Login, accounts, projects, and sessions were all dead. The self-host e2e was never wired into CI, so the regression shipped silently.

## What
- **Schema bootstrap** — new `kortix-migrate` one-shot the API `depends_on` (`service_completed_successfully`). `migrate.ts bootstrap` installs the non-kortix prerequisites (basejump account framework + signup triggers + credit RPCs) from `packages/db/drizzle/0000_bootstrap.sql` — now bundled into the API image — then applies all migrations. Idempotent + no-op on provisioned dev/prod DBs (gated on basejump being absent).
- **Daytona is the self-host default** sandbox runtime (`configure` prompts for the key); `local_docker` kept for fully-local / hermetic-CI use.
- **`self-host update [--tag X]`** — in-place upgrade: re-pull tag → re-migrate → recreate, preserving the Postgres volume. Plus **`self-host version`**.
- **Fixed `local_docker` sessions** — every one threw `Unknown sandbox provider: local_docker` (the snapshot registry has no local adapter). Short-circuited `ensureSandboxImage`: local_docker runs `SANDBOX_IMAGE` directly and bakes no per-project snapshot.
- **CI** — an always-on `self-host-schema` gate in `ci.yml` (runs on every PR touching api/db/cli) + a nightly full e2e (`self-host-e2e.yml`: session + sandbox health + update mechanism). `run.sh` extended to assert the migrate one-shot, basejump, and the update flow.

## Verified
Full self-host e2e green end to end: migrate one-shot (85 tables, basejump) → bootstrap-owner → accounts/projects → **local_docker session + sandbox `/kortix/health` ready** → **update → re-migrate idempotent → data persisted (409)**. Fast `schema-check.sh` green. `packages/db` 89/0 tests.

author: tamnd
body:
Native fuzz targets over the byte-facing surfaces from doc 23 section 7.

Five targets, one per surface:
- rdb: FuzzUnmarshal (DUMP/RESTORE value decoder), FuzzUnmarshalFile (whole-file RDB decoder)
- lua: FuzzParse (parser), FuzzRun (interpreter, with a deadline hook standing in for the script-kill timeout)
- pager: FuzzOpen (file format)
- command: FuzzDispatch (dispatcher, asserts PING still answers after each call)

Two real bugs came out of the first run and are fixed here.

Lua loops with an empty body never ticked the deadline hook. while true do end ignored lua-time-limit and SCRIPT KILL and ran forever. Now each of the four loop forms ticks once per iteration, so the hook fires on the loop itself regardless of the body.

A corrupt RDB count went straight into make with that count as the cap and panicked with cap out of range. The collection decoders now cap the preallocation hint and stop as soon as the reader runs dry. The failing input is kept under rdb/testdata so it replays as a regression seed.

Gate is clean: gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint at zero, govulncheck clean, go test -race green, go mod tidy with no go.sum.

As-built notes in notes/Spec/2064/implementation/90-fuzz-targets.md.

author: roryford
body:
## Summary
Fixes #99. `manifold-tools-llama --scenario all` ran all nine scenarios against a single shared `InferenceService` — one backend, one KV cache, one conversation. The orchestrator appends each `enqueue` turn to that shared conversation and reuses the resident KV cache (it emits `.kvCacheReuse`), so a later scenario prefilled on top of an earlier scenario's tokens and could run out of context budget mid-answer. That surfaced as **intermittent truncation** (e.g. qwen3-0.6B's `structured-json-extraction` clipped to ` \`\`\`json\n `) that disappeared when the same scenario ran in isolation.

## Fix
Reset the conversation and zero the KV cache **before each scenario** in the `--scenario all` loop:

```swift
service.resetConversation()
service.secureWipe()
```

so every scenario starts from a clean context — matching the deterministic behaviour of an isolated `--scenario <id>` run. Placed at the top of the loop so it still runs after the `padScenario` `continue` path, and is a harmless no-op on the first iteration. Matches the existing ManifoldKit idiom (`secureWipe()` is documented as the LlamaBackend `llama_memory_clear` path).

## Test
Adds `test_secureWipeBetweenTurnsPreventsReuse` to `LlamaKVReuseTests` (model-gated, behind the `Llama` trait) — the inverse of the existing `test_twoTurnsEmitKVReuseSecondTurn`: with a `resetConversation()` + `secureWipe()` interposed between two prefix-sharing turns, the second turn must **not** emit `.kvCacheReuse`, pinning the clean-context guarantee the fix relies on. Backend-level clearing of the cached prefix is already covered by `LlamaKVCacheSecureWipeTests`.

## Verification
- `swift build` clean.
- `swift build --build-tests` clean.

body:
## Motivation

Preparation for the 3.0 release. Go semantic import versioning requires
the `/vN` suffix in the module path for major version N, so moving to 3.0
means the module path must change from `github.com/kumahq/kuma/v2` to
`github.com/kumahq/kuma/v3`.

> Changelog: feat(deps)!: migrate module path to /v3

## Implementation information

Mechanical rename of `github.com/kumahq/kuma/v2` -> `github.com/kumahq/kuma/v3`:

- `go.mod` module declaration + `go mod tidy`
- all `.go` imports (2402 files)
- `.proto` `go_package` options (46 files)
- `mk/*.mk` (`GO_MODULE`, version ldflags)
- `.golangci.yml` (importas aliases, depguard)
- shell scripts and openapi specs
- regenerated derived files via `make clean/tools generate`

Historical records (`CHANGELOG.md`, `UPGRADE.md`, the v2 migration MADR)
intentionally keep their `/v2` references.

Verified locally: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/...`, `make generate`
(reproduces byte-identical `/v3` output), `make format`. Full-matrix CI
validates the rest.

BREAKING CHANGE: projects importing Kuma as a Go library must update
imports from `github.com/kumahq/kuma/v2` to `/v3`.

## Supporting documentation

Same approach as the v1->v2 migration
(`docs/madr/decisions/091-migrate-to-v2-module-path.md`).

author: po4erk91
body:
## Problem

The evolve applier had **no failure backoff, attempt cap, or dead-letter state** for a roadmap issue whose implementer child repeatedly aborts without opening a PR. Once the 24h claim TTL lapsed, the same "poison issue" was re-selected and re-attempted every pass — burning a fresh `bypassPermissions` Opus child each time with **no progress, no escalation, and no signal** — and could wedge the queue ahead of completable work. Nothing distinguished "not yet attempted" from "attempted and failed 12 times."

## What changed

- **Attempt ledger.** Each spawned implementer child records a `roadmap_issue_attempt` event (in `_start_roadmap_issue_child`, after a successful `spawn()`).
- **Escalating backoff.** `ROADMAP_ISSUE_BACKOFF_BASE_S * 2^(attempts-1)` (default base **2 days**, so it exceeds the 24h claim TTL; capped at 30d) defers re-selection — an aborting issue is **not** retried on the very next eligible pass.
- **Dead-letter.** After `ROADMAP_ISSUE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default **3**) the issue is excluded from the auto-drain and flagged for a human: a `blocked` label + a **one-time** summary comment (composes with the #50 skip-label gate). A `roadmap_issue_dead_letter` event is the authoritative idempotent marker; the label/comment are best-effort.
- **Soundness.** A successful child writes `roadmap_issue_applied`, which every selection path checks first — so only genuinely-failing issues accrue attempts.
- **Human override.** An exact `evolve_apply_roadmap_issue(issue_number=N)` call bypasses the cooldown/cap to force a retry; the read-only status path never writes to GitHub.
- **Observability.** Per-issue attempt counts/states in `evolve_apply_status()`; stuck/dead-letter counts in `mp_dashboard()`.

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ An issue that aborts without a PR is not re-attempted on the next eligible pass; an escalating cooldown applies.
- ✅ After K aborts the issue is dead-lettered (excluded + `blocked` label + comment) with no manual intervention.
- ✅ Per-issue attempt counts / states are queryable (event rows) and reflected in `evolve_apply_status()` + `mp_dashboard()`.
- ✅ Tests simulate repeated aborts via a mocked `spawn` and assert (a) backoff defers re-selection and (b) dead-letter excludes after K.

## New knobs

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `THREADKEEPER_ROADMAP_ISSUE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | 3 | dead-letter cap |
| `THREADKEEPER_ROADMAP_ISSUE_BACKOFF_BASE_S` | 172800 (2d) | base backoff window; doubles per attempt, capped 30d |

## Tests / docs

- 8 new tests in `tests/test_evolve_applier.py` (backoff escalation, defer/lapse, dead-letter exclude + idempotent flag, end-to-end attempt→backoff, dead-letter blocks auto but exact overrides, ledger classification, status ledger) + 1 in `tests/test_dashboard.py`.
- Updated `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `.env.example`.
- Full suite green locally (`env -u THREADKEEPER_NO_EMBEDDINGS .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`, exit 0).

Generated by the evolve_applier role.

Closes #82

author: rodrigobnogueira
body:
## Why

`main` is green, but two policy/robustness gaps surfaced via dependabot PR #15 and the multer advisory:

1. **Audit gate over-broad.** `security:audit:package` ran `npm audit --audit-level=high` across the whole workspace. Dev/sample-only advisories (the vulnerable `multer` 1.x pulled in transitively by the sample apps' `@nestjs/platform-express`) failed the gate — even though the published package ships `"dependencies": {}` and never exposes them to consumers.
2. **Showcase HTTP bootstrap relied on hoisting.** `sample/00-showcase`'s smoke used `NestFactory`'s default HTTP-driver auto-discovery, which resolves `@nestjs/platform-express` relative to `@nestjs/core`'s install location. That only works when both are hoisted to the same `node_modules`. A lockfile refresh that nests `platform-express` under the sample (as #15's regenerated lockfile does) breaks it with `No driver (HTTP) has been selected`.

## What

- **`package.json`**: `security:audit:package` → `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`. Audits the *published* surface — exactly what consumers `npm install`. The runtime-reachable `multer` is already pinned to `2.2.0` via the root `overrides`; the vulnerable 1.x copies live only in per-sample dev trees, excluded by `--omit=dev`. Verified: `--omit=dev` tree has **0 high / 0 critical**.
- **`sample/00-showcase`**: pass `ExpressAdapter` explicitly in `src/main.ts` and `scripts/smoke.ts`, so the HTTP driver resolves from the sample's own declared `@nestjs/platform-express` dependency — independent of workspace hoisting. Verified the smoke passes against PR #15's exact de-hoisted lockfile.
- **`GUIDELINES_NEST_ASYNCAPI.md`**: record the audit-scope and strictness-scope decisions.

`packages/asyncapi` keeps `"dependencies": {}`. No lockfile change (the fix is behavioral, not a new dependency).

## Validation

`npm ci && npm run ci` green locally (Node 22.22.0): typecheck, 100% coverage, cognitive-complexity, release:check (sample version sync OK), docs build, `security:audit`, and `ci:sample` (showcase smoke + all focused samples).

author: erseco
body:
## Summary

Restores the missing **File → Close** menu entry reported in #1847. It closes the current editor window in the packaged desktop (Electron) app.

## Why it is Electron-only (and how)

The static browser/PWA build and the Electron app both run in the same `static`/offline runtime, so `config.isOfflineInstallation`, `window.__EXE_STATIC_MODE__`, `runtimeConfig.isStaticMode()` and storage capabilities **cannot** distinguish them. The only reliable Electron signal is the presence of `window.electronAPI`.

So the entry is rendered **hidden** in the offline navbar markup (`d-none exe-electron-only`) and is revealed by `navbarFile.js` **only** when `window.electronAPI.closeCurrentWindow` is a function. In the browser/PWA build it stays hidden; the server (online) build never renders the offline block at all.

## Unsaved-changes handling

Close goes through a new `app:closeCurrentWindow` IPC handler that calls `BrowserWindow.close()` on the sender window. The existing `attachEditorWindowCloseGuard(win)` still intercepts the close and prompts for unsaved changes — no confirmation logic is duplicated.

## Changes

- `app/preload.js` — expose `closeCurrentWindow()` on the `electronAPI` bridge.
- `app/main.js` — add the `app:closeCurrentWindow` IPC handler (resolves the sender window via `BrowserWindow.fromWebContents`, returns `true`/`false`).
- `views/workarea/menus/menuNavbar.njk` — add the hidden `File → Close` item in the offline block, after *Save* and before *Export as…*.
- `src/routes/pages.ts` — register the `close` label in the navbar translation map.
- `public/app/workarea/menus/navbar/items/navbarFile.js` — query the button, add `setCloseFileEvent()` (reveal + wire click only under Electron; respects `checkOpenIdevice()`).
- `public/app/workarea/menus/navbar/items/navbarFile.test.js` — tests for the new behavior.

## Testing

- `make fix` — clean (only a pre-existing unrelated `any` warning in `export.ts`).
- Frontend (Vitest) — full suite green; `navbarFile.test.js` covers: button is queried/stored, `setEvents()` calls `setCloseFileEvent()`, entry shown + close invoked when the Electron bridge is present, idevice-open guard blocks the close, and the entry stays hidden with nothing wired when `electronAPI` is absent. Patch coverage on the changed file is 100%.
- Backend (Bun) — `src/routes/pages.spec.ts` green with the new `close` label.

Note: the Electron-only visibility is verified by unit tests. The Playwright E2E harness runs the web/static build where `window.electronAPI` is absent, so it cannot exercise the Electron path.

Closes #1847

author: omob
body:
## Summary

The v1.1.0 re-cut release run failed because `release.yml`'s smoke job tried to run host-side `npm run db:migrate` after the new `db-migrate` Compose service had already migrated. The migrations table recorded `.js` filenames (from the container's `dist/`), and the host migration then failed with:

```
Error: The migration directory is corrupt, the following files are missing: 20230706012890_create_modules_table.js, ...
```

(missing because the host has `.ts`, not `.js`.)

This is the same conflict that bit `ci.yml` and was fixed in PR #73 — but `release.yml` has its own smoke job that wasn't updated in that PR. This PR removes the now-redundant host migration step from `release.yml`. The `db-migrate` container is the sole migrator on both CI and release paths.

## Why this didn't get caught in PR #73's CI

PR #73's CI exercised `ci.yml`'s smoke job (which we fixed in that same PR). `release.yml`'s smoke job only runs on tag push, not on PR. So the conflict only surfaced when v1.1.0 was actually tagged.

## Test plan

- [x] Diff is minimal (6 lines deleted, 4 comment lines added)
- [ ] After merge: re-cut v1.1.0 (delete tag + retag at new commit). The release workflow runs end-to-end, all 11 stages green.

author: debpalash
body:
## What & why

Fixes #622. A first-run user whose model download was interrupted *after* the config/tokenizer files landed but *before* the weight shard got stranded on the **Models & Engines** page with no way out:

- `GET /models` computed `installed` purely from cache **size** (`cached["size_on_disk"] > 0`), so a size-positive-but-weight-less snapshot reported `installed: true`.
- The first-run `WizardLibrary` shows the install/re-download action only when `!m.installed`, so the button was hidden.
- The repair surface (delete / re-download) lives in **Settings → Models**, which is unreachable while the wizard gates the user on the download page → stranded.

This is the same truncated-download class that `download.py` already guards at **install** time (#352) and `model_manager.py` repairs at **load** time (#581/#606) — the install-state detector just had the same blind spot.

## The fix (whole class, not just the symptom)

- Moved the boolean weight-floor scan into `models.py` (the lowest module in the setup import graph) as `snapshot_has_weights()` + `cache_is_complete()`. **One source of the floors** — `download.py`'s install-time validator now delegates to it, so the install-time / install-state / load-time checks can't drift apart.
- `list_models()` and `recommendations()` downgrade a truncated cache to `installed: false` (and `/models` carries an explicit `incomplete: true`). The existing wizard install action re-appears automatically — no frontend change needed.
- **`config_only` repos exempt:** `pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1` is a pipeline repo whose real weights live in referenced sub-repos, so its own cache is legitimately tiny. It gets a new `config_only: true` hint in `models.yaml` (documented field) and is never flagged incomplete — avoids the false-positive the issue's caveat calls out.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_mm2_lifecycle.py` (fail-before / pass-after):
- `snapshot_has_weights` distinguishes a truncated snapshot from a complete one
- `cache_is_complete` flags a truncated weight repo and exempts a `config_only` repo
- `list_models` downgrades a size-positive-but-weight-less cache to `installed: false` / `incomplete: true`

Full backend suite green locally: **1832 passed, 20 skipped, 11 xfailed, 3 xpassed**. No version bump, no hardcoded CJK, backend-only, pure-filesystem (cross-platform), backward-compatible (only corrects `installed` + adds `incomplete`).

Fixes #622

## Problem Statement

This PR fixes an issue where incomplete model caches (containing config/tokenizer files but missing weight files) were incorrectly reported as installed, stranding first-run users on the download page with no recovery path (Issue `#622`).

The root cause: `GET /models` determines installation status solely by checking if `size_on_disk > 0`, so a truncated cache appeared installed despite missing weights. Since the wizard only offers install/re-download actions when `!m.installed`, users with interrupted downloads were locked on the download page, with the recovery surface (Settings → Models) remaining unreachable.

## Solution

### Core Changes

**1. Centralized weight-detection logic** (`models.py`)
- Added `snapshot_has_weights(snapshot_path)` to walk snapshot directories and identify plausible weight files using extension-based size floors (5MB global fallback)
- Added `cache_is_complete(repo_id, snapshot_path)` to determine if a cached repo has all required weights or is legitimately config-only
- Imported and re-exported weight validation constants (`_MIN_WEIGHT_BYTES`, `_WEIGHT_FLOORS`) for single source of truth

**2. Updated API endpoints**
- `/models` now derives `installed` from both cache presence AND weight completeness check
- Adds explicit `incomplete` boolean field marking cases where cache exists but weights are missing
- `/setup/recommendations` applies the new `cache_is_complete()` check to avoid mis-reporting truncated caches as installed

**3. Unified install-time validation** (`download.py`)
- Refactored `_validate_snapshot_has_weights()` to delegate core weight detection to `models.snapshot_has_weights()`
- Ensures consistency across all three check-points: install-time (download.py), install-state (models.py), and load-time repairs

**4. Config-only repo exemption** (`models.yaml`)
- Introduced optional `config_only` field for pipeline-style repos with no standalone weights
- Marked `pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1` with `config_only: true` to prevent false-positive incomplete flags

### Behavior Change Flowchart

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Cache Existence Check                                   │
│ (size_on_disk > 0)                                      │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │
         ┌───────────┴───────────┐
         │                       │
      NO │                       │ YES
         │                       │
         ▼                       ▼
    installed:              Check if config_only=true
    false              ┌─────────┴───────────┐
                       │                     │
                    YES│                     │NO
                       │                     │
                       ▼                     ▼
                   installed:         snapshot_has_weights()?
                   true              ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                   incomplete:        │                    │
                   false           YES│                    │NO
                                      │                    │
                                      ▼                    ▼
                                  installed:          installed:
                                  true                false
                                  incomplete:         incomplete:
                                  false               true
```

## Test Coverage

- Added regression tests in `tests/test_mm2_lifecycle.py` covering:
  - `snapshot_has_weights()` returns `True` with weights, `False` when truncated
  - `cache_is_complete()` correctly identifies incomplete vs. complete caches
  - Config-only exemptions prevent false-positive incomplete flags
  - `list_models()` downgrades truncated caches to `installed: false` with `incomplete: true`
- Full backend test suite: 1832 passed, 20 skipped, 11 xfailed, 3 xpassed

## Technical Details

- **Backend-only, cross-platform fix:** Pure filesystem operations, no frontend changes required
- **Backward-compatible:** Existing behavior for complete caches unchanged
- **User recovery path:** Incomplete caches now display `installed: false`, allowing the wizard's install/re-download action to appear

## Files Changed

- `backend/api/routers/setup/models.py` (+99/-2): Weight detection and endpoint updates
- `backend/api/routers/setup/download.py` (+18/-33): Refactored to delegate to centralized weight check
- `backend/config/models.yaml` (+5/-0): Added `config_only` field for `pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1`
- `tests/test_mm2_lifecycle.py` (+75/-0): Regression tests for weight-aware install state

author: bbrala
body:
When `AnnotationToAttributeRector` converts a Drupal plugin annotation to a PHP attribute, the bare positional (keyless) value was silently dropped.

## The bug

Two GitLab issues, one root cause:

- [#3579141](https://git.drupalcode.org/project/rector/-/work_items/3579141): `@FormElement("foo_eligible_product_for_current_user_select")` converted to `#[\Drupal\Core\Render\Attribute\FormElement]` — the plugin id was lost.
- [#3470861](https://git.drupalcode.org/project/rector/-/work_items/3470861): same problem with single-value annotations like `@ViewsField("id")` losing the id.

## Root cause

In `createAttribute()`, the loop that builds attribute arguments skipped any annotation value with `key === null`:

```php
if ($value->key === null) {
    continue; // dropped the positional value
}
```

A plugin annotation's bare positional value (the `"foo"` in `@FormElement("foo")`) has `key === null`, so it was never emitted as a constructor argument.

## The fix

Instead of skipping keyless values, emit them as positional `Arg`s. Because PHP requires positional arguments before named ones in an attribute, positional and named args are now collected separately and merged positional-first:

- `@FormElement("foo")` → `#[FormElement('foo')]`
- `@FormElement("my_element", label = ..., type = "system")` → `#[FormElement('my_element', label: ..., type: 'system')]`

The existing `deriver` handling and `@Translation` / nested-annotation handling are untouched.

## Tests

Added fixtures to the existing `AnnotationToAttributeRector` test, with `FormElement` and `ViewsField` annotation→attribute mappings added to the test config:

- `form_element_positional_fixture.php.inc` — positional-only id (#3579141)
- `views_field_positional_fixture.php.inc` — single-value positional id (#3470861)
- `form_element_positional_and_keyed_fixture.php.inc` — positional value plus keyed values, proving positional-first ordering

All tests pass: `OK (13 tests, 26 assertions)`.

author: edjchapman
body:
## Summary

Two independent fixes to the management surface, both surfaced while debugging a broken `mac` (chezmoi-fix) run.

### 1. `fix(zsh)` — force BSD `stat` in the brewup lock check
Homebrew coreutils can shadow macOS BSD `stat` on `PATH` with GNU `stat`, whose `-f` flag means *filesystem mode* rather than *format*. When the brewup lock dir existed, GNU `stat -f %m` printed a path string (`File: "/Users/ed/.cache/brewup.lock"...`) that flowed into the `(( ... ))` arithmetic on the next line and produced:

```
/Users/ed/.zshrc:193: bad math expression: operand expected at `"/Users/ed...'
```

Fix: call `/usr/bin/stat -f %m` explicitly so BSD syntax is always used regardless of `PATH` ordering.

### 2. `fix(chezmoi)` — ignore rendered mkdocs `site/` build output
`mkdocs build` writes the rendered site to `site/`. It is `.gitignore`d, but **chezmoi does not honor `.gitignore`** (it uses `.chezmoiignore`), so all 154 files were treated as home-file drift targeting `~/site/` — the bulk of the "156 things need attention" banner, and what made `chezmoi-fix` option 2 (`chezmoi diff`) page a wall of minified JS/CSS and binary PNGs. Added `site` to `.chezmoiignore` alongside the existing `docs`/`mkdocs.yml`/`assets` entries.

## Verification
- Reproduced the exact `bad math expression` error with bare `stat`; confirmed `/usr/bin/stat -f %m` returns a clean epoch.
- `chezmoi diff` dropped from 154 garbled files to 0; `HOME_DRIFT` is now `0` and the home-file option no longer appears in the `mac` menu.

🚨 **Severity**: CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability**: A hardcoded fallback secret ('dev-secret-change-me') was present in 'auth.module.ts' and 'jwt.strategy.ts' when process.env.JWT_SECRET was undefined.
🎯 **Impact**: If deployed without the environment variable, the application continues to run silently using a weak, easily guessable secret, leading to authentication bypass or token forgery.
🔧 **Fix**: Avoided fallback secrets completely in code. Instead, we fail securely by explicitly throwing an error at startup if required security environment variables are missing. This ensures misconfigurations are caught immediately.

body:
Registers the new `model2` case `9_3F_GINJ_GAS_REIN_CAP_STW` so the regression suite covers a group where a binding `GCONINJE GAS REIN` cap and `GCONSALE` interact.

#### Register `9_3F_GINJ_GAS_REIN_CAP_STW` in `regressionTests.cmake`

- **One line added** to the `_model2_tests` list; the case inherits the shared `add_multiple_tests` config (`DEV_SIMULATOR flow_blackoil`, shared tolerances, `DIR model2`).
- The case covers a group with **both** a `GCONINJE GAS REIN` control (with a **binding maximum gas injection rate**) **and** `GCONSALE`: the cap limits reinjection and `GCONSALE` reduces gas production to meet the sales target.
- **Why it matters:** the existing `9_3*` cases have no binding injection limit, so the related opm-common fix only changes the stored control records there. Here the **rates** change, so a future revert of the fix would change the **summary**, not just the restart records.

#### Dependencies

- Requires the matching opm-tests deck: https://github.com/OPM/opm-tests/pull/1536
- Goes with the opm-common fix: https://github.com/OPM/opm-common/pull/5228

body:
## Summary

- Adds liveness-based queue ticket reaping to the janitor startup sweep
- `SIGKILL` bypasses the `finally` block in `_acquire_slot`, leaving `.queue/` ticket files that permanently block waiting dispatches; the janitor now removes them
- Adds `POOL_QUEUE_DIR_NAME` to `constants.py` for parity with `POOL_SLOTS_DIR_NAME`

## What changed

**`packs/dispatch/constants.py`**: Added `POOL_QUEUE_DIR_NAME = ".queue"` so pack modules share one source of truth for the queue directory name.

**`packs/dispatch/janitor.py`**: Added `_reclaim_queue_tickets(queue_dir, workspace_root)` which runs after the main workspace sweep. For each ticket in `.queue/`, if the dispatch workspace no longer exists (no state dir → no live pid possible), the ticket is unlinked and a `queue_ticket_reaped` log event is emitted. The `sweep()` return dict and `janitor_summary` log event gain a `tickets_reaped` counter.

**`tests/unit/dispatch/test_janitor.py`**: Updated two existing tests that checked the exact return dict shape (`TestEmptyRoot`, `TestMissingRoot`). Added `TestQueueTicketReaping` with four cases matching the issue's acceptance criteria:
- (a) Orphaned ticket (no workspace) → reaped
- (b) Live ticket (workspace present) → retained
- (c) After reaping the blocker, the legitimate waiting ticket is at position 0
- (d) Workspace swept to `_orphans/` and ticket reaped in the same pass

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check .` — no errors
- [x] `ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/dispatch/test_janitor.py` — 24 passed (was 20)
- [x] `pytest tests/unit -m unit` — no new failures vs main (14 pre-existing failures unchanged)

Closes #469

author: acidkill
body:
## Summary

Re-scope of #16 down to **just** the `neuron_state` record-id fix. The rest of #16 was an integration branch carrying deployment-specific code; the other atomic PRs (#17–#27) are already merged.

`add_neuron` writes the activation-state record as `neuron_state:state_<sid>`, but `get_neuron_state`, `update_neuron_state` and the delete path addressed `neuron_state:<sid>` **without** the `state_` prefix. So every `get_neuron_state` missed and returned `None`, every update/merge was a silent no-op, and the batch helpers (which delegate to these) cascaded empty. `recall → reinforce` read empty states and wrote nothing back, so `access_frequency` / `last_activated` / `activation_level` stayed at 0 and the whole **activation → decay → tiering → consolidation loop was dormant**.

## Fix

Three reader call sites now address `neuron_state:state_<sid>`, matching the writer in `add_neuron`.

## Credit

Originally reported and fixed by @RobertSigmundsson in #16; re-scoped here to the `neuron_state` change only (co-authored).

body:
# Add GraphQL API support

## Summary

Adds GraphQL support using `@nestjs/graphql` with Apollo driver (code-first approach), exposing 6 core queries while keeping existing REST endpoints fully functional.

## Changes

### New Dependencies
- `@nestjs/graphql@^12` - NestJS GraphQL module
- `@nestjs/apollo@^12` - Apollo driver for NestJS GraphQL
- `graphql@^16` - GraphQL engine
- `@apollo/server@^4` - Apollo Server

### GraphQL Module (`src/graphql/`)
- **`graphql.module.ts`** - Configures code-first GraphQL with ApolloDriver, auto-generates schema file, enables playground in non-production at `/graphql`
- **`models/creator.model.ts`** - ObjectType for Creator (id, stellarAddress, email, displayName, bio, avatarUrl, totalEarned, registeredAt, createdAt, updatedAt)
- **`models/tier.model.ts`** - ObjectType for Tier (id, onChainId, name, description, priceUsdc, durationDays, maxSupply, minted, active, creator relation, createdAt, updatedAt)
- **`models/pass.model.ts`** - ObjectType for Pass (id, onChainId, tier, creator, fan relations, purchasedAt, expiresAt, txHash, active, createdAt)
- **`models/fan.model.ts`** - ObjectType for Fan (id, stellarAddress, displayName, createdAt, updatedAt)
- **`models/pagination.model.ts`** - PaginatedCreators, PaginatedTiers, PaginatedPasses wrapper types
- **`resolvers/creators.resolver.ts`** - Queries: `creator(address: String!)`, `creators(page: Int, limit: Int)`
- **`resolvers/tiers.resolver.ts`** - Queries: `tier(creatorAddress: String!, onChainId: Int!)`, `tiers(creatorAddress: String, page: Int, limit: Int)`
- **`resolvers/passes.resolver.ts`** - Query: `pass(id: ID!)`
- **`resolvers/fans.resolver.ts`** - Query: `fan(address: String!)`
- **`resolvers/*.spec.ts`** - Unit tests for all 4 resolvers (12 tests total)

### Service Changes
- **`passes/passes.service.ts`** - Added `findById(id)` method for GraphQL pass query; injected `AdminConfigService` (fixing pre-existing missing dependency)
- **`tiers/tiers.service.ts`** - Added `findByCreatorAddressPaginated()` for GraphQL tiers query; removed duplicate `findAll` implementations; added missing `CreateTierDto` and `ForbiddenException` imports

### Module Changes
- **`app.module.ts`** - Added `GraphqlAppModule` import; fixed pre-existing middleware import reference
- **`main.ts`** - Added GraphQL playground URL log
- **`passes/passes.module.ts`** - Added `AdminModule` import for `AdminConfigService`

## Queries

```graphql
# Get a single creator by Stellar address
creator(address: "G...") {
  id, stellarAddress, displayName, bio, avatarUrl, totalEarned
}

# List creators with pagination
creators(page: 1, limit: 20) {
  data { id, stellarAddress, displayName }
  total, page, limit
}

# Get a specific tier by creator address and on-chain ID
tier(creatorAddress: "G...", onChainId: 1) {
  id, name, description, priceUsdc, durationDays, active
}

# List tiers with optional creator filter
tiers(creatorAddress: "G...", page: 1, limit: 20) {
  data { id, name, priceUsdc }
  total, page, limit
}

# Get a pass by ID
pass(id: "uuid") {
  id, onChainId, active, purchasedAt, expiresAt
  tier { name }
  creator { displayName }
  fan { stellarAddress }
}

# Get a fan by Stellar address
fan(address: "G...") {
  id, stellarAddress, displayName
}
```

## Testing
- All 12 new GraphQL resolver tests pass
- All pre-existing passing tests remain unaffected
- Playground available at `/graphql` in non-production environments
- REST endpoints unchanged and fully functional

closes #70

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

The parent entry **bezout-identity-oq-02-oq-01-oq-02** ("FTA Generalization to Euclidean Domains") asks, as its fourth open question:

> The Eisenstein criterion for irreducibility of polynomials over UFDs is a key application of the UFD framework. Is it formalized in Mathlib, and can it be used here?

Yes — and it works far beyond UFDs. Mathlib's `Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion` applies at any prime ideal of any commutative ring. This PR packages it into the clean headline theorem:

- **`irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_of_prime`** — for any **integral domain** `R`, any **prime** `p : R`, and `n ≥ 1`, `Xⁿ − p` is irreducible over `R[X]`, via Eisenstein at the prime ideal `(p)`.

Specializing the domain shows the criterion in genuinely different settings:

- **over `ℤ`**: `Yⁿ − 2` and `Yⁿ − 3` are irreducible over `ℤ[Y]`;
- **over the Euclidean domain `ℚ[X]`** (exactly the parent's theme): `Yⁿ − X` and `Y³ − X` are irreducible over `ℚ[X][Y]` — Eisenstein at the prime element `X`. Its root is an n-th root of the variable, generating the function-field extension `ℚ(X)(X^{1/n})`.

This is the `∛3` Eisenstein argument (entry **cube-root-3-irrational-oq-01**) with `ℤ` replaced by an arbitrary integral domain — the natural generality the UFD/Euclidean-domain framework invites.

## Verification

- `./proofs/scripts/docker-build.sh Proofs.BezoutIdentityOQ02OQ01OQ02OQ04` → `✔ Built`, build completed successfully.
- 108 lines, 5 theorems, **0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide** — verified.
- Self-contained: imports Mathlib only.

author: iamfootprint
body:
## Why
Makes the #143 profile-coach draft budget actually effective. The runner only touched `OpsDraftMessage` when an evaluation *carried* a draft — so a draft created on one run lingered as `PENDING_APPROVAL` forever once the agent stopped drafting for that entity (entity improved, or dropped out of the new per-run top-N budget). Without this, a run would stack the fresh capped batch *on top of* the stale drafts and the queue would never shrink.

## Fix
When an evaluation has no draft, call `store.replaceDraft(recId, null)`, which removes only `PENDING_APPROVAL` / `BLOCKED_POLICY` drafts — `APPROVED`/`SENT`/`REJECTED` are preserved. Drafts now reflect current state.

## Test
A second run with no draft clears the prior run's `PENDING_APPROVAL` draft. tsc 0 · eslint 0 · 76 ops tests green.

author: p1ng3r
body:
### Motivation

- Introduce a small, data-driven internal Hazard Deck v1 for Travel v2 so hazards can be drawn and managed by the GM without mutating game objects automatically. 
- Track hazard draw state inside Travel v2 runner sessions so pending/active/cleared hazards and drawn pressure thresholds persist through normalization and save/reopen. 
- Provide GM controls to manually activate or clear hazards while exposing only player-safe text to players via existing station card state.

### Description

- Add a compact hazard registry in `data/travel-events/travel-v2-hazard-deck.js` with clear `id`, `name`, `category`, `description`, `pressureContext`, `triggerContext`, `gmText`, and `playerText` fields. 
- Implement session-local hazard state helpers in `scripts/helpers/travel-v2-hazards.js` to normalize hazard state, draw one pending hazard per threshold (2/3/4) with duplicate-threshold guards, and set hazard status to `active`/`cleared` without side effects. 
- Wire hazard draws into the pressure application flow in `applyTravelV2PressureToRunnerSession` so threshold crossings append pending hazards to the runner session (without mutating actors/items/chat/journals/combat/sockets). 
- Persist and expose hazard state via runner session creation/normalization and surface a GM Hazard Deck panel in the Travel Event Runner UI with `Activate / Apply` and `Clear` buttons. 
- Expose only player-safe `playerText` in the player station card via the existing public state path so players never see GM-only hazard text. 
- Add smoke tests for hazards and include them in the Travel v2 smoke suite to validate threshold draws, duplicate prevention, manual activation/clearing, normalization/save-reopen persistence, safe text separation, and absence of side effects.

### Testing

- Ran static checks with `node --check scripts/apps/travel-event-runner.js` and `node --check scripts/helpers/travel-v2-dev-tools.js`, both succeeded. 
- Executed the full Travel v2 smoke suite with `node scripts/dev/run-travel-v2-smoke.mjs`, which passed and included the new `Travel v2 hazards` smoke checks. 
- Added targeted hazard smoke tests in `scripts/helpers/travel-v2-hazards.smoke.js` covering draw behavior, manual activate/clear, normalization/save-reopen, player/GM text separation, and ensuring no chat/journal/combat/socket side effects.

## Summary
As noted during the demo, the custody wallet minted an ECC + ML-DSA key on every `keygen`, so every wallet was born hybrid. That does not match the migration the PoC models: real accounts already exist with an ECC key and adopt post-quantum as a deliberate step.

- `keygen` now defaults to **ECC-only**; `--quantum` (or `--import-pq-seed`) adds the ML-DSA-44 key.

body:
Closes the last reconciliation gap: resource profiles now work for YAML jobs (`drift serve` / `job.Load`), not just the SDK.

## What
- Job spec gains an optional top-level `profile: sidecar|dedicated` field.
- `job.Load` validates it (unknown → error); `Built.Pipeline` prepends the profile's **local** options (batch/buffer/linger) so caller opts still override.
- New `sdk.ProfileByName(name)` + `Profile.PipelineOptions()` — single source of truth for the local knobs, reused by `WithProfile`. `job → sdk` is acyclic.

## Safety
Process-global knobs (`GOMAXPROCS`/`GOGC`/`GOMEMLIMIT`) are **not** applied from a job — one job must not re-tune the whole server process. For a dedicated single-job binary, use the SDK with `OwnsProcess()`.

```yaml
name: payments
profile: sidecar
source: { type: kafka, ... }
stages: [ ... ]
sink: { type: ... }
```

## Tests
- `sdk`: `ProfileByName` (incl. case-insensitive + unknown), `PipelineOptions` shape.
- `pkg/job`: valid profile loads + builds, unknown profile errors, absent profile OK.

author: masamoto1982
body:
## 概要

Ajisai に**暗黙的(自動)並列コンピューティング能力**を与えるための設計原理と段階的実装プランを `docs/dev/implicit-parallelism-roadmap.md` として起こした。Codex 向けの実装指示書であり、初期実装は Codex、最終調整は Claude が担う前提で構成している。Non-canonical 文書で、`SPECIFICATION.html` が唯一の権威であることを明記。

## 設計の核

> 同じソース・同じ結果・新しい概念ゼロ。違うのは速度だけ。

運用上の仕事モデル(空間 × 時間 × 作業者数、8割集中→2割の斥候で先行分割)をランタイムへ写した設計原理を冒頭に据え、その下に技術フェーズをぶら下げた:

- **原理I** 空間は掛け算(机を片付けよ): SoA `DenseTensor` / `Arc` CoW / 不変性
- **原理II** 空間⇔時間の交換(水位予算): 既存の step/materialization limit の上で動く
- **原理III** 着手前に仕分けよ(disjoint 動線): 静的 purity/DAG 分割で競合を消す
- **原理IV** 8割で斥候(パイプライン先行分割): runahead/ヘルパースレッド、過剰分散の禁止

## 不可侵の3契約

| 契約 | 機構 |
|---|---|
| Same Result | 厳密値ゆえ「並列==逐次」を差分 proptest で CI ゲート化 |
| Never Slower | コスト/空間ゲート + hedged レース(逐次も走者) |
| Zero Syntax | 判断材料は `purity_table` のみ。ユーザコードに現れない |

## 現状ボトルネック(コード根拠)

`Rc` の `!Send`(`types/mod.rs`)、SIMD/rayon 不在(`Cargo.toml`)、`wasm-opt = ["-Os"]`、同期子ランタイム(`child_runtime.rs`)、`Greedy` 既定(`execution_mode.rs`)。

## フェーズ

Phase 0(WASM 速度最適化・即効)→ 1(`Rc→Arc`+差分検証足場)→ 2(純粋性網羅+コスト/空間ゲート)→ 3(SIMD+rayon カーネル・本丸)→ 4(自動並列を既定化)→ 5(WASM スレッド)→ 6(パイプライン先行分割+子ランタイム並行)。Phase 7(検証/CI)は全フェーズ並走。各フェーズに Definition of Done を付与。

## ステータス

設計文書のみ。コード変更なし。実装は本ブリーフに従って後続で行う。

## 배경
main·모든 PR의 CI가 4체크 전부 red(선재). 본 트랙은 **backend·frontend CI 게이트를 실제 green으로** 만드는 인프라 수선(별도 branch `fix/ci-infra`, base `origin/main`).

## Backend (Backend pytest 게이트)
CI는 `pytest tests/`(apps/api)를 실행 — gdal 빌드 실패로 **설치 단계에서 붕괴해 한 번도 pytest까지 도달 못 함**. 층층이 드러난 3중 blocker를 전부 해소:

1. **gdal 빌드 실패** — `gdal-config` 부재. ci.yml에 `libgdal-dev` 시스템 설치 + `gdal==$(gdal-config --version)` 선설치, requirements `gdal==3.9.3`→`gdal>=3.6,<3.12`(시스템 libgdal 불일치 빌드실패 회피).
2. **eppy/bs4 ResolutionImpossible** — gdal 해소 후 표면화. `eppy`(코드 import 0·미구현 계획)가 `beautifulsoup4<=4.8.0` 강제 → langchain의 bs4 4.12.3과 충돌. eppy 제거(사유 주석).
3. **38 선재 pytest 실패**(36 fail + 2 collection error) — gdal·eppy 후 드러남. 오케스트레이션 병렬 수선(19파일). 대부분 모듈 진화 미추종 노후 테스트(molit API 호스트 이관·court_scraper HTML→JSON·cost 라우트 인증요구·celery 스케줄수 등). **2건은 실 모듈 버그를 발견·정직 수정**:
   - `auth_service.py`: `HTTPBearer(auto_error=True)`가 무인증 시 403 반환(계약·HTTP표준=401 위반) → `auto_error=False`+명시적 401. 인접 auth 165 테스트 무회귀.
   - `alris_service.py`: `__init__` OPENAI_API_KEY 무가드 ChatOpenAI 크래시 → 키 가드(llm_provider 정본 패턴).
4. **xmltodict 명시** — molit XML 1차 파서(regex 폴백 보유) 누락 보완.

## Frontend (Frontend 게이트)
`pnpm test:run` 차단 — 선재 노후 테스트 19파일(42 실패). 컴포넌트 의도적 진화에 미추종(ModuleCommandStrip 중복 "실연동"·useDictionary 로딩게이트·워크스페이스→스튜디오게이트·apiClient.getRuntimeConfig 형상변화·자가완결 로컬시뮬 전환 등). 현재 실동작에 맞게 단언 정정(무날조·컴포넌트 무수정). + tsc/eslint 정리.

## 검증 (정직)
- **backend**: CI-미러 venv(전체 requirements·무DB, CI와 동일) 전체 설치 PIP_EXIT=0 + `pytest tests/` **4062 passed 0 fail 0 error**. 모듈 ruff All checks passed.
- **frontend**: vitest 62파일·**494 passed**, tsc **0 error**, 변경 테스트 eslint clean.
- gdal 로컬(Ubuntu 3.8.4) 휠빌드·osgeo import·범위 no-op 검증.

## 정직한 범위·주의
- **Cloudflare Pages/Workers** 배포 체크: 미수정(시크릿/config — 코드 아님).
- `pyproject.toml testpaths=["../../tests"]`는 **propai-platform/tests**(별개 루트 스위트)를 가리킴 — CI는 명시 `tests/`로 apps/api/tests(4062)를 실행하므로 무관(testpaths 무시됨). 그 별개 스위트의 잔여는 본 트랙 범위 외.
- backend ruff는 CI 미게이트(pytest만). 모듈은 clean, 테스트 잔여 style은 경미.

author: cushon
body:
This PR implements a sparse transition table representation for DFA states to reduce their memory footprint.

Previously, every `State` allocated a flat `State[] next` array of size `numClasses` (the number of equivalence classes). For large programs, this flat array dominated memory usage, even though the vast majority of transitions were never computed.

This change introduces a hybrid transition table:
* **Sparse Mode ($\le 8$ transitions)**: The state uses small, packed primitive arrays (`sparseClasses` and `sparseStates`). Lookups are performed via a linear scan.
* **Inflated Mode ($> 8$ transitions)**: If a state accumulates more than 8 transitions, it inflates to a full `inflatedNext` array of size `numClasses`, copying over the existing sparse transitions and reclaiming the sparse arrays.

This hybrid approach keeps the state memory representation extremely compact for typical patterns while dynamically scaling for high-density transition states.

The impact on the benchmarks from https://github.com/eaftan/safere/pull/500 is

* **Memory Footprint**: Reduces the memory footprint per DFA state instance significantly, saving up to **1.6 KB per state** on typical patterns. This reduces heap usage and GC collection frequency.
* **Execution Performance**: Achieves an **overall geometric mean speedup of 1.07x** (7% faster) across the microbenchmark suite.
* **Trade-offs**: There is a minor regression (8–12%) on some matching loops due to the linear scan overhead when looking up sparse transitions, but this is outweighed by the overall memory savings and reduced GC overhead.

Implements #24 — air-to-water (Ecodan / FTC heat-pump) support.

- `__init__.py` — exports the ATW public API.
- `tests/test_atw.py` — 33 tests.

### Verification
- Full suite green (**162 passed**), including the new ATW tests.
- Decode verified against captured packets and **live on an FTC6 + PUZ-WM112** via the MAC-577IF `/smart` API; the generated cool-flow SET packet is **byte-identical** to one the unit accepted.

- Tested on **FTC6** only so far (FTC4/5/7 have hooks but are unverified).

author: rbisecke
body:
## What changed

- `README.md` added at repo root — 236 lines covering concept, features, architecture, AI architecture, setup, testing, CI, and status
- `screenshots/readme/` directory added with five curated PNGs: `dashboard.png`, `history.png`, `log-form.png`, `log-form-expanded.png`, `detail.png`
- `.gitignore` updated from `screenshots/` (blocks entire directory) to `screenshots/*` + `!screenshots/readme/` so the curated README assets are tracked while Playwright test artifacts remain ignored

## Why

The `screenshots/` glob was originally added to keep generated Playwright output out of git. Using `screenshots/*` instead of `screenshots/` is the standard gitignore pattern for "ignore directory contents but allow explicit subdirectories" — the parent directory can still be entered by git, and the negation `!screenshots/readme/` then takes effect. The previous `screenshots/` pattern made the entire directory opaque to git and the negation had no effect.

The README is structured for a technical audience: the hero screenshot and tagline give a 5-second concept read, the architecture and AI sections give depth for anyone who wants to understand the design, and the setup guide is written to succeed on first try with explicit gotchas documented (127.0.0.1 vs localhost, absolute pytest path, STUB_LLM requirement). Marketing language and vague capability claims are absent; every AI claim is specific to a component and a mechanism.

The AI architecture section leads with the key design decision — deterministic Python for safety logic, LLM for prose only — because that framing is what separates a credible AI integration from a "we added a chatbot" project. Each of the five components is described with the specific technique it uses (Instructor + tool-use constrained decoding, BM25 + pgvector RRF, XML-delimited context, 202+polling async pattern, rule-based safety classifier), not just what it does at a high level.

Screenshots are copied to `screenshots/readme/` with clean, permanent names rather than using the phase-labeled originals (`phase3c-*.png`) directly. Phase references are internal planning artifacts and would be confusing to anyone reading the repo without that context.

body:
## A7 — Proof-chain integrity (plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-20-all-agents-fix-plan.md`)

Three additive proof-chain fixes. **No schema or governance-behavior change** — the approval lifecycle is unchanged (a field is stamped, not a transition altered). `rank11` was already satisfied on `main`, so it is not in this PR.

> **SURFACE-before-merge.** Touches the WorkTrace approved-trace update path (rank5) and the receipt proof primitive (rank12) — both proof/work-trace globs. Human makes the merge call. AUTHORITY for this slice was autonomous-with-guardrails, downgraded to surface by the merge-stop rule.

### rank5 (P1) — stamp `approvalId` on the approved trace (PRODUCER half)
`writeApprovedPayloadToTrace` omitted `approvalId`, so the approved `WorkTrace` never carried it. Now stamps `approvalId = lifecycle.id` (both the parked and legacy-row approval forks share this function). `approvalId` is a one-shot trace field, `undefined` on the parked path until this write, so first-set is allowed and a retry with the same id is idempotent (`work-trace-lock.ts`) — exactly like the `approval*` fields already written here. Verified it can never make a previously-OK update start failing.

> ⚠️ **Surfaced in review — a SEPARATE, PRE-EXISTING defect blocks the end-to-end proof link (recommend follow-up "A7b", NOT fixed here).** The receipted-booking view's workTrace leg (`traceId` / `matchedPolicies` / `humanApprovalId`) returns `null` for **all** bookings today, because the consumer joins `WorkTrace` by primary-key `id` (`prisma-receipted-booking-store.ts:137`) while producers store a **non-`id`** value into `Booking.workTraceId` (`calendar-book.ts:360` → `workUnitId`; `riley-budget-executor.ts:32` → `traceId`). `WorkTrace.id` is `@default(cuid())`, distinct from `workUnitId` (`@unique`) and `traceId`. This is pre-existing on `main` (confirmed via `git show`). The plan scoped rank5 as *"MOOT today, assert the TRACE field not the receipt"* — so this PR lands the necessary **producer groundwork** (the stamp) and asserts the trace field. Reconciling `Booking.workTraceId` + the consumer join needs a canonical-id decision + a backfill, which is its own slice.

### rank12 (P2) — inverse receipt transition on `no_show`
An `attended` → `no_show` correction left the calendar receipt at `held`, overstating attendance. Adds `PrismaReceiptStore.demoteCalendarHeldToBooked` (org-scoped inverse of `promoteCalendarBookedToHeld`), called by the `record_attendance` handler on `no_show` (fail-loud, symmetric with promote; the `{count:0}` no-op is intended, mirroring promote).

### rank19 (P2) — assemble the receipted-booking cohort once
The quality and revenue report dimensions each assembled the cohort independently (duplicate N+1 `getView` fan-out, two snapshots). `period-rollup` now assembles it **once** via a shared promise and threads the views into both compute fns — the fan-out runs once and both dimensions share one snapshot. Behavior-preserving (neither dimension reads a `now`-dependent field); the shared promise keeps the assembly concurrent with the other rollup legs.

### rank11 (P2) — already done on `main` (no change)
The Receipt partial-unique is already mirror-commented in `schema.prisma` (equivalent to the `LifecycleRevenueEvent` convention) and its dedup behavior is already tested in `prisma-receipt-store.test.ts`. No no-Postgres index-existence assertion was invented.

## Verification
All RED→GREEN (tests written first, watched fail for the right reason). Gates: **typecheck / lint / format / arch / verify-fast / security / build(10/10)** all green. Full `pnpm test`: the only failures are 4 `@switchboard/chat` `gateway-bridge-attribution` tests — the documented *"attribution flakes under load"* flake (pass 4/4 isolated; my diff is disjoint from chat's attribution surface). No schema change → no drift check; no decision-engine change → no eval. Disjoint from open PR #782 (that guards `buildWorkTrace` construction; this changes the `WorkTraceStore.update` path).

An independent fresh-context review returned the rank5 end-to-end finding above (triaged: real but pre-existing + out-of-scope) and confirmed rank12 + rank19 ship-clean.

**Closes the engine loop.** A case study can now be **auto-scored → editor-approved → into the Index** — without losing the human gate that the Index's credibility depends on.

## What's new
- **`lib/score-case-study.ts`** — `draftDecode(caseStudy)` proposes the four-axis decode (IDEA / AUTHORSHIP / EXECUTION / CONSEQUENCE, 1–5 + a note) and a rationale from the case study's own evidence (context / strategicBet / creativeMove / africanRead / evidence), via `MODELS.editorial`. body:
I know you're investigating too, but I pointed Claude at the problem, instructing to fix the issue with solution that is adaptive with negligible overhead.

> Tinfour's in-circle (Delaunay) predicate decided whether to fall back to its existing exact quad-precision path using a static, absolute threshold (inCircleThreshold) derived from the nominal point spacing (≈ 5.96e-8 for the default constructor). With the issue's large-magnitude coordinates (~3.2e7), the determinant's floating-point round-off error vastly exceeds that threshold, so a wrong-signed fast result was trusted instead of escalating. Inconsistent predicate results produced a non-star-shaped insertion cavity, so the cavity-construction loop's only exit (c.getB() == anchor) was never reached — an infinite loop.

body:
## What this slice fixes
An xhigh GPT-5 whole-feature review found one gap in the slice-1 signal: `classifyModelOutcome` checked parse-success *before* `finish_reason`, so a window where the model hit `max_tokens` (finish_reason "length") but whose JSON still happened to parse was treated as fully clean and never flagged degraded - exactly the incomplete-detection-masquerading-as-clean case the feature exists to catch.

## The fix (cut set byte-identical)
A truncated-but-parsed window's ads were genuinely detected, so we still apply them. `classifyModelOutcome` returns `{ ok:true, parsed, truncated:true }` for that case; `detectAds` uses the ads AND records a new `windowsTruncated` counter + folds "truncated" into `failureReasons`. `windowsFailed` keeps its meaning (windows skipped with no usable ads); `degraded = windowsFailed > 0 || windowsTruncated > 0`. The truncated note fires *after* the wrong-shape parse-error skip, so a truncated-but-unusable window stays a parse-error. The failure-path truncated (parsed null + length) is unchanged.

## Cardinal rule
Purely informational - no cut added, removed, or altered. Proven by a byte-equal baseline test (`toStrictEqual` + `JSON.stringify`) and the still-green SLICE 1 behaviour-neutral block. No `sync.cjs` change needed - `degradeFromStats` already propagates `stats.degraded`. Detector locked.

## Problem
A code-review **tertiary reviewer failed to start ("powershell path too long")** when the reviewer CLI was grok. The review feature hands each reviewer the full adversarial brief; grok receives it on **argv** (`grok -p "<brief>"`), and a large brief blows the Windows command-line cap.

claude/codex/gemini don't hit this because their builders route the prompt through **stdin** (`stdinPrompt`). grok's headless mode can't read piped stdin — but it reads **`--prompt-file <PATH>`**.

## Fix
`StartSession` rewrites grok's trailing `-p <prompt>` → `--prompt-file <tempfile>` (`rewriteGrokPromptToFile`), so only a short path is on argv regardless of brief size. The temp file (0600) is removed in `waitForExit` **after** the process exits. `buildGrokInteractiveArgs` and its tests are untouched; best-effort fallback to `-p` on any temp-file error.

## Validated
- Live: `grok --output-format streaming-json --no-auto-update --always-approve --prompt-file <file>` runs the prompt and exits 0.
- New `rewriteGrokPromptToFile` tests (happy path, no-`-p` carve-out, byte-exact 80KB/multi-line preservation) pass; `go build`/`vet`/`gofmt`/tests green. Version v0.10.11 → **v0.10.12**.

Follow-up to the interactive-grok work. (Note: the grok **ACP** path is unaffected — this is the headless terminal-session path used by reviewers.)

author: onpaj
body:
## What the issue was

`KnowledgeBaseRepository.GetFeedbackStatsAsync` executed four separate database round-trips to compute a single aggregate result: `CountAsync` for total rows, `CountAsync` with a predicate for rows with feedback, and two filtered `AverageAsync` calls. On every admin feedback page load this added 4 full-table aggregation queries on top of the 2 pagination queries, totalling 6 round-trips per request. As `KnowledgeBaseQuestionLogs` grows unboundedly, this scales at O(4 × N).

## How it was fixed / handled

Replaced the four `CountAsync`/`AverageAsync` calls with a single `GroupBy(_ => 1)` LINQ projection that EF Core translates to one SQL aggregation query. The same pattern is already used in `ArticleRepository.GetFeedbackStatsAsync`. The empty-table edge case is handled by returning zeros/nulls when `FirstOrDefaultAsync` returns `null`.

The existing integration tests in `KnowledgeBaseRepositoryIntegrationTests` cover all cases including:
- Empty table → zeros and null averages
- Rows without scores → correct counts and null averages
- Mixed feedback → correct counts and rounded averages
- SQL shape verification (single `COUNT`/`AVG` query, no row materialisation)

### Motivation

- External finality signatures for default routes and context packets previously signed only a subset of record fields, omitting acceptance/validation-critical state and enabling replay-based acceptance bypasses. 
- The change ensures the external approval payload cryptographically binds every field that affects readiness/acceptance so the gateway cannot accept a record that the external authority did not actually approve.

### Description

- Expanded the canonical default-route approval material to include readiness/acceptance fields (`status`, `route_source`, `policy_allowed`, `freshness_status`, `invalidated`, `production_default_route_approval_status`, `packet_quality_review_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) and wired them into `canonical_default_route_approval_payload_hash` (file: `crates/exo-dag-db-domain/src/default_route.rs`).
- Expanded the canonical context-packet approval material to include validation/acceptance fields (`context_quality`, `citation_coverage_bp`, `validation_coverage_bp`, `freshness_status`, `validation_status`, `fallback_reason`, `persistence_status`, `production_default_route_approval_status`, `packet_quality_review_status`, `created_at`) and wired them into `canonical_context_packet_approval_payload_hash` (file: `crates/exo-dag-db-domain/src/context_packet_persistence.rs`).
- Added regression tests that mutate omitted acceptance-critical fields and assert the canonical hashes differ, proving the finality payload now binds the full acceptance state (file: `crates/exo-dag-db-domain/tests/prd17_default_retrieval_contract.rs`).
- Adjusted test acceptance-evidence helpers to generate payloads bound to the deferred route/packet state used in graduation tests, and adapted expectations where appropriate.

author: rfizzle
body:
## Summary

Fills the tier-ability gap for the nine scaled mobs that previously had only stat scaling — **Stray, Bogged, Witch, Pillager, Vindicator, Guardian, Ravager, Silverfish, Endermite**. Every ability uses only vanilla mechanics and follows the existing `AbilityManager` pattern: a tier guard, an `abilities.*` config toggle (default on, hot-reloadable), and one of the established application mechanisms (scoreboard tag read by a narrow mixin, held-item enchantment, or a Fabric event hook).

| Mob | Tier | Ability | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stray | 2 | Slowness II arrows | `getArrow` mixin re-adds effect at amp 1 |
| Bogged | 2 | Poison II arrows | `getArrow` mixin re-adds effect at amp 1 |
| Witch | 3 | Lingering potions | `@Redirect` `SPLASH_POTION` → `LINGERING_POTION` |
| Witch | 5 | Aggressive self-healing | `@ModifyConstant` on the `aiStep` heal-roll chance |
| Pillager | 2 | Quick Charge crossbow | held-item enchant |
| Pillager | 4 | Multishot crossbow | held-item enchant |
| Vindicator | 3 | Door breaking (any difficulty) | `BreakDoorGoal.isValidDifficulty` tag relax |
| Guardian | 3 | Faster beam charge | `getAttackDuration` mixin |
| Ravager | 3 | Wider roar knockback radius | `@ModifyConstant` on the roar AABB radius |
| Silverfish / Endermite | 2 | Call silverfish from infested blocks when hurt | `AFTER_DAMAGE` handler (Endermite); vanilla for Silverfish |

New abilities surface in `/tribulation inspect` and the Jade/WTHIT probe tooltips through a shared `MobScalingDataCollector.describeAbilities` accessor (the inspect command previously showed only attribute modifiers).

## Spec corrections

Two of the spec's "open questions" were deferred on premises that turned out to be wrong; both are implemented here:

- **Witch T5 healing** — the spec deferred this citing a fragile `Witch$WitchGoal` inner class. That class does not exist; the drink logic is inline in `Witch.aiStep`, where the heal-trigger probability is a single `0.05f` constant — cleanly modified via `@ModifyConstant`, no inner class involved.
- **Endermite call-sleepers** — the spec named `ServerLivingEntityEvents.AFTER_DAMAGE`. That event does exist in the bundled Fabric API (1.8.0) and is used as written. (Guardian's faster beam also avoids the spec's fragile `Guardian$GuardianAttackGoal` inner-class mixin by hooking the public `getAttackDuration` instead.)

## Testing

- `./gradlew build` — green (unit tests pass; `AbilityManagerTest` toggle count 19 → 29).
- `./gradlew runGametest` — **81 tests pass**, including new `AbilitiesGameTest` coverage for arrow upgrades (Stray/Bogged), crossbow enchants (Pillager Quick Charge T2 / Multishot T4), the door-breaking difficulty gate (Vindicator), the Endermite infested-block summon, and spawn tests that force the Witch/Ravager/Guardian mixins to apply and validate their injection points. Each ability is asserted both enabled and disabled to prove the config toggle gates it.

## Docs

`site/pages/features.json` (tier table) and `site/pages/config.json` (per-mob toggle list) updated for all ten new toggles.

Closes #51

author: ogoffart
body:
The safety-net timeout that releases the first windows if the XDG portal is slow was armed in bind_context, with its deadline anchored to that moment. An app doing heavy synchronous work before running the event loop (the viewer compiling a .slint file) could burn the whole timeout before the portal query, which only runs on the event loop, had a chance to answer. The windows were then shown with the default accent color and font.

Arm the timer at the top of the watch task instead, so it counts from when the portal query can actually make progress.

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**

- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).
