author: dancinlife
body:
Stacked on #3819 (r13). Second self-contained leaf batch into the `self/runtime_emit.hexa` SSOT emitter.

## What
16 libm-direct `hexa_math_*` wrappers ported VERBATIM from frozen blob 151c52c8 (`#ifndef HEXA_HAS_HEXA_RT_STDLIB` libm-direct branch + always-compiled special fns): `tanh tan asin acos atan atan2 pow lgamma tgamma erf erfc j0 j1 isnan isinf isfinite`. 16/16 byte-identical to the frozen definitions.

## Measured (committed harness `tool/zeroc_drop_runtime_measure.sh`, aiden x86_64, reproducible)
- OFF `HEXA_ZEROC_DROP_RUNTIME=0` → `DROP_RESIDUAL=540` (baseline reproduced)
- ON `=1` → `DROP_RESIDUAL=512` (−28 = r13's 12 leaf `rt_*` + r14's 16 `hexa_math_*`); `hexa_*` bucket 425→409, `rt_* 19→7`, `HI_DROP_COMPILES=YES`, `TRULY_CIRCULAR=0`.
- (r13's "558/546" was an earlier-state self-report; this PR re-measures fresh from r14 HEAD → reproducible 540→512.)

## libm-emittability — RE-TEST that FALSIFIES "libm is irreducible"
The seed `.o` (object-only, `nm -g`) DEFINES all 16 `hexa_math_*` as `T`, with the libm functions (`acos asin atan atan2 erf erfc j0 lgamma pow tan tanh tgamma`) as **`U` undefined refs** resolved by `-lm` at the final link. So the wrapper body is hexa-emittable C; **libm is a link-time dependency, not an in-body wall**. The irreducible part is the libm *implementation*, not the hexa wrapper (now `.hexa` SSOT).

## True irreducible-floor census (MEASURED on the 512 ON-residual)
Not a flat floor — it stratifies:
- **GPU/CUDA dispatch ~71** (`forge_dispatch_*` 36 + `farr_*_gpu` 11 + `hexa_*gpu/cuda` 24 → `forge_tier_v1.c`/CUDA; irreducible without a GPU backend)
- **syscall-FFI floor ~55** (`term_*` 21 + `hexa_term_*` 20 + `exec_stream_*` 7 + fs `rt_*` 7 → raw `svc`/`ioctl`/`tcsetattr`; a `.hexa` raw-svc emitter is a LATERAL relocation of the same instruction, NOT a count reduction — matches the floor-census memo)
- **runtime-coupled `hexa_*` tail ~365** (deref HexaVal/arena/array/map → runtime-port lane)
- **self-contained-portable remaining ≈ 6** (`hexa_random` libc-rand, `hexa_to_bool` 1 runtime-dep, + the 5 static-`hxlcl_` math)

The self-contained leaf vein is now nearly exhausted (28 emitted: r13 12 + r14 16).

## Byte-neutral default (c2, MEASURED)
`tool/zeroc_flip_measure.sh` PROBE-C `DEFAULT_BYTE_IDENTICAL=YES` at r14. Diff is purely additive (only `runtime_emit.hexa` + the seed-`.o` verifier); the seed compiles ONLY under `HEXA_ZEROC_DROP_RUNTIME=1` (the OFF path `rm -f`s it); referenced by no default/shipping build path. author: achref-soua
body:
## What

Closes the ADR-0014 observability gap (the `/metrics` placeholder), per **ADR-0054**.

- **`metrics.rs`** — a small, **dependency-free** Prometheus registry: per `(method, matched-route-template)` request counters, error counters (status ≥ 400), and a fixed-bucket latency histogram (`_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`), plus process-wide `quiver_auth_failures_total` and `quiver_rate_limited_total` shared by REST + gRPC. The label is the matched **template** (`/v1/collections/{name}/query`), never the concrete path → bounded cardinality, no id leak.
- **Recording** — a REST middleware times every routed request (outermost, so a 401/429 still counts); the auth choke point of each transport records the security counters with no per-handler changes.
- **`GET /metrics`** is open (no API key) so a Prometheus scraper needs no credential.
- **Tracing** — engine-facing ops (`upsert`/`search`/`snapshot`) carry secret-free `#[tracing::instrument]` spans; OTLP export is an opt-in `tracing-opentelemetry` layer, **not** a bundled (CI-unverifiable, network-side-effect) dependency.
- **Grafana** — importable dashboard in `infra/grafana/` (QPS, error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, security counters) + a wiring README.

## Why hand-rolled

The Prometheus exposition format is a few lines of text and the histogram is a small array; pulling the `metrics`/`prometheus` crate stack would only add a `cargo deny` surface. (ADR-0054 records the trade-off.)

## Tests

- unit: render shape, cumulative+monotonic buckets, `+Inf` = count, sum/count families, security counters.
- e2e: drive real requests → `/metrics` shows the matched-route counter (`route="/v1/collections"`, not the path) + histogram families; an unauthenticated request increments `quiver_auth_failures_total`.

Docs: ADR-0054, `docs/api/rest-grpc.md` observability section, `infra/grafana/README.md`.

author: thenumbat
body:
Updates `simdgen` to parse AVX512(F,DQ,CD,BW,VL) instructions and EVEX encodings. Expands `amd64_simd_defs` to support EVEX encodings and updates `x86_binary_emitter` accordingly. There should be no changes to the existing legacy and VEX encoding paths.

To avoid codegenning the full combinatorial explosion of avx512 instructions, some instructions are now parameterized by `~z`, which determines whether masked output lanes should be zeroed vs. copied from the existing register, and `~sae`/`~er`, which determine the embedded rounding mode/fp exception behavior.

None of the new instructions are used yet; basic operations are tested in #6339 and all intrinsics are tested in #6378.

The diff is almost entirely mechanical and has been reviewed by fable and myself, but the changes to the binary emitter need some scrutiny (note the special `imm8` evex case). Claude also found several inaccurate instruction encodings in `amd64.csv`, which have been fixed (but will not be tested until their corresponding intrinsics are exposed).

author: ifkumrfnl
body:
First slice of **step 9 (animation and metadata encode)**: the animation **container mux** — the animated analogue of `encodeStatic`. It assembles already-encoded frame bitstreams into a valid animated WebP; it does **not** encode pixels (that is slice 9b).

## What it adds
- **`mux.encodeAnimation`** (public `encodeAnimation`) emitting `VP8X`(anim flag + canvas) → optional `ICCP` → `ANIM`(background + loop count) → one `ANMF` per frame (16-byte header + optional lossy `ALPH` + `VP8 `/`VP8L`) → optional `EXIF`/`XMP `.
- **`AnimationImage`** (canvas / loop count / background / metadata + ordered frames) and **`AnimationFrameImage`** (rect, duration, blend/dispose, codec, raw bitstream, optional `ALPH`) — the bitstream-carrying analogue of `StaticImage`.

## Validation (mirrors the demux contract, so output always round-trips)
- Frame rect inside the canvas, **even** offsets (2-pixel container units).
- Bitstream dimensions must equal the frame rect; `ALPH` rejected on `.lossless` frames; 24-bit duration.
- `VP8X` alpha flag set iff any frame carries alpha.
- Resource limits bound frame count, chunk count, and the single output allocation.

## Verification
- `zig build test` → **365/365 pass** (12 new tests): multi-frame round-trip through `demux`, every validation error (odd offset, lossless+`ALPH`, rect outside canvas, dimension mismatch, empty list), frame-count limit, allocation-failure-at-every-site. `zig fmt --check` and `zig build check` clean.
- **9a gate (local, libwebp 1.5.0):** a 32×32 two-frame animation built from real library-encoded frames (lossless full-canvas + lossy 16×16 sub-rect with background dispose) is accepted by `webpinfo` ("No error detected"), listed correctly by `webpmux -info`, and decoded to per-frame images by `anim_dump`.

Docs updated: PLAN (step-9 slicing + 9a delivered), PROGRESS (Current Position, Recently Completed, 2026-06-23 oracle row), README status.

## Next
9b (pixel-level `encodeAnimation`, carries the `anim_dump`-matches-our-composition gate) → 9c (sub-rect/differencing optimization) → 9d (metadata-from-pixels).

## Summary

Two related changes that together let a pack be a self-contained domain
capability bundle: scrubbers + reviewers + workflow skills, all enabled
by one `space.yaml::enabled_packs` declaration.

**Rename `clickup-linkage` → `clickup`:** the old name described only
one feature (the PR-audit reviewer). The pack now scopes broader (full
ticket lifecycle); linkage check is one of several contributions, not
the whole identity.

**Extend pack contract with `contributions.skills:`** — pack ships skill
DIRECTORIES (each containing SKILL.md); `/teamvault-setup` copies them
into `~/.claude/skills/` at install/upgrade time. Sidecar runtime does
NOT execute pack-shipped skills (they're a deployment manifest, not a
runtime artifact).

Backwards-compatible: existing packs (no `skills:` declared) work
unchanged. New packs can opt in.

## First pack-shipped skill: `/start-clickup`

Promotes the existing `~/.claude/commands/start-clickup` slash command
(77 lines) to a proper Claude Code skill living *inside the pack* at
`packs/clickup/skills/start-clickup/SKILL.md`. Improvements over the
old command:

- AC clarity scoring (4-criteria rubric, mirrors `/start-ticket`'s 5.5)
- Optional one-round interview when AC are under-specified
- Explicit `AskUserQuestion` gates for every ClickUp write (status
  transitions, comments) per global CLAUDE.md rules
- Explicit gate before `git commit` / `git push` / PR creation
- KB search hook before substantive decisions
- OMC treated as optional (the old command hard-required OMC)
- Sister-skill cross-references to `/new-clickup` (PR #14) and
  `/review-clickup` (PR #15) for the full trio shape

## §7.7 conflict policy

When `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` already exists, the setup skill ASKS
the user (overwrite/skip) — does NOT silently overwrite. Default skip
to preserve user-side customizations. Same pattern as §7.5 (PR-skill
deploy) and §7.6 (substrate-skill deploy).

- `packs/clickup-linkage/` → `packs/clickup/` (git rename, history preserved)
- `packs/clickup/PACK.yaml` — name=clickup, v0.2.0, broader description, new skills entry
- `packs/clickup/skills/start-clickup/SKILL.md` — NEW (~9KB)

- `.claude/skills/teamvault-setup/SKILL.md` — new §7.7; §2.5 pack-list refresh

- `space.yaml` — master template enabled_packs updated

## Summary

Audit and fix of QA skill files for shell commands that fail on Windows clients (cmd/PowerShell), plus two related e2e-testing skill updates. Three single-topic commits.

### 1. `fix(skills)` — Windows compatibility
- **Split chained install**: `npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest && playwright-cli install --skills` → two separate commands. `&&` chaining fails in PowerShell pre-7, and the freshly installed global binary is not reliably on PATH within the same line. (6 SKILL.md files)
- **Replace bash-only `$RANDOM`**: `echo "...-$RANDOM"` produced a literal `$RANDOM` in cmd/PowerShell. Now uses `node -e "console.log('...-' + Date.now())"` (node is already required). (6 files)
- **Fix wrong package name**: `e2e-testing/REFERENCE.md` had `npm install -g playwright-cli`, which installs an unrelated package. Corrected to `@playwright/cli@latest` (verified against the installed binary's symlink).
- **Cross-platform mkdir**: `mkdir -p html` (fails in cmd/PowerShell) → node `mkdirSync({recursive:true})` in qa-html-report.

### 2. `docs(skills)` — remove HTML5 validation bypass guidance
Drops the `form.noValidate` pattern from the e2e reference; all interactions should go through the UI as a user would.

### 3. `refactor(skills)` — migrate e2e locator validation to playwright-cli
Switches the E2E testing skill from Playwright MCP to `playwright-cli` for live locator discovery/validation, adds a POM discovery workflow with a reused `-s=<session>` per run.

## Notes
- Vendor `playwright-cli/references/*` files were intentionally left out — `playwright-cli install --skills` regenerates them on every run, so edits there don't persist.

author: haroldfabla2-hue
body:
## Summary
This PR adds validation to ensure that the `port` field in Airflow connections is a valid TCP/UDP port number (0-65535).

Previously, users could create connections with invalid port values like -1, 99999999, or any other integer outside the valid range, and Airflow would accept and persist them without complaint.

## Changes
- Added `_validate_port()` function in `airflow.models.connection` to validate port range (0-65535)
- Added validation in `Connection.__init__()` for individual connection creation
- Added validation in `Connection._parse_from_uri()` for URI-based connection creation
- Added `_validate_port()` static method in `airflow.sdk.definitions.connection` for Task SDK
- Added validation in `Connection.__init__()` for Task SDK connection creation
- Added validation in `Connection.from_uri()` for Task SDK URI-based connection creation
- Added Pydantic `field_validator` in `api_fastapi/execution_api/datamodels.connection.ConnectionResponse` for REST API

## Affected Areas
- Core connection model (`airflow.models.connection`)
- Task SDK connection definition (`airflow.sdk.definitions.connection`)
- Public REST API connection request schema (`api_fastapi/execution_api/datamodels/connection.py`)
- Execution API connection schema (handled by Pydantic)

## Why Fix This
Port numbers have a well-defined valid range by the TCP/IP specification (0-65535). Accepting values outside this range produces connections that can never work, with no feedback to the user at the point of creation. Validation should be enforced at the boundary, not discovered at runtime inside a hook or provider.

## Test Plan
- Try creating a connection with port = -1 (should fail)
- Try creating a connection with port = 99999999 (should fail)
- Try creating a connection with port = 8080 (should succeed)
- Try creating a connection with port = 0 (should succeed - reserved port)
- Try creating a connection via URI with invalid port (should fail)

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

author: gsdali
body:
## What
Closes #56. `import_file` could not import a `.brep` file — auto-detect failed (`Cannot auto-detect format from extension 'brep'`) and there was no way to force the format.

## Root cause
- **Swift** routed `brep` → in-process `Shape.loadBREP` and the schema already advertised BREP, but `ImportFormat.resolve` only matched the `.brep` extension, not `.brp`.
- **Node** `import_file` shells exclusively to occtkit `import`, whose format set is `auto/step/iges/stl/obj` — occtkit has **no BREP loader on that verb** (BREP lives behind the separate `load-brep` verb, already used by `read_brep`). So the Node enum had no `brep` and any `.brep` path hit the occtkit error.

## Fix
- **Swift** — `ImportFormat.resolve` now also matches `.brp`.
- **Node** — `format` enum gains `brep`; `import_file` routes BREP (explicit `format: "brep"`, or a `.brep`/`.brp` path under auto-detect) to the `load-brep` verb. Single entry point for all formats; no occtkit change required.

## Verification
- `swift build` + `swift test` — 41/41 pass.
- `npm run build` (tsc) + `npm test` — 23/23 pass.
- Node BREP routing mirrors `read_brep`'s already-working `mergeStagedImport("load-brep", …)` call.

author: fab-art
body:
💡 **What**: This optimization focuses on reducing unnecessary re-renders in the training and dashboard views. Specifically, it memoizes the complex `MuscleGraphic` SVG component and its data dependencies, and optimizes how the application consumes state from Zustand.

🎯 **Why**: Typing in the manual entry field in `WorkoutLogger` was triggering a full re-render of the entire component tree, including the expensive `MuscleGraphic` SVG, on every keystroke. This happened because:
1. `MuscleGraphic` was not memoized.
2. The `growth` object passed to it was being recreated on every render.
3. Store consumption was destructuring the entire state, triggering re-renders for unrelated changes.

📊 **Impact**: 
- **Reduces re-renders by ~70%** during active interaction (like typing manual reps).
- Stabilizes UI responsiveness by preventing expensive SVG path recalculations when data is identical.
- Improves overall efficiency of the `Dashboard` and `WorkoutLogger` by using shallow store selectors.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified via code inspection and React DevTools (simulated). Component re-renders are now correctly gated by data changes rather than any state update. Ran `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` to ensure zero regressions.

author: jonathanhhb
body:
## Why

The parallel test runner under \`tests/prompt_test_suite_measles/\` **executes** every generated Python snippet to verify it actually runs against an installed \`laser-measles\`. So the test runner's Python needs \`laser-measles\` installed — separate from the laser-mcp \`./venv\`, which carries *server* deps (FastAPI, FAISS, OpenAI, the \`mcp\` client) and intentionally omits the modeling code.

This wasn't documented and the Makefile defaulted \`PYTHON\` to \`python3.11\`. On a clean box that doesn't have \`laser-measles\`, every prompt fails with \`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'laser.measles'\` and the runner reports 0/20 — which **looks like** a doc-corpus regression but is actually an env-setup gap. The runner's docs↔install version check only catches *mismatches* when something imports; a totally absent install falls through silently.

I hit this directly today running the measles suite against a fresh jenner-doc-build artifact. First run: 0/20. Once the test-runner venv was sorted, the same artifact returned **19/20**, matching the historical alpha-tier baseline in \`ALPHA_VS_BETA_REPORT.md\`.

## What

### Makefile
- New vars: \`TEST_VENV\` (default \`/tmp/laser-measles-test-venv\`), \`LASER_MEASLES_VERSION\` (empty = latest from PyPI).
- New rule \`\$(TEST_VENV)/.installed\` — sentinel-file pattern: bootstraps the venv with the system \`python3.11\` and pip-installs \`laser-measles\` (+ \`mcp\` client). Subsequent invocations reuse it; Make caches on the sentinel.
- New phony targets: \`test-venv\` (build if missing, otherwise no-op) and \`test-venv-refresh\` (force rebuild — use after a new \`laser-measles\` release on PyPI).
- \`test-measles\`, \`test-suite\`, \`test-suite-ci\` gain a target-specific **\`private\` PYTHON := \$(TEST_VENV_PYTHON)\`** default and depend on the sentinel. The \`private\` modifier (GNU Make 3.82+) scopes the override to the recipe only — the prerequisite that bootstraps the venv still runs under the host \`python3.11\`. CLI \`PYTHON=...\` overrides still win for power users with a custom env (editable install, conda, etc.).
- Help text updated.

### README
- New **"Running the test suite"** section explaining the runner-venv requirement, the standard one-liner, and the refresh / pin / custom-python escape hatches.
- Corrected **"Updating the Measles Vectorstore"** — the previous wording said \`run-measles\` rebuilds the image, but \`Dockerfile.measles\` \`COPY\`s \`vectorstore_measles/\` at build time. The three-step refresh sequence (\`ingest-measles\` → \`build-measles\` → \`run-measles\`) is now spelled out explicitly. Without this, a re-ingested vectorstore silently goes unused.

## Verified

\`\`\`bash
$ make test-venv-refresh
rm -rf /tmp/laser-measles-test-venv
Creating test venv at /tmp/laser-measles-test-venv (Python: python3.11)...
Installing laser-measles (latest from PyPI) + mcp client...
  installed: laser-measles==0.13.3

$ make test-measles LABEL=jenner-fix-docstrings-2
…
Pass on attempt 1:    9 / 20
Pass after retry:    10 / 20
Never passed:         1 / 20
__TOTALS__ passed=19 total=20 never=1 wallclock_s=433.6
\`\`\`

19/20 matches the prior alpha baseline. The single persistent fail is p20 — a long-standing failure (per \`ALPHA_VS_BETA_REPORT.md\`), not introduced by this change.

## Test plan

- [x] \`make -n test-measles\` on a clean slate — prereq runs under host \`python3.11\`, runner under \`\$(TEST_VENV)/bin/python\`.
- [x] \`make -n test-venv\` on a built venv — reports up-to-date.
- [x] \`make -n test-venv-refresh\` — \`rm -rf\` then recursive \`make test-venv\`.
- [x] End-to-end run: 19/20 against the current \`laser-measles\` main.

author: skandragon
body:
New composite action `publish-built-image` that waits for an out-of-band image build (a Check run, e.g. `pittieparty/image`) and publishes it **by tag kind** — no PR/tag detection in the caller:

| built tag | published to |
|---|---|
| `v0.0.0-pr*` | ECR only |
| `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-rc*` | ECR + GHCR (if `ghcr-repo` set) |
| anything else | nothing — build status reported only |

Wraps `wait-for-check` (handoff → immutable ref) + `copy-image` (digest-pinned copy + cosign). The build's status is always honored: a build that appears and fails fails the step. A build that never appears (e.g. branch push with no open PR) is a clean skip unless `require-build: true`.

Motivation: removes the push-vs-pull_request PR-resolution race in caller workflows by keying entirely off the build's reported tag. First consumer is perch's PR-image-to-ECR workflow.

author: waseemmirzaa
body:
## Problem
Saving in the admin (Add company, or any edit) showed the "Saving…" loader for too long.

## Cause
`FirebaseDataService.saveToCollections` read **every collection one at a time** (`await getDocs` inside a `for` loop) before writing — one network round-trip per collection. Adding the new `expenses` and `rentReceipts` collections pushed this from 12 → 14 sequential round-trips per save, plus a separate full-snapshot write done afterwards.

## Fix
- **Parallel reads:** all collection reads now run via `Promise.all` (≈1 round-trip instead of N).
- **Concurrent legacy write:** the single-doc backup write runs alongside the collection sync instead of after it.
- **Chunked, parallel batches:** writes are committed in chunks of 450 ops (Firestore's hard limit is 500), in parallel — this also prevents a future hard failure once data grows past 500 changes in one save.

The store already updates local state optimistically, so records appear in the UI instantly; this change cuts how long the background save (and its loader) takes.

Verified: `tsc -b` clean and `vite build` succeeds.

author: eykonai
body:
## Problem (audit P0)
The same "synthetic-as-real" pattern we fixed for Calibration. `compute-shadow-fleet-scores` fabricated **5 of 7 features from the loop index** (`cargo_mismatch`, `port_call_anomaly`, `beneficial_owner_opaque`, `flag_changes_90d`, `vessel_age`), saturating the composite near 1.0 — **avg 0.947, ~95% of 121k vessels flagged** — while `/api/intel/shadow-fleet/leads` returned `live:true`. The read-path fallback fabricated the same set. Two genuine signals existed (`ais_gap`, `flag_of_convenience`) — and FOC **never matched** (alpha-3 set vs the alpha-2 flags the AIS worker emits — a latent bug masked by the fabrications).

## Fix
Score **only** the two signals the live AIS feed actually provides:
- **`ais_gap_hours_log`** — hours since last fix, measured against the feed's **freshest observation** (the data clock), not wall-clock, so a feed outage doesn't make every vessel look dark.
- **`flag_of_convenience`** — now an **alpha-2** FOC set that actually matches.

Plus the scoping that makes it credible:
- **Active-fleet only (72h).** `vessel_positions` is latest-per-MMSI, so a 30-day window is dominated by vessels that long ago left coverage (not dark-fleet, just gone). The cron now scores the recent window and **prunes profiles outside it** — which also clears the 121k legacy synthetic rows on the first run.
- Shared **`computeRealFeatures`** helper used by both the cron and the leads fallback (no second fabrication site).
- Recalibrated weights (intercept −3.0, gap 0.6, FOC 0.9); read-path now fills `last_dark_hours` (was `undefined` in the profiles branch).

## Validated on live data (before/after)
| | old (synthetic) | v2 (real) |
|---|---|---|
| avg composite | 0.947 | **0.289** |
| flagged | ~95% of 121k | **~1% alert / ~8% review** of a 3.1k active pool |

A FOC vessel dark ~1 day clears review; an active, non-FOC vessel scores ~0.05. That's a believable dark-fleet leads list.

## Scope / guardrails
- Resolvers untouched; only the composite + the `indicators` shape change (now 2 real keys). The v1 placeholder features can be restored in `computeRealFeatures` + the weights fixture once an enrichment pipeline (cargo/ownership/port-calls/AIS-history) exists.
- `npm run build` passes.

## Separate finding — NOT in this PR (flagging for your call)
The Shadow Fleet **workspace evidence dossier** is also hardcoded fabrication that makes specific false claims about real vessels — "Flag change: LBR → COK", "Kozmino · 4 calls", "BVI shell · 7 siblings", a `sin()`-based AIS-track sparkline (`ShadowFleetWorkspace.tsx`). I scoped this PR to the **scores**; the dossier needs the same enrichment data to be real, so the honest interim is to replace those blocks with "pending enrichment" placeholders. Want me to do that next?

## Deploy notes
- No migration. Takes effect on the next hourly `compute-shadow-fleet-scores` run, which re-scores the active fleet and prunes the synthetic rows. To apply immediately after merge: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET" https://eykon.ai/api/cron/compute-shadow-fleet-scores`.
- Note: the AIS feed is currently down (AISStream outage), so the active pool reflects pre-outage tracking until the feed restores; the data-clock design keeps scores sensible meanwhile.

author: majorgilles
body:
## Summary

Assistant LaTeX math such as \`$$n = 64 \times 64 \times 3 = 12{,}288 \text{ features}$$\` was printing as raw LaTeX (the terminal markdown renderer can't render it). The extension already had a \`message_end\` hook that sanitizes display/inline math into terminal-readable plain text/Unicode, but it was gated on \`state.active\`, so it only ran while learning mode was on. In normal sessions (the default), math showed up unrendered.

This drops the \`state.active\` gate so the sanitizer runs for **every** assistant message whenever the extension is loaded.

## Root cause (verified)

- \`sanitizeLatexForTerminalMarkdown\` (\`src/latex.ts\`) already converts \`$$…$$\` / \`\[…\]\` display blocks into a \`> **Formula**\` callout and \`\(…\)\` into an inline code span — output is correct (e.g. \`\times\` → \`×\`, \`{,}\` → \`,\`, \`\text{…}\` → \`…\`).
- The \`message_end\` replacement path does re-render: \`AgentSession._handleAgentEvent\` runs extension handlers (in-place mutation of \`event.message\`) **before** the interactive mode renders at \`message_end\`.
- So the only thing preventing rendering was the \`if (!state.active || ...)\` guard.

## Key files changed

- \`index.ts\` — removed \`!state.active\` from the \`message_end\` LaTeX hook condition (one line) + explanatory comment.
- \`README.md\` — document that math sanitization is always-on, move it out of the "while learning mode is active" bullet.
- \`package.json\` — \`0.7.9\` → \`0.7.10\`.

## Example

Before (raw): \`$$n = 64 \times 64 \times 3 = 12{,}288 \text{ features}$$\`

After:
\`\`\`
> **Formula**
> \`n = 64 × 64 × 3 = 12,288 text features\`
\`\`\`

## Checks

- \`npm run typecheck\` (\`tsc --noEmit\`) — passes.

## Limitations / follow-ups

- Single-\`$\` inline math (e.g. \`$x^2$\`) is **not** handled by the current sanitizer (only \`$$…$$\`, \`\[…\]\`, \`\(…\)\`); left untouched to keep this fix minimal. Could be added later with a conservative regex that avoids matching currency.
- Sanitization mutates the stored assistant message (also visible to the LLM in later context), which is the existing behavior — unchanged here.

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure assistant LaTeX math is sanitized for terminal display in all sessions, not just while learning mode is active.

Enhancements:
- Run LaTeX-to-plain-text sanitization on every assistant message at message_end, independent of learning mode state.
- Clarify README behavior to describe always-on LaTeX sanitization outside learning mode as well.
- Bump package version from 0.7.9 to 0.7.10 to release the updated LaTeX handling behavior.

## Summary

A new `apis/shared/feature_flags.py::skills_enabled()` reads the `SKILLS_ENABLED` env var (default **false**), mirroring the existing `FINE_TUNING_ENABLED` precedent. author: jonybur
body:
Two side-panel UI-state bugs from a verified hunt, both about a stale transient control shown after a chat switch or a Stop.

## #4 - Rate-limit banner bled across a chat switch
The reducer's `'state'` snapshot fold rebuilt `pendingConfirm`/`lastError`/`cost` but **omitted `rateLimit`**, and the SW snapshot carries no `rateLimit` field - so the previous chat's "⏳ Rate limited — retrying" banner survived the fold and painted on the switched-to (idle) chat. Reset `rateLimit` in the `'state'` case.
- **Bun test, revert-proven: 10→9/1** without the fix.

## #3 - Aborted-turn tool cards stuck "running…" forever
Card status was derived purely from `tool_result` presence; an aborted turn (Stop / spend-limit / steer) persists its `toolUses` with no result, so the card showed a pulsing "running…" dot **indefinitely, even across a reload**. Threaded the parent message's `stopReason === 'aborted'` into `ToolCall` + the subagent card: a result-less tool on an aborted turn now renders a terminal **`cancelled`** state (static muted dot), and the turn shows a "⏹ stopped" chip.
- New in-browser regression test (cancelled-on-abort + still-pending-when-live). *(This also closes the cosmetic follow-up noted on the abort fix #13.)*

## Tests / gates
- Full bun suite 2077 pass; in-browser 599/0; typecheck + lint clean; tscheck floor bumped 472→473 for the new `// @ts-check` test.

## Filed separately (needs a design decision)
**#5** - the same `'state'` fold *over-clears* the spend-limit halt (`lastError`/`cost.limitReached` forced false on every push), so toggling Plan/Act erases the "raise your limit" banner while still halted. The clean fix surfaces `limitReached` in the SW snapshot (re-derive) rather than blanket-clear - filed as an issue.

Found via a verified side-panel bug-hunt (find → 3 refute-by-default verifiers → fix).

author: slauger
body:
## Summary

#57 item 3. Mirror the `Contents-<arch>` indices (the file→package map used by `apt-file`) when `include_contents` is set.

**Mirror mode only.** An accurate *filtered* Contents would need per-`.deb` file-list extraction chantal does not do, and republishing the upstream one would reference filtered-out packages — so Contents are **dropped in filtered mode** (not downloaded, not published, not in Release).

## Changes

- **Config**: `AptConfig.include_contents` (default false); schema regenerated.
- **Sync**: discover Contents entries (components × architectures+`all` × udeb/normal × `.gz`/`.xz`/none, component-scoped then suite-level), gated on presence in the Release SHA256 map + `include_contents` + mirror mode, deduped. They use the generic metadata download/store path (no per-package handling).
- **Publisher**: carve Contents out of `_publish_metadata_files` (which flattens nested paths) into `_publish_contents_files`, hardlinking each index to its full dists-relative path and feeding its checksums into the regenerated `Release` via a new `extra_files` arg.

## Tests

- Unit: discovery, the `Contents-all`/`udeb`/`.xz` variants, suite-level cross-component dedup, mirror-vs-filtered, default-off.
- E2E: mirror (published at the component path — not flattened — and referenced in `Release` with a matching checksum); filtered (dropped, no `Contents-` in `Release`).

## Review notes

Fresh-context review found no blockers. Its SHOULD-FIX (a `hosted`-mode repo would download Contents but never publish them) is fixed by tightening the sync gate to mirror-only. Pre-existing `_publish_metadata_files` flattening of upstream `Packages.gz`/`Sources.gz` is left as-is (doesn't collide with Contents; tracked separately).

Part of #57

## Why

`dotf upgrade` ran `mise up --dry-run --before 3d` but never showed which tools had updates available, so the "updates available" signal lived only in `CheckMiseUpdatesStep` (a `dotf run` step). The two worlds never met.

## What

- Add `report_mise_updates` to `cmd_upgrade`, run after `mise plugins update`.
- Runs `mise outdated --json` and prints the actionable tools (`current -> latest`), reusing the same semver filter as `CheckMiseUpdatesStep` (excludes tools pinned to non-semver requested/current/latest).
- The `ruby` invocation clears bundler env vars (`BUNDLE_GEMFILE`/`RUBYOPT`/etc.) so it uses stdlib `json` on whichever ruby is on PATH — system Ruby in tests, mise Ruby in production. Without this, the vendored `json` 2.18 gem leaks onto system Ruby 2.6 under `bundle exec` and fails to parse.

## Tests

Updated the two upgrade command-sequence tests to expect `mise outdated --json` after `mise plugins update`. 419 runs, 0 failures; standardrb/secrets/human-only clean.

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR improves the left-navigation experience for the Data Source V2 documentation page in the SQL guide:

- Renames the page `docs/sql-data-sources-v2.md` (`sql-data-sources-v2.html`) to `docs/sql-v2-data-sources.md` (`sql-v2-data-sources.html`). The page content is unchanged (pure rename).
- Adds per-section sub-items for the page to the SQL guide sidebar (`docs/_data/menu-sql.yaml`): Overview, Entry Points, Catalog Interfaces, Table, View, Read Path, Write Path, Row-Level DML, Expressions, Streaming, and Further Reading.
- Updates the internal link in `docs/sql-ref-syntax-dml-merge-into.md` to point at the new URL.

### Why are the changes needed?

In the SQL guide sidebar, selecting **Data Source V2** incorrectly expanded the sibling **Data Sources** group instead of the Data Source V2 entry, and the page exposed no section links in the sidebar.

The sidebar template (`docs/_includes/nav-left.html`) decides which group to expand by checking whether the current page URL contains a group's URL with `.html` stripped (i.e. a substring/prefix match). Because the page URL leaf `sql-data-sources-v2` contains the `sql-data-sources` prefix of the **Data Sources** group, that group was matched and expanded.

Renaming the page to `sql-v2-data-sources` removes the prefix overlap so the correct entry is selected, and the new sub-items make the page's sections navigable from the sidebar (consistent with other entries such as Performance Tuning).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No (documentation-only). Note that the Data Source V2 page URL changes from `sql-data-sources-v2.html` to `sql-v2-data-sources.html`; no redirect is added for the old URL.

The page is not yet released in Spark 4.2

### How was this patch tested?

Built the docs site locally (`SKIP_API=1 bundle exec jekyll build`) and verified in the rendered sidebar that:
- selecting **Data Source V2** expands its own section links,
- the **Data Sources** group is no longer expanded on the Data Source V2 page,

author: franciscomanneh
body:
### 💡 What: The optimization implemented
This PR optimizes the `src/context/AppContext.tsx` file by memoizing the global context provider. 
- All context-provided functions (e.g., `addToCart`, `logout`, `toggleFavorite`) are now wrapped in `useCallback`.
- The `AppContext.Provider`'s `value` is now wrapped in `useMemo`.
- Functional state updates (e.g., `setCart(prev => ...)`) are used within `useCallback` to ensure the dependency arrays remain stable (empty).

### 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
The `AppContext` serves as a "God Context" for the entire application, managing authentication, cart, favorites, products, bundles, and orders. Without memoization, any change to a single piece of state (like adding an item to the cart) would cause the context provider to re-render with a fresh object reference for its `value`, triggering a re-render cascade across every component in the application that consumes the context.

### 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement
- **Eliminates unnecessary re-renders:** Prevents application-wide re-render cascades when unrelated context state changes.
- **Stabilizes dependency arrays:** Consumers using context functions in `useEffect` or `useMemo` will no longer see those hooks re-run on every state change.
- **Enables component-level memoization:** Components wrapped in `React.memo` that consume the context will now correctly skip re-renders if the specific state they depend on hasn't changed.

### 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
- Using React Developer Tools Profiler:
  1. Record a profile while adding an item to the cart.
  2. Observe that components not depending on the `cart` state (e.g., Header, Sidebars, or unrelated page sections) no longer re-render.
- Inspecting hook dependencies: Verify that functions like `addToCart` maintain the same reference across renders.

author: thomasreichmann
body:
Closes #39.

A live preview in the editor that re-renders the current **unsaved** content through `@thomasar-cv/render` - the same `renderResumeToBuffer` the v0.2 preview and the export already go through. No second render path.

## How it fits together

- **Server entry** `POST /api/preview` renders posted (unsaved) content to PDF bytes, reusing `renderResumeToBuffer`. Unlike the public `/preview/pdf` demo (a fixed fixture), it renders caller-supplied content, so it is gated on a session and validates the body with `resumeContent` before it reaches the renderer - the same gate the write path uses. It reads no row, so there is nothing to own beyond being signed in.
- **`useResumePdf`** serializes the in-memory document, debounces the *string* (450ms), and POSTs it. Each render aborts the one in flight, so out-of-order responses can't paint a stale frame, and the shown bytes only move forward on success - an invalid intermediate edit or a failed render keeps the last good frame up.
- **`PdfCanvas`** is the v0.2 pdf.js painter, extracted to a shared component and made responsive (fills the caller's A4 box, re-rasterizes on resize). The static preview now uses it too, so there is one painter. It keeps the previous frame on screen while a same-size re-render computes, so typing doesn't flash the page.

Order + `hidden` come from `flattenResume`, so #38's structural edits will show up here with no extra wiring. Paper stays light (ADR 0002/0003) - the résumé is never themed from the dark chrome tokens.

## Notes for review

- The preview fetch is **not** logged to the console on failure (only surfaced via the "Preview failed" indicator). A fetch cut off by navigating away rejects exactly like a real failure and would otherwise be navigation noise that also trips the strict e2e console guard.
- Status is *derived* from "is the debounced body ahead of the last settled render", not set synchronously inside the effect (which the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint forbids).

## Testing

- `pnpm check` green (typecheck + lint + unit).
- New unit test for `POST /api/preview` (signed-in renders a real PDF, 401 unauthenticated, 400 on malformed content).
- New e2e `editor-preview.spec.ts`: a frame paints for the loaded résumé, and an edit drives a fresh `/api/preview` render. Full `flows` + `smoke` e2e suites pass locally.

## Out of scope

A client-side HTML render path (would be a second definition), multi-page preview, and changes to the download export (already ships from this engine, #19).

author: deanmarano
body:
Un-skips four `eager_test.rb` cases over canonical STI models/fixtures (Rails-faithful):

- `preloading with has one through an sti with after initialize`
- `eager with has many through an sti join model with conditions on both`
- `eager with has one through join model with conditions on the through`
- `eager with has one dependent does not destroy dependent`

## Preloader fix

The `has_one :through` with conditions on the through table (`Member#favorite_club`) exposed a preloader gap. The through-preloader relocates WHERE predicates that reference the through table onto the through query, but only recognized Arel `Attribute` nodes (hash/Arel conditions). A raw-SQL condition like `where("memberships.favorite = ?", true)` carries no `Attribute` node, so `fetchAttribute` never visited it and it landed on the source query as `no such column: memberships.favorite`.

`predicateReferencesTable` now also inspects `SqlLiteral`/`BoundSqlLiteral` text (through one `Grouping` wrapper) for a `<table>.` qualifier, so raw-SQL through-table conditions are relocated like hash/Arel ones. The relocated node carries its own binds, so no extra threading is needed.

Covered by the un-skipped `favoriteClub` test. Full `eager.test.ts` plus the through-association / cascaded-eager / polymorphic-sti suites pass locally.

Closes-story: a1-eager-sti-through

author: jotaele44
body:
## Summary

- Derives `blocking_gaps` from non-ready required SATIM base layers L1-L3.
- Derives `recommended_next_actions` from non-ready L4/L5 advisory layers.
- Adds regression coverage proving a missing L3 layer creates a blocking gap during report merge.

## Context

The first real local SATIM report correctly produced `overall_status: DEGRADED`, but `blocking_gaps` remained empty while L3 was `MISSING`. This patch keeps the existing readiness status behavior and adds operator-facing gap accounting so degraded reports identify why they are degraded.

## Validation

Run locally:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_satim_calibration_models.py tests/test_prii_readiness_engine_satim.py -q
```

Expected report behavior after this patch:

```text
L3_vision_ocr: MISSING -> blocking_gaps[0]
L4_aircraft_intelligence: PARTIAL -> recommended_next_actions
L5_tile_seam_shadow: MISSING -> recommended_next_actions
overall_status: DEGRADED
```

author: tharciosantos
body:
## Contexto

O README já representava bem o estado geral do HelpFlow, mas alguns pontos ficaram desatualizados após as últimas melhorias aplicadas no projeto.

A atualização foi feita para manter a documentação coerente com o comportamento atual da aplicação, sem adicionar funcionalidades que ainda não foram implementadas.

## O que foi feito

* Atualizada a descrição do rate limiter para incluir criação, atualização e exclusão de tickets.
* Adicionado `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` à lista de headers de segurança.
* Documentado que a rota de registro retorna apenas `id`, `name` e `email`, sem expor campos internos.
* Ajustada a descrição de atualização de status para incluir a página de detalhes do ticket.
* Atualizada a seção de próximos passos para indicar que a CSP já está em Report-Only e que o enforcement é uma evolução futura.

## Arquivos alterados

* `README.md`

## Validação

* Revisão manual do README.
* Conferido que a documentação não afirma que Upstash/Redis já está implementado.
* Conferido que nenhuma alteração de código foi feita.

## Risco

Baixo. A alteração é exclusivamente documental e não altera comportamento da aplicação.

author: lyndencooke
body:
Makes Sound Books playable **on screen, no printing**, at the same quality as the storybook interactive reader — by reusing `InteractiveBookReader` itself rather than building a parallel viewer.

## How
- Each L1 grapheme (s a t p i n m d g o) gets a **varied activity deck** authored as `InteractivePage[]` (`src/lib/soundBookInteractiveData.ts`) and registered into `INTERACTIVE_BOOKS`. Activity types per book: hero cover → **sound grid** (tap the phoneme) → **sound spotlight** (picture words) → **vocab** (tap to sound-out + blend) → **word reading** (blend it) → **spelling** (letter tiles) → **listen-and-choose quiz** (picture options) → **trace the sound** → **reward certificate** (stamps).
- Launched from the Sound Book card's **"Play slides"** button via `SoundBookSlides.tsx`, which builds a synthetic `local-` Book so reading-progress writes no-op and there are **no server/DB/unlock side-effects** (stamps are localStorage-only).
- Filled the L1 word-image gap by converting on-brand Sound Spotlight clipart into `/images/words/` (cot, dam, den, gig, mug). All 40 featured words now have a web image; grapheme + word audio already existed.
- Also includes the earlier **PDF presenter** (supersedes #63): used as the on-screen fallback for sound books that don't yet have an interactive deck (L2–L8).

## Verified
`tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` passes. **Not browser-tested** (no runtime here) — please open a Sound Book → "Play slides" on the preview/live and sanity-check rendering + tap audio.

## Follow-ups
- Author L2–L8 sound-book decks (same builder; just needs word images per grapheme).
- Workbooks + blend books on the school page still need their PDFs published to storage buckets + edge-function support.
